\|\,\Gamma_{j}\,\|\lesssim\ell_{j}^{-2}\simeq b^{-2j}
up to an arbitrarily small

\varepsilon>0
loss due to lattice anisotropies.

Proof.

Inside a block the range of
\Pi_{j}
consists of covariantly constant fields with respect to
parallel transport Eq.(
4.20
). Inside a block, parallel transport to
c_{B}
identifies the subspace of
covariantly constant fields with the constant fields for the ordinary graph
differences. On this subspace the quadratic form of
A=\Delta_{A^{h}}+\mu^{2}

coincides with that of
\Delta+\mu^{2}
up to unitary conjugation, so the standard
discrete Poincaré inequality on a cube of side
\ell_{j}
applies.
∎

The operators relevant for the horizon-projected measure are spectral multipliers of
\Delta_{A^{h}}
of the form

C_{\sigma}\;=\;\int_{0}^{\infty}e^{-t\Delta_{A^{h}}}\,d\mu_{\sigma}(t),

(4.36)

with
d\mu_{\sigma}
a finite positive measure supported in
[c_{1}\sigma^{-2},\infty)
. It is convenient to represent
C_{\sigma}
as a continuous superposition of massive resolvents via the Laplace transform
[
13
]
:

C_{\sigma}\;=\;\int_{0}^{\infty}\bigl(\Delta_{A^{h}}+m^{2}\bigr)^{-1}\,d\nu_{\sigma}(m^{2}),

(4.37)

where
d\nu_{\sigma}
is a finite positive measure determined by
d\mu_{\sigma}
. Applying Theorem
4.1
at each mass
m\geq m_{0}\sim\sigma
yields a family
\{\Gamma_{j}(m)\}_{j\geq 0}
with the same finite-range constant
C\,b^{j}a
and uniform positivity and covariance. Fubini’s theorem then gives the finite-range decomposition

C_{\sigma}\;=\;\sum_{j=0}^{\infty}C_{\sigma}^{(j)},\qquad C_{\sigma}^{(j)}\;=\;\int_{0}^{\infty}\Gamma_{j}(m)\,d\nu_{\sigma}(m^{2}),

(4.38)

with each
C_{\sigma}^{(j)}
positive, gauge covariant, reflection covariant, and of finite range
C\,b^{j}a
. The operator-norm and
\ell^{1}
bounds of Theorem
4.1
propagate to
C_{\sigma}^{(j)}
uniformly in
\sigma
once
m_{0}\sim\sigma
is fixed, since
\nu_{\sigma}
is supported on
[m_{0}^{2},\infty)
.

Let
F
be a bounded functional supported in
\Lambda_{+}
. Consider the Gaussian functional integral on the slice with covariance
C_{\sigma}
,

\mathcal{G}(F)\;=\;\int e^{-\frac{1}{2}\langle\phi,C_{\sigma}^{-1}\phi\rangle}\,F(\phi)\,\mathcal{D}\phi,

(4.39)

where
\phi
ranges over site-adjoint fields on the slice and
\mathcal{D}\phi
is the normalized Lebesgue measure. Since each
C_{\sigma}^{(j)}
is positive, reflection covariant, and of finite range, the quadratic form
\langle\phi,C_{\sigma}\phi\rangle
splits into a sum of East-West contributions plus a boundary term supported in a fixed-width slab around
\Pi
. Consequently, the OS form

\langle F,F\rangle_{\mathrm{OS}}\;=\;\int\overline{F(\phi^{\theta})}\,F(\phi)\,e^{-\frac{1}{2}\langle\phi,C_{\sigma}^{-1}\phi\rangle}\,\mathcal{D}\phi

(4.40)

is nonnegative by the same block-positivity argument as for the Wilson action
[
1
,
23
]
. Furthermore, since
C_{\sigma}^{(j)}
is of finite range and reflection covariant, the associated Gaussian measure induces a transfer operator
T^{(j)}
on
\mathcal{H}_{a}
with positive kernel supported on pairs of configurations
(U_{0},U_{a})
that differ only within a fixed-width collar, and the full transfer operator is the strong product of the
T^{(j)}
:

T_{\sigma}\;=\;\prod_{j=0}^{\infty}T^{(j)}\qquad\text{(strong product on }\mathcal{H}_{a}\text{)}.

(4.41)

Each
T^{(j)}
is a positive, self-adjoint contraction, hence so is
T_{\sigma}
. The spectral bound for
T_{\sigma}
is thus controlled scale by scale.

The dependence of
C_{\sigma}^{(j)}
on the background and on the parameters
\sigma
and
b
is smooth in the strong operator topology. Differentiating under the Laplace integral (
4.37
) reduces to differentiating
\Gamma_{j}(m)
with respect to
m^{2}
, which is bounded uniformly thanks to the resolvent identity

\frac{\partial}{\partial m^{2}}\bigl(\Delta_{A^{h}}+m^{2}\bigr)^{-1}\;=\;-\bigl(\Delta_{A^{h}}+m^{2}\bigr)^{-2}.

(4.42)

The finite-range structure is unaffected by differentiation. Differentiability with respect to
b
and to the block geometry is verified by a finite-difference argument using stability of
\Pi_{j}
under small deformations of block boundaries; since the projections are defined by local parallel transports, small changes at the boundary affect only finitely many matrix elements of
\Pi_{j}
and preserve gauge and reflection covariance. These properties ensure robustness of the decomposition under small parameter variations, which will be used implicitly in the multiscale analysis.

Appendix 5
Polymer representation at each scale

This section develops a mathematically rigorous polymer expansion for the scale-
k
effective action and establishes a uniform control of large-field events by an Osterwalder-Schrader (OS) compatible regulator. For completeness, the lattice set-up, reflection map, the OS-positivity argument, and the transfer time-slicing formalism are derived in full detail before constructing the polymer representation and verifying the Kotecký-Preiss criterion
[
19
,
25
,
26
]
. Throughout, the gauge group is
G=\mathrm{SU}(N)
with
N\geq 2
, and all bounds are uniform in the spatial volume.

Fix a lattice spacing
a>0
and positive integers
L,T\in\mathbb{N}
. The periodic hypercubic lattice is

\Lambda\,=\,\big\{(x_{0},\mathbf{x})\in a\,\mathbb{Z}^{4}:\ x_{0}\in a\{0,1,\dots,T-1\},\ \mathbf{x}\in a(\mathbb{Z}/L\mathbb{Z})^{3}\big\}.

(5.1)

Directed bonds are
b=(x,\mu)
with
\mu\in\{0,1,2,3\}
and unit vectors
\hat{\mu}
. To each bond is attached a group element
U_{b}\in G
, with orientation convention

U_{(x,-\mu)}\,=\,U_{(x-\hat{\mu},\mu)}^{-1}.

(5.2)

Plaquettes are oriented unit squares
p=(x;\mu,\nu)
,
\mu<\nu
, with plaquette variable

U_{p}\,=\,U_{(x,\mu)}\,U_{(x+\hat{\mu},\nu)}\,U_{(x+\hat{\nu},\mu)}^{-1}\,U_{(x,\nu)}^{-1}.

(5.3)

The Wilson action at inverse bare coupling
\beta>0
is

S_{W}[U;\beta]\,=\,\beta\sum_{p\subset\Lambda}\Big(1-\tfrac{1}{N}\Re\mathrm{Tr}\,U_{p}\Big).

(5.4)

The product Haar probability measure on bonds is

d\mu_{\mathrm{H}}(U)\,=\,\prod_{b\subset\Lambda}dU_{b},

(5.5)

where each
dU_{b}
is the normalized Haar measure on
G
.

Time reflection
\theta:\Lambda\to\Lambda
is defined by

\theta(x_{0},\mathbf{x})\,=\,\big((-x_{0})\!\!\!\!\!\pmod{aT},\,\mathbf{x}\big).

(5.6)

The reflection plane is
\Pi=\{(0,\mathbf{x})\}
; the half-lattices are
\Lambda_{+}=\{x\in\Lambda:\ 0<x_{0}<aT/2\}
and
\Lambda_{-}=\theta(\Lambda_{+})
. The induced involution on bonds is chosen as in
[
1
,
2
,
4
,
10
]
:

\theta(x_{0},\mathbf{x})=(-x_{0},\mathbf{x}),\qquad(\Theta U)(x,0)=U(\theta x-a\hat{0},0)^{-1},\qquad(\Theta U)(x,i)=U(\theta x,i)\quad(i=1,2,3)

(5.7)

for spatial
i\in\{1,2,3\}
and temporal direction
\mu=0
. This choice makes the plaquette map
U\mapsto U_{p}

\theta
-covariant. Site and link reflections are unitarily equivalent via a half-time translation;
we work with the site reflection
\Theta
as above and use unitary conjugacy to relate to link
reflection when convenient (Corollary 3.7).

We work in temporal-axial gauge away from
\Pi
, namely

U_{(x,0)}\,=\,\mathbf{1}\quad\text{whenever}\quad x_{0}\notin\{0,aT/2\}.

(5.8)

In this gauge, time-like plaquettes reduce to products of spatial links at adjacent times, and the reflection
\,\theta(x_{0},x)=(a-x_{0},x)\,
maps the constrained set
\{U(x,0)=1\}
to itself; hence temporal-axial gauge is compatible with link reflection about
\Pi_{1/2}
.
Also in this gauge all time-like links vanish in the bulk, while dynamical degrees of freedom remain in a boundary slab
S
around
\Pi
; this is the standard set-up for OS factorization
[
2
,
4
,
10
]
.

On each time slice
t\in a\{0,1,\dots,T-1\}
, consider the spatial gauge group
\mathcal{G}_{t}=\{g:\{x_{0}=t\}\to G\}
acting by

(g\cdot U)_{(x,i)}\,=\,g(x)\,U_{(x,i)}\,g(x+\hat{i})^{-1},\qquad i=1,2,3.

(5.9)

Define the lattice Landau functional

\mathcal{L}_{t}(g;U)\,=\,\sum_{\mathbf{x},\,i=1}^{3}\big\|\,\mathbf{1}-g(x_{0}\!=\!t,\mathbf{x})\,U_{(x,i)}\,g(x_{0}\!=\!t,\mathbf{x}+\hat{i})^{-1}\,\big\|_{F}^{2}.

(5.10)

On the finite slice,
\mathcal{L}_{t}(\cdot;U)
attains a global minimum. A measurable, reflection-covariant tie-breaking rule selects a minimizer
h_{t}[U]
and defines the slice representative
U^{\,h}
. Let
\Delta_{A^{h}(t)}
be the spatial covariant Laplacian acting on adjoint-valued site fields on slice
t
.
Fix
\sigma>0
and choose a completely monotone (CM) near-plateau profile

\chi_{\sigma}:[0,\infty)\to(0,1]
with
\chi_{\sigma}(0)=1
and rapid decay

\chi_{\sigma}(\lambda)\leq Ce^{-c\,\lambda/\sigma^{2}}
for
\lambda\geq 0
; see (4.12).
Define the horizon operator on slice
t
by

P_{\sigma}(t):=\chi_{\sigma}\!\big(\Delta_{A^{h}}(t)\big)=\int_{0}^{\infty}e^{-s\,\Delta_{A^{h}}(t)}\,d\nu_{\sigma}(s),

(5.11)

where
d\nu_{\sigma}
is the finite positive measure furnished by Bernstein’s theorem.
With this choice
P_{\sigma}(t)
is a positive contraction, exponentially local, and
reflection-covariant.
Hence
P_{\sigma}(t)
is a positive contraction, reflection-covariant on the slice, and its kernel is
exponentially localized by the Davies-Gaffney bounds as in (
4.15
).
By the heat-kernel representation and Davies-Gaffney bounds,
P_{\sigma}(t)
is a positive contraction with exponentially decaying kernel and is reflection-covariant
[
13
,
10
]
.
The gauge-fixed, projected Euclidean measure is

d\mu_{\sigma}(U)\,=\,Z_{\sigma}^{-1}\,\exp\!\big(-S_{W}[U;\beta]\big)\,\Big(\prod_{t}\mathcal{W}_{\sigma}(t;U)\Big)\,J[U]\,d\mu_{\mathrm{H}}(U),

(5.12)

where
J[U]
is the Faddeev-Popov determinant associated with the slice-wise Landau gauge (represented as a Grassmann Gaussian with kernel
M[U^{\,h}(t)]

[
4
,
10
]
), and
\mathcal{W}_{\sigma}(t;U)
is the positive scalar weight obtained from
P_{\sigma}(t)
on the adjoint sector perpendicular to constants. We emphasize that
P_{\sigma}
is a positive contraction (not idempotent); all OS
and locality arguments use positivity and exponential locality only; section.4.

Lemma 5.1

(Reflection positivity of the projected bosonic measure)
.

Let
F
be a bounded, gauge-invariant functional depending only on bonds in
\Lambda^{+}
and on no Grassmann variables. Then

\int(F\circ\Theta)(U)\,F(U)\,d\mu_{\sigma}(U)\;\geq\;0.

(5.13)

Equivalently, after integrating out the Grassmann fields so that the ghost sector contributes the positive factor
\det{}^{\prime}M[A_{h}]
(the determinant on the orthogonal complement of constant adjoint modes), the resulting purely bosonic measure is reflection positive.

Proof.

We first integrate the Grassmann fields, which yields the multiplicative factor
\det{}^{\prime}M[A_{h}]
with
M[A_{h}]
real symmetric and strictly positive on the orthogonal complement of constants; see Lemma 2.3 and the Schur complement analysis across
\Pi
in Lemma
9.2
. The resulting weight is a product of nonnegative slice factors and a nonnegative boundary kernel. The remainder of the proof is the standard OS factorization argument for the bosonic sector (temporal-axial gauge away from
\Pi
so that mixed plaquettes lie in a fixed slab), identical to Theorem 2.1 and Theorem 6.1. ∎

OS positivity is asserted only for bosonic, gauge-invariant observables. Correlators with explicit ghost insertions are not OS-positive in general and are not used in any step of the transfer-matrix or spectral-gap analysis. Therefore, in constructing the transfer matrix and Hilbert space, we restrict to the
physical (gauge-invariant) subspace
of states. The Faddeev-Popov ghost fields, introduced as a gauge-fixing device, do not appear in any physical correlation functions and their degrees of freedom are absent in the physical Hilbert space. More precisely, the BRST symmetry ensures that all ghost contributions cancel out for gauge-invariant observables, and physical state vectors are taken from the cohomology of the BRST charge (or equivalently, the kernel of the Faddeev-Popov operator) with no ghost excitations. As a result, the transfer Hamiltonian
H
can be defined to act on the gauge-invariant subspace, on which the inner product induced by the OS measure is positive-definite. In this way, Osterwalder-Schrader reflection positivity is maintained for all physical states, and the presence of ghost fields does not spoil the positivity or unitarity of the theory’s physical Hilbert space. Ghosts appear solely through the positive determinant
\det{}^{\prime}M[A_{h}]
after Berezin integration.
Fix a time
t
, and let
\mathcal{C}_{t}
denote the configuration space of spatial bonds at time
t
, with product Haar measure
d\mu_{\mathrm{H},\mathrm{sp}}
. Denote
U_{t}\in\mathcal{C}_{t}
. The slab contribution between slices
t
and
t+a
induces a positive kernel

\mathcal{K}_{\sigma}(U_{t+a},U_{t})\,=\,\int\exp\!\Big(-S_{W}^{\mathrm{slab}}[U_{t},\tilde{U},U_{t+a}]\Big)\,\mathcal{W}_{\sigma}(t;U)\,\mathcal{W}_{\sigma}(t+a;U)\,J^{\mathrm{slab}}[U]\,d\mu_{\mathrm{H}}^{\mathrm{slab}}(U),

(5.14)

where the integration is over bonds strictly inside the slab,
d\mu_{\mathrm{H}}^{\mathrm{slab}}
is the corresponding Haar product, and
J^{\mathrm{slab}}
is the ghost Berezin integral with Dirichlet boundary on the slab faces. The kernel
\mathcal{K}_{\sigma}
is symmetric and nonnegative:

\mathcal{K}_{\sigma}(U^{\prime},U)\,=\,\mathcal{K}_{\sigma}(U,U^{\prime})\ \geq\ 0,\qquad\mathcal{K}_{\sigma}\in L^{2}\!\left(\mathcal{C}_{t}\times\mathcal{C}_{t+a},\,d\mu_{\mathrm{H},\mathrm{sp}}\otimes d\mu_{\mathrm{H},\mathrm{sp}}\right).

(5.15)

Define
T_{\sigma}:L^{2}(\mathcal{C}_{t},d\mu_{\mathrm{H},\mathrm{sp}})\to L^{2}(\mathcal{C}_{t},d\mu_{\mathrm{H},\mathrm{sp}})
by

(T_{\sigma}\psi)(U_{t})\,=\,\int_{\mathcal{C}_{t+a}}\mathcal{K}_{\sigma}(U_{t+a},U_{t})\,\psi(U_{t+a})\,d\mu_{\mathrm{H},\mathrm{sp}}(U_{t+a}).

(5.16)

By (
5.15
),
T_{\sigma}
is a positive self-adjoint contraction. The OS reconstruction identifies the physical Hilbert space
\mathcal{H}
with the completion of
L^{2}(\mathcal{C}_{0},d\mu_{\mathrm{H},\mathrm{sp}})
under the inner product

\langle\phi,\psi\rangle_{\mathcal{H}}\,=\,\int\overline{\phi(U_{0})}\,\psi(U_{0})\,d\nu_{0}(U_{0}),\qquad d\nu_{0}(U_{0})\,=\,Z_{0}^{-1}\,W^{+}(U_{0})\,d\mu_{\mathrm{H},\mathrm{sp}}(U_{0}),

(5.17)

and the unit time translation is implemented by
T_{\sigma}
; the Hamiltonian is

H_{\sigma}\,=\,-\,a^{-1}\log T_{\sigma},

(5.18)

a positive self-adjoint operator
[
2
,
7
]
.

Fix an integer block factor
b\geq 2
and define the scale-
k
lattice spacing
a_{k}=b^{k}a
. Partition the spatial torus into disjoint cubes (blocks)
B
of side
b^{k}a
. The finite-range decomposition from Section 4 yields a decomposition of the scale-
k
covariance
C_{k}
into positive operators
C_{k}^{(j)}
with range bounded by

\mathrm{range}(C_{k}^{(j)})\,\leq\,R_{j}\,=\,c_{0}\,b^{j}\,\sigma,

(5.19)

and exponential off-range decay, with constants independent of
k
. The fluctuations inside a block are modeled, after linearization around
U^{\,h}
, by a centered Gaussian field with covariance

C_{k}^{\mathrm{int}}\,=\,\sum_{j\leq j_{*}}C_{k}^{(j)},

(5.20)

where
j_{*}
is the largest index with
R_{j_{*}}\leq\mathrm{diam}(B)
.

For block-supported functionals
F_{1},\dots,F_{n}
, define the truncated (cumulant) expectation with respect to the normalized Gaussian measure with covariance
C_{k}^{\mathrm{int}}
by

\big\langle F_{1};\dots;F_{n}\big\rangle^{\mathrm{T}}\,=\,\left.\frac{\partial^{n}}{\partial t_{1}\cdots\partial t_{n}}\log\Big\langle\exp\big(\sum_{i=1}^{n}t_{i}F_{i}\big)\Big\rangle\right|_{t_{1}=\cdots=t_{n}=0}.

(5.21)

Because
C_{k}^{\mathrm{int}}
has finite range, the cumulant vanishes unless the supports form a connected union of blocks, and it decays exponentially when the union has large diameter.

For a plaquette
p
define the deviation

\delta_{p}(U)\,=\,\tfrac{1}{2}\big\|\,\mathbf{1}-U_{p}\,\big\|_{F}^{2}\,\in[0,2N].

(5.22)

Fix a smooth convex function
\varphi:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)
with
\varphi(s)=s
for
0\leq s\leq 1
,
\varphi(s)=s^{2}
for
s\geq 2
, and
\varphi^{\prime\prime}\geq 0
. For
\lambda>0
, define the large-field regulator

\mathcal{R}_{k}(U)\,=\,\exp\!\Big(-\lambda\sum_{p\subset\Lambda_{k}}\varphi\big(\delta_{p}(U)\big)\Big),

(5.23)

where
\Lambda_{k}
is the coarse lattice obtained by grouping
b^{k}\times b^{k}\times b^{k}
spatial plaquettes. The factor
\mathcal{R}_{k}
is a product of reflection-invariant local positives, hence multiplying
d\mu_{\sigma}
by
\mathcal{R}_{k}
preserves reflection positivity: for
F
supported in
\Lambda_{+}
,

\int\overline{F\circ\Theta}\,F\,\mathcal{R}_{k}\,d\mu_{\sigma}\,=\,\int\overline{F\circ\Theta}\,\big(\mathcal{R}_{k}^{1/2}\big)\,\big(\mathcal{R}_{k}^{1/2}\big)\,F\,d\mu_{\sigma}\,\geq\,0,

(5.24)

by the argument of Lemma
5.1
with
W^{\pm}
replaced by
W^{\pm}\mathcal{R}_{k}^{1/2}
.

Let
\Omega_{\delta}
be the small-field set in a given block
B
,

\Omega_{\delta}\,=\,\big\{U:\ \delta_{p}(U)\leq\delta\ \text{for all plaquettes }p\subset B\big\}.

(5.25)

Its complement
\Omega_{\delta}^{\complement}
is suppressed uniformly:

Lemma 5.2

(Uniform large-field suppression)
.

There exist
c_{1},c_{2}>0
depending only on
\varphi
and
G
such that, for any block
B
and
\lambda>0
,

\int_{\Omega_{\delta}^{\complement}\cap B}\mathcal{R}_{k}(U)\,d\mu_{\mathrm{H}}(U)\,\leq\,\exp\big(-c_{1}\,\lambda\,|\mathcal{P}(B)|+c_{2}\,|\mathcal{P}(B)|\big),

(5.26)

where
|\mathcal{P}(B)|
is the number of plaquettes in
B
.

Proof.

On
\Omega_{\delta}^{\complement}
there is at least one plaquette
p\subset B
with
\varphi(\delta_{p}(U))\geq\varphi(\delta)
. By Fubini and the product structure of
\mathcal{R}_{k}
and
d\mu_{\mathrm{H}}
,

\int_{\Omega_{\delta}^{\complement}\cap B}\mathcal{R}_{k}\,d\mu_{\mathrm{H}}\,\leq\,\sum_{p\subset B}\int\exp\!\big(-\lambda\varphi(\delta_{p}(U))\big)\,d\mu_{\mathrm{H}}(U_{p}).

(5.27)

The one-plaquette integral satisfies

\int\exp\!\big(-\lambda\varphi(\delta_{p}(U))\big)\,d\mu_{\mathrm{H}}(U_{p})\,\leq\,\exp(-c_{1}\lambda+c_{2}),

(5.28)

for
\lambda
large enough, by Laplace’s method and the nondegeneracy of the Haar density near
\mathbf{1}
. Combining (
5.27
)-(
5.28
) yields (
5.26
).
∎

A
polymer

X
is a finite connected union of blocks in a fixed time layer. The effective interaction on that layer admits the unique expansion

S_{k}(U)\,=\,\sum_{X}\Phi_{k}(X;U|_{X}),

(5.29)

where
\Phi_{k}(X;\cdot)
depends only on bonds in
X
, is gauge-invariant and reflection-covariant, and vanishes on disconnected
X
. Introduce the diameter norm

\|\Phi_{k}\|_{a}\,=\,\sup_{x}\ \sum_{X\ni x}\ \|\Phi_{k}(X)\|\,e^{a\,\mathrm{diam}(X)},

(5.30)

with operator norm
\|\cdot\|
induced by the Gaussian reference with covariance
C_{k}^{\mathrm{int}}
and the regulator, and graph diameter
\mathrm{diam}(X)
(see Appendix (
13
).

Let
\{V(B;\cdot)\}_{B}
be block-local base functionals obtained by integrating slab fluctuations at fixed boundary fields. Define
V(X;U|_{X})=\sum_{B\subset X}V(B;U|_{B})
and set

\Phi_{k}(X;U|_{X})\,=\,\sum_{n\geq 1}\,\frac{1}{n!}\!\!\!\!\!\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}B_{1},\dots,B_{n}\subset X\\
\text{connected}\end{subarray}}\!\!\!\!\big\langle V(B_{1};\cdot);\dots;V(B_{n};\cdot)\big\rangle^{\mathrm{T}}(U|_{B_{1}\cup\cdots\cup B_{n}}),

(5.31)

with truncated expectation (
5.21
) taken w.r.t. the normalized Gaussian measure restricted to
\Omega_{\delta}
with regulator
\mathcal{R}_{k}
inserted. By finite range of
C_{k}^{\mathrm{int}}
and Lemma
5.2
, (
5.31
) is well defined and yields connected activities.

Theorem 5.3

(Scale-
k
polymer bound)
.

There exist
a>0
,
\epsilon>0
, and
C<\infty
, independent of
k
, such that if
\sup_{B}\|V(B)\|\leq\epsilon
, then

\|\Phi_{k}\|_{a}\,\leq\,C\,\epsilon^{2}.

(5.32)

Proof.

Consider the generating functional

\mathcal{Z}(\{t_{B}\})\,=\,\Big\langle\exp\Big(\sum_{B}t_{B}V(B;\cdot)\Big)\Big\rangle,

(5.33)

with
\langle\cdot\rangle
the normalized Gaussian expectation with covariance
C_{k}^{\mathrm{int}}
on
\Omega_{\delta}
and regulator
\mathcal{R}_{k}
. By dominated convergence (Lemma
5.2
)
\log\mathcal{Z}
is analytic for small
|t_{B}|
, and its Taylor coefficients at the origin are the cumulants (
5.21
). For blocks
B_{1},\dots,B_{n}\subset X
, the BKAR/tree-graph inequality for Gaussian cumulants
[
25
,
26
]
yields

\big|\langle V(B_{1});\dots;V(B_{n})\rangle^{\mathrm{T}}\big|\,\leq\,\|V(B_{1})\|\cdots\|V(B_{n})\|\sum_{\mathcal{T}}\prod_{(i,j)\in\mathcal{T}}\alpha(B_{i},B_{j}),

(5.34)

where the sum runs over trees
\mathcal{T}
on
\{1,\dots,n\}
, and

\alpha(B_{i},B_{j})\,=\,\sup_{y\in B_{i},\,z\in B_{j}}\big\|C_{k}^{\mathrm{int}}(y,z)\big\|\,\leq\,\exp\!\big(-c\,\mathrm{dist}(B_{i},B_{j})/R_{j_{*}}\big),

(5.35)

for some
c>0
, by finite range and exponential off-range decay. For a connected family covering
X
, any tree has at least
\mathrm{diam}(X)/R_{j_{*}}
edges and
\sum_{(i,j)\in\mathcal{T}}\mathrm{dist}(B_{i},B_{j})\gtrsim\mathrm{diam}(X)
; hence

\sum_{\mathcal{T}}\prod_{(i,j)\in\mathcal{T}}\alpha(B_{i},B_{j})\,\leq\,C_{1}^{|X|}\,\exp\!\big(-c^{\prime}\,\mathrm{diam}(X)\big),

(5.36)

with constants
C_{1},c^{\prime}>0
independent of
k
. Inserting (
5.36
) into (
5.34
), summing over
n\geq 2
and connected block families with
\|V\|\leq\epsilon
, and choosing
\epsilon
sufficiently small gives

\|\Phi_{k}(X)\|\,\leq\,C_{2}\,\epsilon^{2}\,\exp\!\big(-c^{\prime}\,\mathrm{diam}(X)\big).

(5.37)

Multiplying by
e^{a\,\mathrm{diam}(X)}
with
a<c^{\prime}
and summing over
X\ni x
yields (
5.32
).
∎

Let
\Gamma
be a finite family of mutually compatible polymers (disjoint unions). The polymer partition function is

\mathcal{Z}_{\mathrm{poly}}\,=\,\sum_{\Gamma}\ \prod_{X\in\Gamma}\zeta_{k}(X),\qquad\zeta_{k}(X)\,=\,\int\exp\!\big(-\Phi_{k}(X;U|_{X})\big)\,d\nu_{X}(U|_{X})-1,

(5.38)

where
d\nu_{X}
is the normalized product measure induced by slab integration and the regulator on
X
. For
\|\Phi_{k}\|_{a}
small,
|\zeta_{k}(X)|\leq C\,\|\Phi_{k}(X)\|
. The Kotecký-Preiss criterion
[
19
]
holds under the following bound.

Proposition 5.4

(Kotecký-Preiss verification)
.

There exist
a>0
and
\epsilon_{1}>0
, independent of
k
, such that if
\|\Phi_{k}\|_{a}\leq\epsilon_{1}
, then

\sup_{X}\ \sum_{Y\not\sim X}|\zeta_{k}(Y)|\,e^{a\,\mathrm{dist}(X,Y)}\,\leq\,\tfrac{1}{2}\,a\,|X|.

(5.39)

Proof.

By Theorem
5.3
and analyticity, there is
C_{0}
with
|\zeta_{k}(Y)|\leq C_{0}\,\epsilon^{2}\exp(-c^{\prime}\,\mathrm{diam}(Y))
. The number
N(m;r)
of polymers
Y
with
\mathrm{diam}(Y)=m
at graph distance
r
from
X
satisfies
N(m;r)\leq C_{4}\,\exp(C_{5}(m+r))
. Therefore

\sum_{Y\not\sim X}|\zeta_{k}(Y)|\,e^{a\,\mathrm{dist}(X,Y)}\,\leq\,\sum_{m\geq 1}\sum_{r\geq 0}C_{4}\,e^{C_{5}(m+r)}\,C_{0}\,\epsilon^{2}\,e^{-c^{\prime}m}\,e^{ar}.

(5.40)

Choosing
a\in(0,C_{5})
and
\epsilon_{1}>0
so that
C_{0}C_{4}\,\epsilon_{1}^{2}\sum_{m\geq 1}e^{(C_{5}-c^{\prime})m}\sum_{r\geq 0}e^{(a-C_{5})r}\leq\tfrac{1}{2}a
yields (
5.39
).
∎

Under (
5.39
), the logarithm of
\mathcal{Z}_{\mathrm{poly}}
and all connected truncated correlations of local gauge-invariant observables admit absolutely convergent cluster expansions with exponential spatial decay
[
19
,
26
]
(see Appenfix (
13
). Combined with Lemma
5.1
and the transfer representation (
5.16
)-(
5.18
), time-sliced truncated correlations possess a positive spectral representation in the Hilbert space
\mathcal{H}

[
2
,
7
]
.

Appendix 6
Uniform ultraviolet stability (Theorem A)

In this section a complete and self-contained proof is given of the uniform control of a single renormalization step. The argument proceeds in three stages. First, the transfer time-slicing formalism and Osterwalder-Schrader (OS) reflection positivity for the horizon-projected, gauge-fixed lattice measure are derived in detail, which produces a positive, self-adjoint transfer operator at each scale. Second, a covariant decomposition of the fluctuation covariance into scale-localized, positive pieces with uniform exponential off-range bounds is constructed. Third, a gauge-invariant polymer/cluster expansion is set up with a reflection-compatible large-field regulator. The integration of a single RG step is then controlled by a Battle-Brydges-Federbush tree inequality together with the Kotecký-Preiss criterion, leading to the uniform contraction estimate in Theorem
6.7
.

Throughout this section, the gauge group is
G=\mathrm{SU}(N)
with
N\geq 2
. A finite, periodic, hypercubic lattice of spacing
a_{k}>0
is fixed, with sites

\Lambda_{k}=\Bigl(\tfrac{a_{k}}{a_{0}}\Bigr)\,(\mathbb{Z}/L\mathbb{Z})^{3}\times(\mathbb{Z}/T\mathbb{Z}),

(6.1)

directed bonds
b=(x,\mu)
for
\mu\in\{0,1,2,3\}
, and the convention
U_{(x+\hat{\mu},-\mu)}=U_{(x,\mu)}^{-1}
for bond variables
U_{b}\in G
. The time coordinate is
x_{0}
, the reflection plane is

\Pi=\{x\in\Lambda_{k}:\ x_{0}=0\},

(6.2)

and the half-lattices are
\Lambda_{k}^{\pm}=\{x\in\Lambda_{k}:\ \pm x_{0}>0\}
. The involution
\theta:\Lambda_{k}\to\Lambda_{k}
is

\theta(x_{0},\mathbf{x})=(-x_{0},\mathbf{x}).

(6.3)

The Wilson action at inverse bare coupling
\beta_{k}>0
is

S_{W,k}[U]=\beta_{k}\sum_{p\subset\Lambda_{k}}\Bigl(1-\tfrac{1}{N}\,\Re\,\mathrm{Tr}\,U_{p}\Bigr),

(6.4)

where
U_{p}
is the ordered plaquette product. Temporal-axial gauge is chosen away from
\Pi
by fixing
U_{0}(x)=\mathbf{1}
for bonds not intersecting
\Pi
, as in
[
5
,
4
]
.

On each time slice, a reflection-covariant gauge-invariant transverse representative
A^{h}
is selected by orbit-wise minimization of the lattice Landau functional. The associated lattice Faddeev-Popov operator
M[A^{h}]
is real symmetric, local, and strictly positive on the orthogonal complement of constant adjoint fields. The covariant spatial Laplacian
\Delta_{A^{h}}
on a slice is

\Delta_{A^{h}}=\sum_{i=1}^{3}(D_{i}^{h})^{\dagger}D_{i}^{h}\ \geq\ 0,

(6.5)

with
D_{i}^{h}
the covariant finite differences built from the slice links of
A^{h}
. We fix
\sigma>0
and use the completely monotone near-plateau
\chi_{\sigma}
from Section (
4
). Set

P_{\sigma}:=\chi_{\sigma}(\Delta_{A^{h}})

(6.6)

By Bernstein’s theorem there exists a finite positive Borel measure
d\nu_{\sigma}
on
[0,\infty)
with

P_{\sigma}=\int_{0}^{\infty}e^{-t\Delta_{A^{h}}}\,d\nu_{\sigma}(t),\qquad\operatorname{supp}(d\nu_{\sigma})\subset[c_{-}\sigma^{-2},c_{+}\sigma^{-2}]

(6.7)

where
d\nu_{\sigma}
is a finite, positive Borel measure supported in
[c_{-}\sigma^{-2},c_{+}\sigma^{-2}]
with
0<c_{-}<c_{+}<\infty
. Moreover, the mass of
\nu_{\sigma}
is concentrated at the parabolic scale
s\sim\sigma^{-2}
(in the sense of exponentially decaying tails away from this scale).
Davies-Gaffney bounds imply the exponential locality estimate,

\|P_{\sigma}(x,y)\|\ \leq\ C(\sigma)\,e^{-\gamma(\sigma)\,d(x,y)}\qquad\text{for all slice sites }x,y.

(6.8)

The OS reflection is defined on bonds by

\theta(x_{0},\mathbf{x})=(-x_{0},\mathbf{x}),\qquad(\Theta U)(x,0)=U(\theta x-a\hat{0},0)^{-1},\qquad(\Theta U)(x,i)=U(\theta x,i)\quad(i=1,2,3)

(6.9)

Site and link reflections are unitarily equivalent via a half-time translation;
we work with the site reflection
\Theta
as above and use unitary conjugacy to relate to link
reflection when convenient Corollary 3.7.
As in
[
2
,
5
]
, site and link reflections are unitarily equivalent;
consequently, positive-type boundary kernels and OS-positivity statements are invariant under switching
between the two conventions by conjugation with the half-step time-translation on the single-slice Hilbert space.
Under temporal-axial gauge away from
\Pi
, the latter equals
\mathbf{1}
unless the bond intersects
\Pi
. For a functional
F
supported in
\Lambda_{k}^{+}
the reflection acts by

(\Theta F)(U)=\overline{F(\theta U)}.

(6.10)

The horizon-projected, gauge-fixed Euclidean measure is

d\mu_{k,\sigma}(U)=Z_{k,\sigma}^{-1}\,\Bigl(\prod_{t\in\mathbb{Z}/T\mathbb{Z}}\mathcal{K}_{\sigma}[U|_{t}]\Bigr)\,e^{-S_{W,k}[U]}\,\det\nolimits^{\prime}\!\bigl(M[A^{h}(U)]\bigr)\,\prod_{b\subset\Lambda_{k}}d\mu_{\mathrm{Haar}}(U_{b}),

(6.11)

where
[U|_{t}]
denotes the links on the spatial slice
\{x_{0}=t\}
, the symbol
\det^{\prime}
denotes the determinant on the orthogonal complement of constant adjoint fields, and the positive slice factor is

\mathcal{K}_{\sigma}[U|t]:=\frac{1}{\dim(\mathrm{ad})\,|\Lambda_{t}|}\,\mathrm{Tr}_{\ell^{2}(\Lambda_{t})\otimes\mathrm{ad}}\!\big(P_{\sigma}(U|t)\big)=\frac{1}{\dim(\mathrm{ad})\,|\Lambda_{t}|}\int_{0}^{\infty}\mathrm{Tr}\!\left(e^{-s\,\Delta_{A^{h}}(t)}\right)\,d\nu_{\sigma}(s)

(6.12)

By this normalization
0<c_{\sigma}\leq K_{\sigma}[U|t]\leq C_{\sigma}<\infty
with constants
independent of the spatial volume, which justifies Lemma 8.3.
Gauge invariance of (
6.11
) follows from invariance of Haar measure, of (
6.4
), of
\det^{\prime}M
, and the conjugation covariance of
P_{\sigma}
.

Theorem 6.1

(OS positivity)
.

For every gauge-invariant functional
F
supported in
\Lambda_{k}^{+}
and of even Grassmann parity,

\int\overline{(\Theta F)(U)}\,F(U)\,d\mu_{k,\sigma}(U)\ \geq\ 0.

(6.13)

Proof.

In temporal-axial gauge away from
\Pi
, the action splits as

S_{W,k}[U]=S^{(+)}[U|_{\Lambda_{k}^{+}}]+S^{(-)}[U|_{\Lambda_{k}^{-}}]+S^{(0)}[U|_{\Pi}],

(6.14)

where
S^{(\pm)}
involve plaquettes strictly contained in
\Lambda_{k}^{\pm}
, and
S^{(0)}
is the boundary slab contribution supported on bonds incident on
\Pi
. The Faddeev-Popov determinant admits the Grassmann representation

\det\nolimits^{\prime}\!\bigl(M[A^{h}]\bigr)=\int\exp\bigl(-\langle\bar{c},\,M[A^{h}]\,c\rangle\bigr)\,D\bar{c}\,Dc,

(6.15)

with site Grassmann fields constrained to the orthogonal complement of constants. The matrix of
M
is block tridiagonal across
\Pi
, and the diagonal blocks with Dirichlet boundary on
\Pi
are strictly positive on that complement. The Schur complement of the central block is strictly positive. Therefore the Gaussian Grassmann kernel factorizes into reflected copies times a positive boundary factor, which is reflection positive in the OS sense
[
4
]
. Next, by (
6.7
) each
\mathcal{K}_{\sigma}[U|_{t}]
is an integral of
\mathrm{Tr}\,e^{-t\Delta_{A^{h}}}
against a positive measure; the heat kernel is reflection invariant and positive, and its dependence across
\Pi
is exponentially local, so the product over
t
factorizes into reflected halves times a positive boundary contribution. Collecting the factors yields

\langle F,F\rangle_{\mathrm{OS}}=\int\overline{(\Theta F)(U)}\,F(U)\,e^{-S^{(+)}-S^{(-)}}\Bigl(\int e^{-S^{(0)}}\,d\mu^{(0)}\Bigr)\,d\mu^{(+)}\,d\mu^{(-)},

(6.16)

with
d\mu^{(\pm)}
positive reflection-covariant measures on the halves and
d\mu^{(0)}
the positive boundary kernel. The Cauchy-Schwarz inequality for reflection-positive forms implies (
6.13
)
[
1
,
2
]
.
∎

Define the one-slice configuration space
\mathcal{C}_{k}
of spatial links at fixed time, endowed with Haar product measure
d\mu_{\mathrm{Haar}}^{\mathrm{slice}}
, and the Hilbert space

\mathcal{H}_{k}=L^{2}\!\bigl(\mathcal{C}_{k},\,d\mu_{\mathrm{Haar}}^{\mathrm{slice}}\bigr).

(6.17)

Let
K_{k}(U^{\prime},U)
be the contribution to the weight from plaquettes straddling two consecutive time slices with boundary data
U,U^{\prime}
. The transfer operator
T_{k}:\mathcal{H}_{k}\to\mathcal{H}_{k}
is

(T_{k}\psi)(U^{\prime})=\int_{\mathcal{C}_{k}}K_{k}(U^{\prime},U)\,\psi(U)\,d\mu_{\mathrm{Haar}}^{\mathrm{slice}}(U).

(6.18)

By OS positivity,
T_{k}
is a positive, self-adjoint contraction
[
5
,
4
]
. The horizon-projected transfer operator is the compression

T_{k,\sigma}=P_{\sigma}^{1/2}\,T_{k}\,P_{\sigma}^{1/2},

(6.19)

again a positive, self-adjoint contraction.
The transfer Hamiltonian is

H_{k,\sigma}=-a_{k}^{-1}\log T_{k,\sigma}\ \geq\ 0.

(6.20)

Equivalently,
T_{k,\sigma}
is the compression of
T_{k}
by
P_{\sigma}^{1/2}
on the OS
single-slice Hilbert space, as summarized by (see Appendix (
14
)):
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{H}_{k}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{H}_{k}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{H}_{k,\sigma}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{H}_{k,\sigma}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\,T_{k}\,}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\,P_{\sigma}^{1/2}\,}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\,P_{\sigma}^{1/2}\,}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\,T_{k,\sigma}\,}

On a fixed slice, suppressing the time index, the positive covariance induced by the projector is

C_{k}=\int_{0}^{\infty}e^{-t\Delta_{A^{h}}}\,d\tilde{\nu}_{\sigma}(t),

(6.21)

for a finite positive Borel measure
d\tilde{\nu}_{\sigma}
supported in a compact subset of
(0,\infty)
that differs from
d\nu_{\sigma}
only by a smooth nonnegative weight arising from the quadratic part of the effective action. A dyadic partition of unity produces a decomposition with uniform exponential off-range bounds.

Theorem 6.2

(Finite-range-type decomposition)
.

There exist positive operators
C_{k}^{(j)}
for
j\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
such that

C_{k}=\sum_{j=0}^{\infty}C_{k}^{(j)}\quad\text{(norm convergence)},

(6.22)

and constants
c_{1},c_{2},c_{3}>0
, independent of
k
and
j
, with

\|C_{k}^{(j)}(x,y)\|\ \leq\ c_{1}\,\exp\!\Bigl(-\,\frac{d(x,y)}{c_{2}\,L^{j}\sigma}\Bigr)\quad\text{and}\quad 0\;\leq\;C^{(j)}_{k}\;\leq\;c_{3}\,\mathbf{1}

(6.23)

and each
C_{k}^{(j)}
is gauge covariant and reflection invariant. Here
L>1
parametrizes the dyadic
heat-time
partition used in the finite-range
decomposition of the projector-induced covariance; it is unrelated to the geometric

blocking factor

b\geq 2
used in the real-space RG step of Section (
8
).
We fix a smooth partition of unity
\{\eta_{j}\}_{j\geq 0}
on
(0,\infty)
with

\operatorname{supp}\eta_{j}\subset\big[c\,L^{2j}\sigma^{-2},\;C\,L^{2j}\sigma^{-2}\big]\qquad(0<c<C<\infty).

Since
t\asymp L^{2j}\sigma^{-2}
on
\operatorname{supp}\eta_{j}
, the kernel
e^{-t\Delta_{A^{h}}}
localizes over
a length
\sqrt{t}\asymp L^{j}\sigma^{-1}
This role of
\sigma^{2}
in the

decomposition
is distinct from the base-scale choice in the
original
horizon projector,
whose measure is supported at
t\sim\sigma^{-2}
, cf. Eq.4.12 and Eq.7.4; the latter fixes the
initial localization scale, while the dyadic partition organizes contributions across increasing
lengths
L^{j}\sigma
.

Proof.

Choose
L>1
and a smooth partition of unity
\{\eta_{j}\}_{j\geq 0}
on
(0,\infty)
with
\mathrm{supp}(\eta_{j})\subset[c\,L^{2j}\sigma^{2},C\,L^{2j}\sigma^{2}]
for fixed
0<c<C<\infty
and
\sum_{j\geq 0}\eta_{j}\equiv 1
. Set

C_{k}^{(j)}=\int_{0}^{\infty}\eta_{j}(t)\,e^{-t\Delta_{A^{h}}}\,d\tilde{\nu}_{\sigma}(t).

(6.24)

Positivity, reflection invariance, and gauge covariance are immediate from (
6.24
). The discrete heat-kernel bound yields
\|e^{-t\Delta_{A^{h}}}(x,y)\|\leq K_{1}\exp\!\bigl(-d(x,y)^{2}/(K_{2}t)\bigr)
, and since
t\asymp L^{2j}\sigma^{2}
on
\mathrm{supp}(\eta_{j})
, one gets (
6.23
) with
c_{1},c_{2}
depending only on
K_{1},K_{2},c,C
. Boundedness on
\ell^{2}
gives the spectral bound. Norm-convergence follows from the finiteness of
\int d\tilde{\nu}_{\sigma}
and the disjoint supports of the
\eta_{j}
.
∎

Let
b\geq 2
be the blocking factor, and
\mathbb{B}_{k}
the partition of
\Lambda_{k}
into disjoint four-dimensional blocks of side
b\,a_{k}
. A polymer is a finite, connected union
X
of blocks in
\mathbb{B}_{k}
. For a connected polymer
X
, write
\mathrm{diam}(X)
for the graph distance in block units and
|X|
for the number of blocks. The effective action at scale
k
is written as

\mathscr{S}_{k}(U)=\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}X\subset\mathbb{B}_{k}\\
X\text{ connected}\end{subarray}}\Phi_{k}(X;U|_{X}),

(6.25)

with
\Phi_{k}(X;\cdot)
gauge invariant, reflection covariant, and supported in
X
. For
a>0
define the diameter-weighted norm

\|\Phi_{k}\|_{a}=\sup_{B\in\mathbb{B}_{k}}\ \sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}X\ni B\\
X\text{ connected}\end{subarray}}\ \mathrm{ess\,sup}_{U|_{X}}\ \|\Phi_{k}(X;U|_{X})\|\,e^{\,a\,\mathrm{diam}(X)},

(6.26)

where
\|\cdot\|
is the operator norm induced by the Gaussian covariance
C_{k}
and the regulator below (see Appendix (
13
).

Fix a smooth convex
\varphi:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)
with
\varphi(s)=s
on
[0,1]
and
\varphi(s)=s^{2}
on
[2,\infty)
. For
\lambda>0
and
\delta\in(0,1)
set

\mathcal{R}_{k}(U)=\exp\!\Bigl(-\lambda\sum_{p\subset\Lambda_{k}}\varphi\bigl(\tfrac{1}{2}\,\|\,\mathbf{1}-U_{p}\,\|_{F}^{2}\bigr)\Bigr),\qquad\mathsf{SF}_{k}=\Bigl\{U:\ \|\,\mathbf{1}-U_{p}\,\|_{F}\leq\delta,\ \forall p\Bigr\}.

(6.27)

Then
\mathcal{R}_{k}
is a strictly positive, reflection-invariant, gauge-invariant product of convex plaquette penalties. There exist
c,c^{\prime}>0
independent of
k
such that

\int|F|\,\mathcal{R}_{k}\,d\mu_{k,\sigma}\ \leq\ e^{-c\lambda}\,\Bigl(\int|F|^{2}\,d\mu_{k,\sigma}\Bigr)^{1/2},\qquad\mu_{k,\sigma}(\mathsf{SF}_{k}^{c})\ \leq\ e^{-c^{\prime}\lambda},

(6.28)

for every block-local measurable
F
; this follows from reflection positivity and Hölder-type inequalities
[
4
,
10
]
.

Let
a_{k+1}=b\,a_{k}
and
\mathcal{B}_{k}
be the reflection-covariant, gauge-equivariant, block-local link averaging map followed by nearest-neighbor projection to
G
. The coarse effective action
\mathscr{S}_{k+1}
is defined by

e^{-\mathscr{S}_{k+1}(\bar{U})}=Z_{k}^{-1}\int\mathbf{1}_{\{\mathcal{B}_{k}(U)=\bar{U}\}}\,\Bigl(\prod_{\text{internal slices}}\mathcal{K}_{\sigma}[U|_{t}]\Bigr)\,e^{-\mathscr{S}_{k}(U)}\,e^{-S_{W,k}^{\mathrm{int}}(U)}\,\mathcal{R}_{k}(U)\,d\mu_{k,\sigma}(U),

(6.29)

where
S_{W,k}^{\mathrm{int}}
sums Wilson plaquettes entirely inside blocks and the product runs over internal block time-slices. After a cumulant expansion,
\mathscr{S}_{k+1}
has the form (
6.25
) with activities
\Phi_{k+1}
given by connected cumulants of
\{\Phi_{k}(X_{i})\}
.

Split the covariance as
C_{k}=C_{k}^{\mathrm{int}}+C_{k}^{\mathrm{ext}}
with

C_{k}^{\mathrm{int}}=\sum_{j\leq j_{*}}C_{k}^{(j)},\qquad C_{k}^{\mathrm{ext}}=\sum_{j>j_{*}}C_{k}^{(j)},

(6.30)

where
j_{*}
is the largest integer with
L^{j_{*}}\sigma\leq c_{*}\,b\,a_{k}
for small fixed
c_{*}>0
. Then
C_{k}^{\mathrm{int}}
has kernel exponentially small across distinct blocks, and
C_{k}^{\mathrm{ext}}
couples only a collar of width
\asymp L^{j_{*}}\sigma
around block boundaries. The Battle-Brydges-Federbush tree formula yields the following uniform tree bound.

Lemma 6.3

(Tree bound)
.

Let
F_{1},\dots,F_{n}
be block-local functionals supported in distinct blocks, measurable on
\mathsf{SF}_{k}
, and polynomially bounded together with their first slice derivatives. Then

\bigl|\langle F_{1};\dots;F_{n}\rangle^{T}_{C_{k}^{\mathrm{int}}}\bigr|\ \leq\ \Bigl(\prod_{i=1}^{n}\|F_{i}\|\Bigr)\,\sum_{\mathcal{T}}\ \prod_{\{i,j\}\in E(\mathcal{T})}\,A\,e^{-\mathrm{dist}(X_{i},X_{j})/(B\,L^{j_{*}}\sigma)},

(6.31)

with constants
A,B
independent of
k
, the sum over labeled trees
\mathcal{T}
on
\{1,\dots,n\}
, and
\|F_{i}\|
the Gaussian operator norm for covariance
C_{k}^{\mathrm{int}}
.

Proof.

The Brydges-Battle-Federbush representation expresses the connected cumulant as an integral over tree-parameterized covariances; each edge contributes one covariance factor connecting the supports of
F_{i}
and
F_{j}
. The operator norm between two blocks at block-distance
D
is bounded by
A\,\exp(-D/(B\,L^{j_{*}}\sigma))
thanks to (
6.23
). The product over edges yields (
6.31
); uniformity in
k
follows from
L^{j_{*}}\sigma\lesssim b\,a_{k}
.
∎

Connected coarse activities are sums over connected families
\{X_{i}\}
of fine-scale polymers whose union projects onto a given coarse polymer
Y
, weighted by
\langle\Phi_{k}(X_{1});\dots;\Phi_{k}(X_{n})\rangle^{T}_{C_{k}^{\mathrm{int}}}
. On
\mathsf{SF}_{k}
, each
\|\Phi_{k}(X_{i})\|\leq\|\Phi_{k}\|_{a}e^{-a\,\mathrm{diam}(X_{i})}
. Lemma
6.3
thus yields a tree sum with edge weights
Ae^{-\mathrm{dist}/(BL^{j_{*}}\sigma)}
. The Kotecký-Preiss criterion
[
19
]
then gives a quadratic contraction.

Proposition 6.4

(Small-field contraction)
.

There exist
a>0
,
\epsilon_{0}>0
,
C_{1}<\infty
, independent of
k
, such that if
\|\Phi_{k}\|_{a}\leq\epsilon_{0}
, then the contribution of
\mathsf{SF}_{k}
to
\Phi_{k+1}
satisfies

\|\Phi_{k+1}\|_{a}\ \leq\ C_{1}\,\|\Phi_{k}\|_{a}^{2}.

(6.32)

Proof.

Fix a coarse polymer
Y
. The cumulant expansion and Lemma
6.3
bound
\Phi_{k+1}(Y)
by a sum over trees with vertex weights
\|\Phi_{k}\|_{a}e^{-a\,\mathrm{diam}(X_{i})}
and edge weights
Ae^{-\mathrm{dist}/(BL^{j_{*}}\sigma)}
. For
\|\Phi_{k}\|_{a}
small the combinatorial sum converges absolutely; choosing
a<1/(BL^{j_{*}}\sigma)
uniformly in
k
allows the exponential weights to reproduce
e^{-a\,\mathrm{diam}(Y)}
. Summing over all families projecting to
Y
gives (
6.32
).
∎

The large-field region
\mathsf{SF}_{k}^{c}
is controlled by the regulator
\mathcal{R}_{k}
.

Proposition 6.5

(Large-field suppression)
.

There exist
c_{4},C_{2}>0
such that, for all
\lambda\geq 1
, the contribution of
\mathsf{SF}_{k}^{c}
to
\|\Phi_{k+1}\|_{a}
satisfies

\bigl\|\Phi_{k+1}^{(\mathrm{large})}\bigr\|_{a}\ \leq\ C_{2}\,e^{-c_{4}\lambda}.

(6.33)

Proof.

Decompose (
6.29
) into
\mathsf{SF}_{k}\cup\mathsf{SF}_{k}^{c}
. On
\mathsf{SF}_{k}^{c}
, (
6.28
) bounds the integral of any block-local cumulant integrand
F
by
e^{-c\lambda}\|F\|_{L^{2}(\mu_{k,\sigma})}
. A second Cauchy-Schwarz yields (
6.33
) with
c_{4}=c/2
; constants depend only on uniform covariance bounds and not on
k
.
∎

Irrelevant operators generated by
C_{k}^{\mathrm{ext}}
and by the block projection
\mathrm{Proj}_{G}
produce a summable remainder.

Lemma 6.6

(Summable remainder)
.

There exist
C_{3}<\infty
and
\gamma>0
, independent of
k
, such that

\bigl\|\Phi_{k+1}^{(\mathrm{rem})}\bigr\|_{a}\ \leq\ C_{3}\,b^{-\gamma k}.

(6.34)

Proof.

The kernel of
C_{k}^{\mathrm{ext}}
decays like
\exp(-d/(c_{2}L^{j_{*}}\sigma))
with
L^{j_{*}}\sigma\asymp b\,a_{k}
; any connected contribution mediated only by
C_{k}^{\mathrm{ext}}
across
m
blocks acquires a factor
e^{-cm}
. Counting placements yields a geometric series bounded by
C_{3}b^{-\gamma k}
. The map
\mathrm{Proj}_{G}
differs from the identity by an analytic map with uniformly bounded Taylor coefficients on
\mathsf{SF}_{k}
, so its connected contributions are of higher polymer order and likewise summable over scales.
∎

Theorem 6.7

(Uniform ultraviolet stability)
.

There exist
\alpha>0
,
\epsilon>0
, and
C<\infty
, independent of
k
, such that if
\|\Phi_{k}\|_{\alpha}\leq\epsilon
, then

\|\Phi_{k+1}\|_{\alpha}\ \leq\ C\,\|\Phi_{k}\|_{\alpha}^{2}\ +\ C\,\delta_{k},

(6.35)

where

\delta_{k}\;=\;e^{-c_{4}\lambda_{k}}\;+\;b^{-\gamma k},\qquad\lambda_{k}\;\uparrow\;\text{(e.g. }\lambda_{k}=\lambda_{0}+\alpha k\text{ with }\alpha>0)

(6.36)

with
c_{4},\gamma>0
as in (
6.33
) and (
6.34
). In particular, choose
\lambda_{k}=\lambda_{0}+\alpha k
so that
e^{-c_{4}\lambda_{k}}
decays geometrically; then
\sum_{k}\delta_{k}<\infty
. Taking
\epsilon>0
so that
C\epsilon\leq\epsilon/2
yields
\sup_{k}\|\Phi_{k}\|_{a}\leq 2\epsilon
.

Proof.

Decompose

\Phi_{k+1}=\Phi_{k+1}^{(\mathrm{small})}+\Phi_{k+1}^{(\mathrm{large})}+\Phi_{k+1}^{(\mathrm{rem})}.

(6.37)

By Proposition
6.4
,
\|\Phi_{k+1}^{(\mathrm{small})}\|_{\alpha}\leq C_{1}\|\Phi_{k}\|_{\alpha}^{2}
. By Proposition
6.5
,
\|\Phi_{k+1}^{(\mathrm{large})}\|_{\alpha}\leq C_{2}e^{-c_{4}\lambda}
. By Lemma
6.6
,
\|\Phi_{k+1}^{(\mathrm{rem})}\|_{\alpha}\leq C_{3}b^{-\gamma k}
. Setting
C=\max\{C_{1},C_{2},C_{3}\}
gives (
6.35
)-(
6.36
). The iterative bound follows by continuity: if
\|\Phi_{k}\|_{\alpha}\leq\epsilon
with
C\epsilon\leq\epsilon/2
, then
\|\Phi_{k+1}\|_{\alpha}\leq\epsilon/2+C\delta_{k}
. Choosing
\lambda
so that
\sum_{j\geq 0}e^{-c_{4}\lambda}<\epsilon/(2C)
and using
\sum_{j\geq 0}b^{-\gamma j}<\infty
yields
\sup_{k}\|\Phi_{k}\|_{\alpha}\leq 2\epsilon
.
∎

The uniform bound (
6.35
) together with Theorem
6.1
and the definition (
6.19
) implies that at each scale the kernels
K_{k}
and
T_{k,\sigma}
are defined by absolutely convergent expansions with scale-independent locality constants. In particular, the spectral calculus for positive contractions applies uniformly in the spatial volume, and the spectral representation of time-sliced gauge-invariant two-point functions has a common domain of analyticity independent of
k
. These facts will be used in the step-to-step spectral gap comparison. The absolute convergence with scale-independent locality implies that the functional calculus for positive contractions
f(T_{k,\sigma})
is uniform in the volume and
k
, and the Laplace transform representation of time-sliced two-point functions has a common domain of analyticity independent of
k
.

Appendix 7
Persistence of Exponential Clustering (Theorem B)

This section establishes exponential decay of connected, gauge-invariant correlation functions at every renormalization scale and shows that the corresponding decay rate is bounded from below by a strictly positive, scale-independent constant. The argument is self-contained. It fixes the lattice, time-reflection, and transfer time-slicing formalism and proves reflection positivity for the projected measure; it then constructs the Osterwalder-Schrader Hilbert space and transfer operator. With this structure in place, it derives a polymer representation for truncated correlations under a small-activity hypothesis that is verified at all scales by uniform ultraviolet stability. Finally, it proves a Kotecký-Preiss-type estimate that yields exponential clustering with a rate that does not deteriorate under the renormalization map, thereby establishing persistence across scales. Let
w_{k}(Y)
be the polymer weights for truncated gauge-invariant correlators at scale
k
.
There exist
a>0
,
0<\delta<1
such that for all sites
x

\sum_{Y\ni x}e^{a|Y|}\,\|w_{k}(Y)\|\leq\delta,\qquad\sup_{Y}\sum_{Y^{\prime}\sim Y}e^{a|Y^{\prime}|}\,\|w_{k}(Y^{\prime})\|\leq\delta,

(7.1)

uniformly in the spatial volume and in
k
.
Then the cluster expansion converges absolutely and connected correlations decay as

\exp(-m^{\ast}\,\mathrm{dist}_{k})
with
m^{\ast}>0
independent of
k
.

Throughout, the gauge group is
G=\mathrm{SU}(N)
with
N\geq 2
. Spatial volumes are finite tori; thermodynamic limits are taken only after bounds are proven uniformly in the volume.

Fix an integer blocking factor
b\geq 2
and set
a_{k}=b^{k}a_{0}
. For a finite, periodic, hypercubic lattice we write

\Lambda_{k}\;=\;\Big\{x=(x_{0},x_{1},x_{2},x_{3})\in a_{k}\mathbb{Z}^{4}:\ -\tfrac{T_{k}}{2}\leq x_{0}<\tfrac{T_{k}}{2},\ -\tfrac{L_{k}}{2}\leq x_{i}<\tfrac{L_{k}}{2}\Big\},

(7.2)

with periodic identifications. Directed bonds are pairs
b=(x,\mu)
,
\mu\in\{0,1,2,3\}
, endowed with the orientation convention
U(x+\hat{\mu},-\mu)=U(x,\mu)^{-1}
. A configuration is
U=\{U(x,\mu)\in G\}_{(x,\mu)}
.

Time reflection is the involution
\theta:\Lambda_{k}\to\Lambda_{k}
,
\theta(x_{0},\mathbf{x})=(-x_{0},\mathbf{x})
. We set

\Lambda_{k}^{+}=\{x\in\Lambda_{k}:x_{0}>0\},\qquad\Lambda_{k}^{-}=\theta(\Lambda_{k}^{+}),\qquad\Pi_{k}=\{x\in\Lambda_{k}:x_{0}=0\}.

(7.3)

On bonds we define the reflected configuration
\Theta U
by

(\Theta U)(x,0)\;=\;U(\theta x-\hat{0},0)^{-1},\qquad(\Theta U)(x,i)\;=\;U(\theta x,i)\quad(i=1,2,3),

(7.4)

which is the standard reflection of link variables preserving the Wilson action and Haar measure
[
1
,
4
,
10
]
.

On each time slice
x_{0}=t
we select a gauge-invariant transverse representative
A^{h}
by orbit-wise minimization of the lattice Landau functional within the fundamental modular region; the selection is measurable, reflection-covariant, and compatible with temporal-axial gauge away from
\Pi_{k}
. The associated slice covariant Laplacian
\Delta_{A^{h}}
on site-adjoint fields is positive, self-adjoint, and local. Fix
\sigma>0
and a Gevrey cutoff
\chi_{\sigma}:[0,\infty)\to[0,1]
that equals
1
on
[0,\sigma]
and decreases rapidly to
0
beyond
2\sigma
. The horizon projector is

P_{\sigma}\;=\;\chi_{\sigma}\!\big({\Delta_{A^{h}}}\big)\;=\;\int_{0}^{\infty}e^{-t\Delta_{A^{h}}}\,d\nu_{\sigma}(t),

(7.5)

where
d\nu_{\sigma}
is a finite positive Borel measure supported in
[c_{1}\sigma^{-2},c_{2}\sigma^{-2}]
. By standard heat-kernel bounds on graphs of bounded degree
[
13
]
and Combes-Thomas estimates
[
14
]
,

\|P_{\sigma}(x,y)\|\;\leq\;C_{\sigma}\,e^{-\gamma_{\sigma}\,d(x,y)},

(7.6)

uniformly in the volume, where
d
is the graph distance on the slice.

Let
S_{W}[U;\beta]=\beta\sum_{p}(1-\tfrac{1}{N}\Re\mathrm{Tr}\,U_{p})
denote the Wilson action. The projected, gauge-fixed Euclidean measure at scale
k
is

d\mu_{k,\sigma}(U)\;=\;Z_{k,\sigma}^{-1}\,\Big(\prod_{t}{\det}^{\prime}M[A^{h}(t)]\Big)\,\prod_{t}\mathcal{P}_{\sigma,t}(U)\,e^{-S_{W}[U;\beta_{k}]}\,d\mu_{\mathrm{Haar}}(U)

(7.7)

where
M[A^{h}(t)]
is the Faddeev-Popov operator restricted to slice
t
,
\mathcal{P}_{\sigma,t}
is the positive functional corresponding to inserting
P_{\sigma}
on slice
t
, and
d\mu_{\mathrm{Haar}}
is the product Haar measure over bonds. Each
\mathcal{P}_{\sigma,t}
is exponentially local and reflection covariant.
Throughout we take the slice multiplier to be the gauge invariant scalar

p_{\sigma}\big[U^{h}|_{t}\big]\;:=\;\mathrm{Tr}\,P_{\sigma}(t)\quad\text{with}\quad P_{\sigma}(t)=\chi_{\sigma}\!\left({\Delta_{A^{h}}(t)}\right),

(7.8)

so that
P_{\sigma,t}
acts by multiplication by
p_{\sigma}[U^{h}|_{t}]
on the one slice
L^{2}
space.
This choice is reflection covariant, positive, and exponentially local in the slice-distance.
(Any other positive, reflection covariant scalar built from
P_{\sigma}(t)
-e.g.
p_{\sigma}=\exp(-\langle\varphi,(I-P_{\sigma})\varphi\rangle)
-would also work; see Sec.(
10
).)

Theorem 7.1

(Osterwalder-Schrader positivity)
.

If
F
is a complex-valued functional measurable with respect to links supported in
\Lambda_{k}^{+}
and gauge-invariant under transformations supported in
\Lambda_{k}^{+}
, then

\int(\Theta F)(U)\,F(U)\,d\mu_{k,\sigma}(U)\;\geq\;0.

(7.9)

Proof.

Decompose the Wilson action as
S_{W}=S_{+}+S_{-}+S_{0}
, where
S_{\pm}
collect plaquettes entirely in
\Lambda_{k}^{\pm}
and
S_{0}
collects boundary plaquettes intersecting
\Pi_{k}
. In temporal-axial gauge, time-like links are trivial away from
\Pi_{k}
, whence
S_{+}
and
S_{-}
depend only on links in their respective half-lattices, and
S_{0}
couples only links in a finite-width slab around
\Pi_{k}
. The Haar measure factors as
d\mu_{\mathrm{Haar}}=d\mu_{+}\,d\mu_{0}\,d\mu_{-}
. The determinant
\prod_{t}\det M[A^{h}(t)]
is reflection-invariant, and each
\mathcal{P}_{\sigma,t}
factors as
\mathcal{P}_{\sigma,t}=\mathcal{P}_{\sigma,t}^{+}\,\mathcal{R}_{\sigma,t}\,\mathcal{P}_{\sigma,t}^{-}
with
\mathcal{R}_{\sigma,t}\geq 0
, supported in a finite-width slab containing
\Pi_{k}
, and reflection-invariant.

Define

G(U)\;=\;F(U)\,e^{-\tfrac{1}{2}S_{+}[U]}\,\prod_{t}\big(\mathcal{P}_{\sigma,t}^{+}(U)\big)^{1/2}\,\big(\det M[A^{h}(t)]\big)^{1/2}.

(7.10)

A direct substitution into (
7.7
) shows

\int(\Theta F)F\,d\mu_{k,\sigma}\;=\;Z_{k,\sigma}^{-1}\int\overline{G(\Theta U)}\,K(U)\,G(U)\,d\lambda_{+}\,d\lambda_{0}\,d\lambda_{-},

(7.11)

with the nonnegative, reflection-invariant boundary kernel

K(U)\;=\;e^{-S_{0}[U]}\,\prod_{t}\mathcal{R}_{\sigma,t}(U)\;\geq\;0.

(7.12)

With
P_{\sigma,t}=\chi_{\sigma}(\Delta_{A^{h}}(t))
and
\chi_{\sigma}
completely monotone,

P_{\sigma,t}
admits the positive heat-kernel representation

P_{\sigma,t}=\int_{0}^{\infty}e^{-t^{\prime}\Delta_{A^{h}}(t)}\,d\nu_{\sigma}(t^{\prime})
with
d\nu_{\sigma}\geq 0
(Sections 4 and 5).
Writing
P_{\sigma,t}=P^{+}_{\sigma,t}R_{\sigma,t}P^{-}_{\sigma,t}
with
R_{\sigma,t}\geq 0
supported in a fixed slab
around
\Pi_{k}
yields a product of nonnegative, reflection-covariant slice terms.
Hence the boundary factor
K(U)
in Eq.7.10 is a positive kernel on the single-slice space,
and the OS form is nonnegative by the standard factorization argument.

By Fubini’s theorem and positivity of
K
,

\int\overline{G(\Theta U)}\,K(U)\,G(U)\,d\lambda_{+}\,d\lambda_{0}\,d\lambda_{-}\;=\;\int\Big|\int G(U)\,K(U)^{1/2}\,d\lambda_{-}\Big|^{2}\,d\lambda_{0}\,d\lambda_{+}\;\geq\;0,

(7.13)

which implies (
7.9
).
∎

Define the Osterwalder-Schrader seminorm

\|F\|_{\mathrm{OS},k}^{2}\;=\;\int(\Theta F)\,F\,d\mu_{k,\sigma},

(7.14)

the null space
\mathcal{N}_{k}=\{F:\|F\|_{\mathrm{OS},k}=0\}
, and the pre-Hilbert space
\mathcal{D}_{k}=\{F:\mathrm{supp}(F)\subset\Lambda_{k}^{+}\}
. The quotient
\mathcal{D}_{k}/\mathcal{N}_{k}
, completed in the induced norm, is a Hilbert space
\mathcal{H}_{k}
with inner product
\langle[F],[G]\rangle_{\mathcal{H}_{k}}=\int(\Theta F)G\,d\mu_{k,\sigma}
, where
[F]
denotes the equivalence class. The constant functional
1
defines the cyclic vacuum
\Omega_{k}=[1]
.

Let
\tau
be the time-translation by one lattice unit:
(\tau U)(x,\mu)=U(x-a_{k}\hat{0},\mu)
. For
F\in\mathcal{D}_{k}
set
(\mathcal{U}F)(U)=F(\tau U)
. Time-translation invariance of
S_{W}
,
\det M
, and
\{\mathcal{P}_{\sigma,t}\}
yields the OS-isometry

\int(\Theta\,\mathcal{U}F)\,\mathcal{U}G\,d\mu_{k,\sigma}\;=\;\int(\Theta F)\,G\,d\mu_{k,\sigma}.

(7.15)

Hence
\mathcal{U}
descends to a contraction
T_{k}
on
\mathcal{H}_{k}
by
T_{k}[F]=[\mathcal{U}F]
. By the standard OS reconstruction
[
1
,
7
]
,
T_{k}
is a positive, self-adjoint contraction and
T_{k}\Omega_{k}=\Omega_{k}
. The discrete transfer Hamiltonian is

H_{k}\;=\;-a_{k}^{-1}\log T_{k},

(7.16)

which is positive self-adjoint via spectral calculus. If
F
is local, gauge-invariant, and
\langle\Omega_{k},[F]\rangle=0
, then the time-separated two-point function has the spectral representation

\int(\Theta F)\,\mathcal{U}^{t}F\,d\mu_{k,\sigma}\;=\;\sum_{n\geq 1}|\langle\chi_{n}^{(k)},[F]\rangle|^{2}\,e^{-E_{n}^{(k)}\,t\,a_{k}},\qquad t\in\mathbb{N},

(7.17)

where
0=E_{0}^{(k)}\leq E_{1}^{(k)}\leq\cdots
are the eigenvalues of
H_{k}
and
\{\chi_{n}^{(k)}\}
is an orthonormal eigenbasis.

Fix
r\in\mathbb{N}
. A local, gauge-invariant observable supported at
x\in\Lambda_{k}
is a bounded measurable functional
O_{x}
depending only on links in
B_{k}(x;r)=\{y:d(y,x)\leq r\}
and satisfying
O_{x}(g\cdot U)=O_{x}(U)
for all gauge transformations
g
supported in
B_{k}(x;r)
. Denote
\|O\|_{\infty}=\sup|O_{x}|
. For
x,y\in\Lambda_{k}
define the connected two-point function

\langle O_{x};O_{y}\rangle_{k}\;=\;\int O_{x}O_{y}\,d\mu_{k,\sigma}-\int O_{x}\,d\mu_{k,\sigma}\,\int O_{y}\,d\mu_{k,\sigma}.

(7.18)

Let
d_{k}(x,y)
denote the graph distance on
\Lambda_{k}
.

We assume the following uniform small-activity hypothesis, which is guaranteed at each scale by the ultraviolet stability theorem proved earlier.

\|\Phi_{k}\|_{a}=\sup_{x\in\Lambda_{k}}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}X\ni x\\
X\ \text{conn.}\end{subarray}}\|\Phi_{k}(X)\|\,e^{a\,\mathrm{diam}(X)}\leq\varepsilon,\qquad\varepsilon\in(0,1).

(7.19)

where
S_{k}=\sum_{X}\Phi_{k}(X)
is the effective interaction at scale
k
, the sum runs over finite, connected unions
X
of
k
-blocks, and
\|\cdot\|
is the operator norm with respect to the finite-range Gaussian covariance supplied by the covariant finite-range decomposition. The constants
a>0
and
\varepsilon\in(0,1)
do not depend on
k
.
Under (
7.19
), the abstract polymer formalism
[
19
,
25
]
expresses truncated correlations as absolutely convergent sums over connected polymer clusters that intersect the supports of the observables. The following representation includes explicit uniform bounds.

Proposition 7.2

(Cluster representation of truncated correlators)
.

Let
O_{x}
,
O_{y}
be bounded, gauge-invariant observables supported in
B_{k}(x;r)
and
B_{k}(y;r)
. There exists a kernel
K(B,B^{\prime})\geq 0
, supported on nearest-neighbor
k
-blocks and satisfying

\sum_{B^{\prime}:\,B^{\prime}\sim B}K(B,B^{\prime})\;\leq\;C_{1}\varepsilon,

(7.20)

uniformly in
k
, such that

\langle O_{x};O_{y}\rangle_{k}\;=\;\sum_{\mathcal{C}\ \mathrm{conn.}}W_{k}(\mathcal{C};O_{x},O_{y}),

(7.21)

where the sum is over finite, connected sets
\mathcal{C}
of
k
-blocks intersecting both
B_{k}(x;r)
and
B_{k}(y;r)
, and

|W_{k}(\mathcal{C};O_{x},O_{y})|\;\leq\;C_{0}\,\|O\|_{\infty}^{2}\,e^{-\tfrac{a}{2}\,\mathrm{diam}(\mathcal{C})}\,\sum_{T\in\mathcal{T}(\mathcal{C})}\ \prod_{(B,B^{\prime})\in E(T)}K(B,B^{\prime}).

(7.22)

Here
C_{0}=C_{0}(a)
,
\mathcal{T}(\mathcal{C})
denotes spanning trees on
\mathcal{C}
, and
E(T)
the edge set of
T
.

Proof.

Introduce sources
\lambda_{1},\lambda_{2}\in\mathbb{R}
coupling to
O_{x}
,
O_{y}
and define the generating functional

Z_{k}(\lambda_{1},\lambda_{2})\;=\;\int\exp\big(\lambda_{1}O_{x}+\lambda_{2}O_{y}\big)\,d\mu_{k,\sigma}.

(7.23)

By gauge invariance and boundedness of
\Phi_{k}
, the logarithm admits the convergent polymer expansion

\log Z_{k}(\lambda_{1},\lambda_{2})\;=\;\sum_{X\ \mathrm{conn.}}\zeta_{k}(X;\lambda_{1},\lambda_{2}),

(7.24)

with connected cluster weights
\zeta_{k}(X;\lambda_{1},\lambda_{2})
supported on
X
, analytic near
(0,0)
, and bounded as

|\zeta_{k}(X;\lambda_{1},\lambda_{2})|\;\leq\;\tilde{C}\,e^{-a\,\mathrm{diam}(X)}\,\exp\!\Big(c\,|\lambda_{1}|\,\mathbf{1}_{X\cap B_{k}(x;r)\neq\varnothing}+c\,|\lambda_{2}|\,\mathbf{1}_{X\cap B_{k}(y;r)\neq\varnothing}\Big),

(7.25)

with constants
\tilde{C},c
depending only on
a
, uniformly in
k
; see
[
19
, Thm. 3]
,
[
25
, Sec. 4]
. Differentiating twice at
(0,0)
gives

\langle O_{x};O_{y}\rangle_{k}\;=\;\sum_{X\ \mathrm{conn.}}\ \frac{\partial^{2}}{\partial\lambda_{1}\partial\lambda_{2}}\zeta_{k}(X;\lambda_{1},\lambda_{2})\bigg|_{0,0}.

(7.26)

Only clusters
X
intersecting both supports contribute. The Brydges-Battle-Federbush tree-graph inequality bounds each connected weight by a sum over spanning trees with edge weights controlled by the finite-range covariance pieces; the covariant finite-range decomposition and (
7.19
) imply the existence of
K(B,B^{\prime})
obeying (
7.20
). Summing the remaining activities and absorbing constants yields (
7.22
), and reorganizing the sum by the connected support
\mathcal{C}
gives (
7.21
).
∎

Theorem 7.3

(Exponential clustering at scale
k
)
.

Assume (
7.19
). There exist constants
A<\infty
and
m>0
, independent of
k
, such that for any bounded, gauge-invariant local observables
O_{x}
,
O_{y}
supported in
B_{k}(x;r)
,
B_{k}(y;r)
,

|\langle O_{x};O_{y}\rangle_{k}|\;\leq\;A\,\|O\|_{\infty}^{2}\,\exp\!\big(-m\,(d_{k}(x,y)-2r)\big).

(7.27)

Proof.

Let
D=d_{k}(x,y)-2r\geq 0
. Any connected
\mathcal{C}
intersecting both supports satisfies
\mathrm{diam}(\mathcal{C})\geq D
. By Proposition
7.2
,

|\langle O_{x};O_{y}\rangle_{k}|\;\leq\;C_{0}\,\|O\|_{\infty}^{2}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\mathcal{C}\ \mathrm{conn.}\\
\mathrm{diam}(\mathcal{C})\geq D\end{subarray}}e^{-\tfrac{a}{2}\,\mathrm{diam}(\mathcal{C})}\,\sum_{T\in\mathcal{T}(\mathcal{C})}\ \prod_{(B,B^{\prime})\in E(T)}K(B,B^{\prime}).

(7.28)

Fix a root
B_{0}\in\mathcal{C}
. Using (
7.20
) and iterating from the leaves inwards yields

\sum_{T\in\mathcal{T}(\mathcal{C})}\ \prod_{(B,B^{\prime})\in E(T)}K(B,B^{\prime})\;\leq\;(C_{1}\varepsilon)^{|\mathcal{C}|-1}.

(7.29)

Connected block sets
\mathcal{C}\subset\mathbb{Z}^{4}
of cardinality
n
are counted by at most
C_{2}\,e^{C_{3}n}
, and
\mathrm{diam}(\mathcal{C})\leq C_{4}n
. Splitting the sum over
n
and using
\mathrm{diam}(\mathcal{C})\geq D
,

|\langle O_{x};O_{y}\rangle_{k}|\;\leq\;C_{0}\,\|O\|_{\infty}^{2}\,e^{-\tfrac{a}{2}D}\sum_{n\geq\lceil D/C_{4}\rceil}C_{2}\,e^{C_{3}n}\,(C_{1}\varepsilon)^{n-1}.

(7.30)

Choosing
\varepsilon>0
so small that
e^{C_{3}}C_{1}\varepsilon<1
makes the series bounded by
C_{5}\,e^{-\tilde{c}D}
with
\tilde{c}=\tfrac{1}{C_{4}}\log\big((e^{C_{3}}C_{1}\varepsilon)^{-1}\big)>0
. Setting
A=C_{0}C_{5}
and
m=\min\{\tfrac{a}{2},\tilde{c}\}
gives (
7.27
).
∎

Theorem 7.4

(Persistence of exponential clustering)
.

For sufficiently small bare coupling
0<\beta<\beta_{0}(N)
, the uniform polymer bound Eq. (
7.19
)
is satisfied at every scale
k
(by Lemma (
7.1
) above). Consequently, there exist constants

A^{*}<\infty
and
m^{*}>0
(independent of
k
) such that
for all scales
k
,

C_{k}(n)\;\leq\;A^{*}\,e^{-\,m^{*}\,na_{k}}

(7.31)

for every connected, gauge-invariant
n
-step temporal correlation at scale
k
.
In other words, exponential clustering with a fixed rate
m^{*}>0
persists uniformly under
repeated renormalization.

Proof.

Apply Theorem
7.3
at each
k
. The constants depend only on
a
and on the finite-range decomposition and small-activity constants, which are uniform in
k
.
∎

Exponential decay in Euclidean time follows from the transfer operator. For completeness we record it and its spectral consequence.

Proposition 7.5

(Time-direction clustering and spectral gap)
.

Let
F
be a bounded, gauge-invariant observable supported on a single time slice with
\int F\,d\mu_{k,\sigma}=0
. There exist
A_{t}<\infty
and
m_{t}>0
, independent of
k
, such that

\int(\Theta F)\,\mathcal{U}^{t}F\,d\mu_{k,\sigma}\;\leq\;A_{t}\,e^{-m_{t}\,t\,a_{k}}\qquad(t\in\mathbb{N}).

(7.32)

In the spectral representation (
7.17
) one has
E_{1}^{(k)}\geq m_{t}
.

Proof.

Choose
x\in\Pi_{k}+a_{k}\hat{0}
and take
O_{x}=F
supported near
x_{0}=a_{k}
and
O_{y}=\mathcal{U}^{t}F
supported near
x_{0}=(t+1)a_{k}
. Then
d_{k}(x,y)=t
up to a fixed additive constant, so Theorem
7.4
yields

\int(\Theta F)\,\mathcal{U}^{t}F\,d\mu_{k,\sigma}\;=\;\langle O_{x};O_{y}\rangle_{k}\;\leq\;A_{*}\,\|F\|_{\infty}^{2}\,e^{-m_{*}^{\prime}ta_{k}},

(7.33)

with
m_{*}^{\prime}>0
independent of
k
. If
\langle O_{x};O_{y}\rangle_{k}\leq A^{\ast}e^{-m^{\ast\prime}d_{k}(x,y)a_{k}}

for all gauge-invariant
O
, the OS spectral representation implies

E_{1}(k)\geq m^{\ast\prime}
, hence

\Delta_{k}\geq 1-e^{-m^{\ast\prime}a_{k}}
.
∎

In particular, by Osterwalder-Schrader positivity, this decay implies a nonzero mass gap in the physical state sector: the lowest mass (glueball) satisfies
m_{\mathrm{phys}}\geq m_{t}>0
.

Appendix 8
Gap monotonicity and step-scaling (Theorem C)

In this section a complete transfer-time-slicing formalism is derived for the reflection-positive, gauge-invariant lattice Yang-Mills measures produced at each renormalization scale. The construction yields a positive self-adjoint transfer operator
T_{k}
on the Osterwalder-Schrader (OS) Hilbert space
\mathcal{H}_{k}
at scale
k
, and an explicit coarse-graining map
V_{k}:\mathcal{H}_{k+1}\to\mathcal{H}_{k}
intertwining OS structures at consecutive scales. Let
T_{k}
and
T_{k+1}
be the OS-transfer operators at scales
k
and
k+1
,
and
V_{k}:H_{k+1}\to H_{k}
the isometric coarse-graining map. Then

T_{k+1}\ \preccurlyeq\ V_{k}^{*}\,T_{k}\,V_{k}\ +\ E_{k},

(8.1)

where
E_{k}\geq 0
and
\|E_{k}\|\leq\varepsilon_{k}
with
\sum_{k}\varepsilon_{k}<\infty
.
The block-spin relation of kernels yields

K_{k+1}=\mathbb{E}[K_{k}]+\Delta K_{k},

with
\Delta K_{k}\geq 0
controlled by the exponential locality of the spectral projector and the finite-range decomposition.
Schur’s test and OS positivity give
\|E_{k}\|\leq\varepsilon_{k}
.
The min-max principle for positive contractions then implies gap monotonicity with a summable defect (see Appendix (
14
)). The arguments rely only on reflection positivity
[
1
,
2
]
, the single-step transfer-kernel formalism for lattice gauge theories
[
4
]
, exponential locality of the smooth spectral projector through Combes-Thomas/Davies-Gaffney bounds
[
14
,
13
]
, and standard spectral theory
[
27
]
. Let
\lambda_{2}(T_{k})\in(0,1)
denote the second eigenvalue (counted with multiplicity) of the positive contraction
T_{k}
acting on the OS Hilbert space
\mathsf{H}_{k}
at mesh size
a_{k}
. We introduce the
contraction gap
and the
lattice energy
as

\Delta_{k}\;:=\;1-\lambda_{2}(T_{k})\in[0,1],\qquad E_{1,k}\;:=\;-\frac{1}{a_{k}}\log\lambda_{2}(T_{k})\in(0,\infty).

(8.2)

These are related by
E_{1,k}=-a_{k}^{-1}\log(1-\Delta_{k})
; in particular, for small
\Delta_{k}
one has
E_{1,k}\sim\Delta_{k}/a_{k}
.

The periodic hypercubic space-time lattice is

\Lambda_{k}\ =\ \bigl(a_{k}\,\mathbb{Z}/(Ta_{k}\mathbb{Z})\bigr)\ \times\ \prod_{i=1}^{3}\bigl(a_{k}\,\mathbb{Z}/(La_{k}\mathbb{Z})\bigr),

(8.3)

with discrete Euclidean time coordinate
x_{0}\in\{0,a_{k},\dots,(T-1)a_{k}\}
and spatial coordinate
\mathbf{x}\in(\mathbb{Z}/L\mathbb{Z})^{3}a_{k}
. Directed bonds are pairs
b=(x,\mu)
with
\mu\in\{0,1,2,3\}
, where
\mu=0
designates time-like bonds and
\mu=1,2,3
spatial bonds; reversing orientation gives
U_{(x+\hat{\mu},-\mu)}=U_{(x,\mu)}^{-1}
. The configuration space is the compact Lie group manifold

\mathcal{U}_{k}\ =\ \mathrm{SU}(N)^{\mathcal{B}_{k}},

(8.4)

equipped with the product Borel
\sigma
-algebra and product Haar probability measure
d\lambda
. The Wilson action is

S_{W}[U]\ =\ \beta\,\sum_{p}\Bigl(1-\frac{1}{N}\,\Re\mathrm{Tr}\,U_{p}\Bigr),\qquad\beta=\frac{2N}{g_{0}^{2}}.

(8.5)

At scale
k
we consider the probability measure

d\mu_{k}(U)\ =\ Z_{k}^{-1}\,e^{-S_{W}[U]}\,\bigl(\det M[A^{h}(U)]\bigr)\,\prod_{t}\,\mathcal{P}_{\sigma,k}\!\bigl(U|_{\Sigma_{t}}\bigr)\,d\lambda(U),

(8.6)

where
M[A^{h}(U)]
is the lattice Faddeev-Popov operator associated with the slice-wise Landau minimizer
A^{h}(U)
,
\Sigma_{t}=\{(t,\mathbf{x})\}
is a time slice, and
\mathcal{P}_{\sigma,k}
is the positive, exponentially local density induced by the smooth horizon projector
P_{\sigma,k}
on a slice. The measure
\mu_{k}
is invariant under unit time translation
\tau_{k}
by
a_{k}
and satisfies reflection positivity with respect to the time reflection
\theta_{k}:(x_{0},\mathbf{x})\mapsto(-x_{0},\mathbf{x})

[
4
]
. Writing
\Lambda_{k}^{+}=\{x\in\Lambda_{k}:x_{0}>0\}
,
\Pi_{k}=\{x_{0}=0\}
, and
\overline{\Lambda}_{k}^{+}=\Lambda_{k}^{+}\cup\Pi_{k}
, a bounded measurable functional
F:\mathcal{U}_{k}\to\mathbb{C}
is supported in
\Lambda_{k}^{+}
if it depends only on bonds with both endpoints in
\overline{\Lambda}_{k}^{+}
. The OS conjugation
\Theta_{k}
acts by

(\Theta_{k}F)(U)\ =\ \overline{F\!\bigl(\theta_{k}\cdot U\bigr)},\qquad(\theta_{k}\cdot U)(x,\mu)\ =\ \begin{cases}U(\theta_{k}x-\hat{0},0)^{-1},&\text{if }\mu=0,\ x\in\Pi_{k},\\
U(\theta_{k}x,\mu),&\text{otherwise},\end{cases}

(8.7)

the special case for time-like bonds crossing
\Pi_{k}
being the standard one ensuring positivity of the single-step kernel
[
4
]
. Reflection positivity states that

\langle F,F\rangle_{k}\ :=\ \int_{\mathcal{U}_{k}}(\Theta_{k}F)(U)\,F(U)\,d\mu_{k}(U)\ \geq\ 0

(8.8)

for all bounded
F
supported in
\Lambda_{k}^{+}
.

Let
\mathcal{D}_{k}
denote the vector space of bounded,
\Lambda_{k}^{+}
-supported functionals. The sesquilinear form (
8.8
) induces an inner product on the quotient
\mathcal{D}_{k}/\mathcal{N}_{k}
, where
\mathcal{N}_{k}=\{F\in\mathcal{D}_{k}:\langle F,F\rangle_{k}=0\}
. The completion is the OS Hilbert space
\mathcal{H}_{k}
, and the class of the constant functional is denoted
\Omega_{k}
. Time translation acts by
(\tau_{k}F)(U)=F(\tau_{k}^{-1}\!\cdot U)
,
(\tau_{k}^{-1}\!\cdot U)(x,\mu)=U(x-a_{k}\hat{0},\mu)
, and extends by continuity to a contraction on
\mathcal{H}_{k}
thanks to (
8.8
).

Proposition 8.1

(Transfer operator at scale
k
)
.

There exists a unique positive self-adjoint contraction
T_{k}
on
\mathcal{H}_{k}
such that for all
F,G\in\mathcal{D}_{k}
,

\langle F,T_{k}G\rangle_{k}\ =\ \int_{\mathcal{U}_{k}}(\Theta_{k}F)(U)\,G\!\bigl(\tau_{k}\!\cdot U\bigr)\,d\mu_{k}(U),\qquad T_{k}\Omega_{k}=\Omega_{k}.

(8.9)

Moreover
T_{k}
is the closure of the symmetric contraction induced by
\tau_{k}
on
\mathcal{D}_{k}/\mathcal{N}_{k}
.

Proof.

For
F,G\in\mathcal{D}_{k}
, the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality with (
8.8
) gives

\bigl|\langle F,\tau_{k}G\rangle_{k}\bigr|^{2}\ \leq\ \langle F,F\rangle_{k}\,\langle\tau_{k}G,\tau_{k}G\rangle_{k}\ =\ \langle F,F\rangle_{k}\,\langle G,G\rangle_{k},

(8.10)

so
\tau_{k}
defines a contraction on
\mathcal{D}_{k}/\mathcal{N}_{k}
, extending to a contraction on
\mathcal{H}_{k}
. Reflection invariance implies

\langle F,\tau_{k}G\rangle_{k}\ =\ \langle\tau_{k}F,G\rangle_{k},

(8.11)

hence
\tau_{k}
is symmetric on
\mathcal{D}_{k}/\mathcal{N}_{k}
. The Hellinger-Toeplitz theorem
[
27
, Thm. VIII.1]
implies that the closure
T_{k}
is self-adjoint and remains a contraction. The identity (
8.9
) is the defining OS relation and
T_{k}\Omega_{k}=\Omega_{k}
follows from
\tau_{k}\mathbf{1}=\mathbf{1}
. Positivity of
T_{k}
is immediate from
\langle F,T_{k}F\rangle_{k}=\int(\Theta_{k}F)F\circ\tau_{k}\,d\mu_{k}\geq 0
by (
8.8
).
∎

Let
e^{-\eta_{n}(T_{k})}
denote the eigenvalues of
T_{k}
in nonincreasing order, counted with multiplicity, with
e^{-\eta_{1}(T_{k})}=1
corresponding to
\Omega_{k}
. Define the spectral gap

\Delta_{k}\ :=\ 1-e^{-\eta_{2}(T_{k})}.

(8.12)

The OS spectral representation
[
2
,
7
]
represents time-separated two-point functions of gauge-invariant local observables as Laplace transforms of positive measures supported in
[\eta_{2}(T_{k}),\infty)
.

The renormalization step from scale
k
to
k+1
is described by a measurable, gauge-equivariant, reflection-compatible block map

\mathcal{B}_{k}\,:\,\mathcal{U}_{k}\ \longrightarrow\ \mathcal{U}_{k+1},

(8.13)

assigning to each coarse bond a nearest-neighbor projection in
\mathrm{SU}(N)
of the arithmetic mean of ordered products of fine links along a fixed family of paths inside the two adjacent fine blocks. The coarse measure
\mu_{k+1}
is the pushforward of
\mu_{k}
under
\mathcal{B}_{k}
with a reflection-compatible, positive insertion
\Theta_{k}(U)
built from
P_{\sigma,k}
on the internal time boundaries of blocks:

\int_{\mathcal{U}_{k+1}}F(\bar{U})\,d\mu_{k+1}(\bar{U})\ =\ \frac{1}{Z_{k}}\int_{\mathcal{U}_{k}}F\!\bigl(\mathcal{B}_{k}(U)\bigr)\,\Theta_{k}(U)\,d\mu_{k}(U),

(8.14)

for all bounded measurable
F
. Here
Z_{k}=\int\Theta_{k}\,d\mu_{k}\in(0,\infty)
. Define the coupling measure

d\pi_{k}(U,\bar{U})\ =\ \frac{1}{Z_{k}}\,\Theta_{k}(U)\,\delta_{\mathcal{B}_{k}(U)}(d\bar{U})\,d\mu_{k}(U),

(8.15)

whose marginals are
\mu_{k}
and
\mu_{k+1}
by (
8.14
).

For
f\in\mathcal{D}_{k+1}
supported in
\Lambda_{k+1}^{+}
define
\mathcal{V}_{k}f:\mathcal{U}_{k}\to\mathbb{C}
by

(\mathcal{V}_{k}f)(U)\ =\ f\!\bigl(\mathcal{B}_{k}(U)\bigr).

(8.16)

This map descends to a bounded linear map
V_{k}:\mathcal{H}_{k+1}\to\mathcal{H}_{k}
.

Lemma 8.2

(Contractivity of
V_{k}
)
.

For all
f\in\mathcal{D}_{k+1}
,

\|V_{k}f\|_{\mathcal{H}_{k}}^{2}\ =\ \int(\Theta_{k}\mathcal{V}_{k}f)\,\mathcal{V}_{k}f\,d\mu_{k}\ \leq\ Z_{k}\,\|f\|_{\mathcal{H}_{k+1}}^{2}.

(8.17)

Proof.

Using (
8.14
) with
F(\bar{U})=(\Theta_{k+1}f)(\bar{U})\,f(\bar{U})
and the reflection invariance of
\Theta_{k}
,

\int(\Theta_{k}\mathcal{V}_{k}f)\,\mathcal{V}_{k}f\,d\mu_{k}\ =\ Z_{k}\,\int(\Theta_{k+1}f)\,f\,d\mu_{k+1}\ =\ Z_{k}\,\|f\|_{\mathcal{H}_{k+1}}^{2}.

(8.18)

∎

Let
\mathcal{C}_{k}=\mathrm{SU}(N)^{\text{spatial bonds at a fixed time}}
denote the slice configuration space and
d\nu_{k}
the marginal of
\mu_{k}
on a time slice. There exists a bounded positive kernel
K_{k}:\mathcal{C}_{k}\times\mathcal{C}_{k}\to[0,\infty)
such that for all
F,G
depending on a single slice,

\int_{\mathcal{U}_{k}}F\!\bigl(U|_{\Sigma_{0}}\bigr)\,G\!\bigl(U|_{\Sigma_{a_{k}}}\bigr)\,d\mu_{k}(U)\ =\ \int_{\mathcal{C}_{k}\times\mathcal{C}_{k}}F(U_{0})\,K_{k}(U_{0},U_{1})\,G(U_{1})\,d\nu_{k}(U_{0})\,d\nu_{k}(U_{1}),

(8.19)

and the transfer operator
T_{k}
is the
L^{2}(d\nu_{k})
operator induced by
K_{k}
, restricted to
\mathcal{H}_{k}

[
4
]
. To localize the coupling across a reflection-invariant time collar, define for
w\in\mathbb{N}
the collar

\mathsf{Col}_{w}^{(k)}\ =\ \{x\in\Lambda_{k}\,:\,-w\,a_{k}\leq x_{0}\leq w\,a_{k}\},

(8.20)

and the collar insertion

\Xi_{k,w}(U)\ =\ \prod_{t=-wa_{k}}^{wa_{k}}\mathcal{P}_{\sigma,k}\!\bigl(U|_{\Sigma_{t}}\bigr).

(8.21)

The function
\Xi_{k,w}
is positive, reflection invariant, exponentially local, and bounded above and below by strictly positive constants independent of the spatial volume.

Lemma 8.3

(Uniform bounds for the collar insertion)
.

Fix
\sigma>0
and
w\in\mathbb{N}
. There exist constants
0<c_{\sigma}\leq C_{\sigma}<\infty
,
independent of the spatial volume and of
k
, such that

c_{\sigma}^{\,2w+1}\;\leq\;\Xi_{k,w}(U)\;\leq\;C_{\sigma}^{\,2w+1}\qquad\text{for all configurations }U

(8.22)

In particular,
\Xi_{k,w}
is strictly positive and reflection invariant.

Proof.

On each slice
t
, the factor
P_{\sigma,k}(U|_{\Sigma_{t}})
is a positive scalar functional.
In the heat-kernel regime (case (A) above), write

P_{\sigma,k}=\int_{0}^{\infty}e^{-s\Delta_{A^{h}}^{(k)}(t)}\,d\nu_{\sigma}(s)
and note that

0\leq e^{-s\Delta}\leq I
implies
0\leq P_{\sigma,k}\leq\nu_{\sigma}((0,\infty))=:C_{\sigma}
and,
by positivity and normalization at
0
. For the normalized trace,
\frac{1}{\dim(\mathrm{ad})|\Lambda_{t}|}\mathrm{Tr}(e^{-s\Delta_{A^{h}}(t)})\geq e^{-s\,\lambda_{\max}}
, where
\lambda_{\max}
is the (background-uniform) spectral radius
of the slice Laplacian on a graph of fixed degree. Hence
K_{\sigma}[U|t]\geq\int_{0}^{\infty}e^{-s\,\lambda_{\max}}\,d\nu_{\sigma}(s)=:c_{\sigma}>0
, uniformly in the volume.
In the Helffer-Sjöstrand regime (case (B)), for the choices

p_{\sigma}=\operatorname{Tr}P_{\sigma}
or
p_{\sigma}=\exp(-\langle\varphi,(I-P_{\sigma})\varphi\rangle)
,
we have
0<p_{\sigma}\leq\dim(\mathcal{H}_{t})
and
p_{\sigma}\geq e^{-\|\varphi\|^{2}}>0
, with constants
depending only on
\sigma
and the fixed test field. Multiplying over the
(2w+1)
slices in the
collar yields the stated bounds. Reflection invariance is immediate from slice-wise reflection
covariance of
P_{\sigma,k}
.
∎

Lemma 8.4

(Approximate factorization across a collar)
.

There exist constants
c,\gamma>0
, independent of
k
and
w
, such that for any bounded
F_{-}
supported in
\Lambda_{k}^{-}\setminus\mathsf{Col}_{w}^{(k)}
and
F_{+}
supported in
\Lambda_{k}^{+}\setminus\mathsf{Col}_{w}^{(k)}
,

\Bigl|\ \int(\Theta_{k}F_{+})\,F_{-}\ \Xi_{k,w}\,d\mu_{k}\ -\ \Bigl(\int(\Theta_{k}F_{+})\,\Xi_{k,w}\,d\mu_{k}\Bigr)\ \Bigl(\int F_{-}\,\Xi_{k,w}\,d\mu_{k}\Bigr)\ \Bigr|\ \leq\ c\,e^{-\gamma w}\,\|F_{+}\|_{\infty}\,\|F_{-}\|_{\infty}.

(8.23)

Proof.

Let
\mu_{k}^{(w)}
be the probability measure with density proportional to
\Xi_{k,w}
with respect to
\mu_{k}
. Since
\Xi_{k,w}
is a product of slice-local positive factors and reflection invariant,
\mu_{k}^{(w)}
retains reflection positivity and the nearest-neighbor coupling in time. The exponential locality of
\mathcal{P}_{\sigma,k}
follows from its heat-kernel representation and Combes-Thomas/Davies-Gaffney bounds
[
14
,
13
]
, and implies that the influence of boundary conditions across
\mathsf{Col}_{w}^{(k)}
on observables supported at a distance at least
wa_{k}
decays exponentially in
w
. The constants in the off-diagonal heat-kernel (and resolvent) bounds are uniform in the background because the covariant differences enter only through unitary parallel transports; hence the Dirichlet form is background-independent up to unitary conjugation. More precisely, by the persistence of exponential clustering established at scale
k
for connected gauge-invariant correlators with decay rate
m_{*}>0
(Section 7), one has for the truncated correlation under
\mu_{k}^{(w)}

\bigl|\langle(\Theta_{k}F_{+});F_{-}\rangle_{\mu_{k}^{(w)}}\bigr|\ \leq\ C\,e^{-m_{*}wa_{k}}\,\|F_{+}\|_{\infty}\,\|F_{-}\|_{\infty}.

(8.24)

Since
\Xi_{k,w}
is bounded above and below by positive constants independent of
k,w
, the truncated correlation bound (
8.24
) implies (
8.23
) with
\gamma=m_{*}a_{k}
up to a change of constants.
∎

Let
f\in\mathcal{D}_{k+1}
be supported in
\Lambda_{k+1}^{+}
and set
F=\mathcal{V}_{k}f
. By Proposition
8.1
at scale
k+1
and the pushforward identity (
8.14
),

\langle f,T_{k+1}f\rangle_{\mathcal{H}_{k+1}}\ =\ \frac{1}{Z_{k}}\ \int(\Theta_{k}F)(U)\,F\!\bigl(\tau_{k}\!\cdot U\bigr)\,\Theta_{k}(U)\,d\mu_{k}(U).

(8.25)

Fix
w\in\mathbb{N}
. Multiplying and dividing by
\Xi_{k,w}
and using Lemma
8.4
with
F_{+}=F\circ\tau_{k}
,
F_{-}=F
, one obtains

\langle f,T_{k+1}f\rangle_{\mathcal{H}_{k+1}}\ \leq\ \frac{1}{Z_{k}}\ \int(\Theta_{k}F)\,F\circ\tau_{k}\ \Xi_{k,w}\,d\mu_{k}\ +\ \varepsilon_{k}(w)\,\|f\|_{\mathcal{H}_{k+1}}^{2},

(8.26)

with
\varepsilon_{k}(w)\leq Ce^{-\gamma w}
. Define the positive bounded operator
B_{k,w}:\mathcal{H}_{k}\to\mathcal{H}_{k}
by

\langle G,B_{k,w}H\rangle_{\mathcal{H}_{k}}\ :=\ \frac{1}{Z_{k}}\ \int(\Theta_{k}G)\,H\ \Xi_{k,w}\,d\mu_{k},\qquad G,H\in\mathcal{D}_{k}.

(8.27)

Then, using (
8.9
) at scale
k
,

\frac{1}{Z_{k}}\ \int(\Theta_{k}F)\,F\circ\tau_{k}\ \Xi_{k,w}\,d\mu_{k}\ =\ \langle V_{k}f,\,B_{k,w}^{1/2}\,T_{k}\,B_{k,w}^{1/2}\,V_{k}f\rangle_{\mathcal{H}_{k}}.

(8.28)

Since
\Xi_{k,w}
is bounded and reflection invariant,
B_{k,w}
is positive and satisfies
\|B_{k,w}-I\|\leq Ce^{-\gamma w}
. Writing
B_{k,w}^{1/2}=I+R_{k,w}
with
\|R_{k,w}\|\leq Ce^{-\gamma w}
and noting that
0\preccurlyeq T_{k}\preccurlyeq I
, one has the operator inequality

B_{k,w}^{1/2}\,T_{k}\,B_{k,w}^{1/2}\ \preccurlyeq\ T_{k}\ +\ Ce^{-\gamma w}\,I.

(8.29)

Combining (
8.26
), (
8.28
), and (
8.29
) yields, for all
f\in\mathcal{D}_{k+1}
,

\langle f,T_{k+1}f\rangle_{\mathcal{H}_{k+1}}\ \leq\ \langle f,\ V_{k}^{*}T_{k}V_{k}f\rangle_{\mathcal{H}_{k+1}}\ +\ C^{\prime}e^{-\gamma w}\,\|f\|_{\mathcal{H}_{k+1}}^{2}.

(8.30)

By density this holds for all
f\in\mathcal{H}_{k+1}
.

Lemma 8.5

(Quantitative collar multiplier bound)
.

Fix
\sigma>0
and
w\in\mathbb{N}
. With
B_{k,w}
defined by Eq.(
8.27
), there exist
constants
c_{\sigma},C_{\sigma}>0
(independent of the spatial volume and
k
) such that

c_{\sigma}^{\,2w+1}I\,\preceq\,B_{k,w}\,\preceq\,C_{\sigma}^{\,2w+1}I
and

\bigl\|\,B_{k,w}-I\,\bigr\|\;\leq\;C\,e^{-\gamma w}.

(8.31)

Consequently, via the holomorphic functional calculus on positive operators,

B_{k,w}^{1/2}=I+R_{k,w}\qquad\text{with}\qquad\|R_{k,w}\|\;\leq\;C^{\prime}e^{-\gamma w}.

(8.32)

Proof.

By (8.22) each slice factor in
\Xi_{k,w}
is bounded between
c_{\sigma}
and
C_{\sigma}
,
hence the product over
(2w+1)
slices satisfies
c_{\sigma}^{\,2w+1}\leq\Xi_{k,w}\leq C_{\sigma}^{\,2w+1}
. Since
B_{k,w}
is the OS Gram operator with weight
\Xi_{k,w}
, the
same spectral bounds hold on
B_{k,w}
. The exponential locality of
P_{\sigma,k}
and the
clustering bound from Theorem 7.4 imply that the off-diagonal (in time) corrections induced by

\Xi_{k,w}
across the collar are
O(e^{-\gamma w})
, which yields
\|B_{k,w}-I\|\leq Ce^{-\gamma w}
.
Analyticity of
z\mapsto z^{1/2}
on a neighborhood of
[c_{\sigma}^{2w+1},C_{\sigma}^{2w+1}]

transfers this estimate to
B_{k,w}^{1/2}
, giving the stated bound on
R_{k,w}
.
∎

Proposition 8.6

(Interlacing with summable error)
.

There exists
c>0
and a summable sequence
\varepsilon_{k}>0
such that

T_{k+1}\ \preccurlyeq\ V_{k}^{*}\,T_{k}\,V_{k}\ +\ E_{k},\qquad\|E_{k}\|\ \leq\ \varepsilon_{k},\qquad E_{k}\ \succeq\ 0.

(8.33)

Proof.

Choose
w(k)=\lfloor c\,b^{k}\rfloor
with
c>0
fixed; then
e^{-\gamma w(k)}
is superexponentially small and summable in
k
. Define
E_{k}=C^{\prime}e^{-\gamma w(k)}I_{\mathcal{H}_{k+1}}
. Inequality (
8.33
) is the operator form of (
8.30
).
∎

Let
P_{k}
denote the orthogonal projection onto
\Omega_{k}^{\perp}
. We write
\eta_{2}(T):=-\log\lambda_{2}(T)
for the second spectral exponent of a positive
contraction
T
, so that
\lambda_{2}(T)=e^{-\eta_{2}(T)}
and
\Delta(T)=1-\lambda_{2}(T)
. For a positive contraction
A
with normalized vacuum, the variational characterization of the second spectral exponent is

e^{-\eta_{2}(A)}\;=\;\sup\{\,\langle\psi,A\psi\rangle:\psi\in\mathrm{Dom}(A),\ \|\psi\|=1,\ \langle\psi,\Omega\rangle=0\,\}.

(8.34)

see
[
27
, Sec. XIII.1]
.

Theorem 8.7

(Gap monotonicity with summable defect)
.

There exists a summable sequence
(\varepsilon_{k})_{k\geq 0}
such that

\Delta_{k+1}\ \geq\ \Delta_{k}\ -\ \varepsilon_{k}\qquad\text{for all }k\geq 0.

(8.35)

Proof.

Let
S=S_{-}\cup S_{0}\cup S_{+}
be the decomposition of the time slab into left, collar, and right
regions. By Lemma 8.4 (approximate factorization across a collar), for any gauge-invariant local
functional
F
supported in
S_{-}\cup S_{+}
one has

\Big|\langle F\rangle_{k}-\langle F_{-}\rangle_{k}\,\langle F_{+}\rangle_{k}\Big|\;\leq\;C\,e^{-\gamma\,\mathrm{dist}(S_{-},S_{+})},

(8.36)

where
\gamma>0
is the uniform clustering rate at scale
k
from Theorem 7.4. By construction of
the single-RG-step coarse-graining (Sec. 8), (
8.36
) implies the operator-norm
bound
