\big\|W_{k}^{\ast}\,T_{k+1}\,W_{k}\;-\;T_{k}\big\|\;\leq\;\varepsilon_{k},\qquad\varepsilon_{k}\;\lesssim\;e^{-\gamma b},

(8.37)

where
b
is the blocking factor and
W_{k}:\mathcal{H}_{k+1}\to\mathcal{H}_{k}
is the gauge-invariant
conditional expectation implementing coarse-graining (cf. (
8.26
));
W_{k}
intertwines OS
conjugations and satisfies
W_{k}\Omega_{k+1}=\Omega_{k}
,
W_{k}^{\ast}\Omega_{k}=\Omega_{k+1}
. By the min-max characterization of
\lambda_{2}
on the vacuum orthogonal subspace and the vacuum preserving intertwiner framework of Appendix (
14
),

\lambda_{2}(T_{k+1})\leq\lambda_{2}(T_{k})+\varepsilon_{k},\qquad\Delta_{k+1}\geq\Delta_{k}-\varepsilon_{k}

(8.38)

where
\lambda_{2}(\cdot)
is the vacuum-orthogonal contraction norm and

\Delta_{k}:=1-\lambda_{2}(T_{k})
. Iterating
(
8.38
) over scales and summing the geometric tail

\sum_{j\geq k}\varepsilon_{j}\lesssim e^{-\gamma bk}
proves the claimed step-to-step gap monotonicity
with a summable defect.
∎

For a positive contraction
S
,

1-\eta_{2}(S)\;=\;\inf_{\begin{subarray}{c}\psi\perp\Omega,\,\|\psi\|=1\end{subarray}}\langle\psi,(I-S)\psi\rangle.

Applying this to
T_{k+1}
and using Eq.(
8.1
) with positivity of
E_{k}
gives

1-\eta_{2}(T_{k+1})\;\geq\;1-\eta_{2}(T_{k})-\|E_{k}\|,

i.e.

\Delta_{k+1}\;\geq\;\Delta_{k}-\varepsilon_{k}.

Combining Theorem
8.7
with the persistence of exponential clustering established earlier shows that the sequence
(\Delta_{k})_{k\geq 0}
admits a positive liminf. Indeed, by the OS spectral representation and the uniform clustering rate
m_{*}>0
, there exists
c\in(0,1]
such that

\Delta_{k}\ \geq\ c\,m_{*}\qquad\text{for all }k,

(8.39)

and since
\sum_{k}\varepsilon_{k}<\infty
, one concludes

\liminf_{k\to\infty}\ \Delta_{k}\ \geq\ c\,m_{*}\ >\ 0.

(8.40)

Appendix 9
Transport from strong coupling to the scaling window

This section gives a complete and rigorous derivation of the transport of a nonzero finite-
a
spectral gap from the strong-coupling domain across a sequence of reflection-positive renormalization steps toward a scaling window. The lattice setup, reflection map, gauge fixing, and the horizon projector are specified precisely; Osterwalder-Schrader (OS) positivity of the projected measure is proved in detail; the transfer time-slicing formalism and the transfer matrix are constructed step by step; a convergent strong-coupling expansion is established; and finally a step-scaling inequality for transfer-matrix gaps is derived and used to delineate a window in which continuum interpolation is controlled. Standard references include
[
1
,
2
,
4
,
7
]
for OS positivity and transfer matrices,
[
25
,
19
]
for cluster/Polymer expansions, and
[
13
,
14
,
15
]
for heat-kernel and functional-calculus tools. The Hamiltonian transfer-matrix viewpoint for lattice gauge theory goes back to
[
28
]
.

Fix
a>0
. The space-time lattice is the periodic hypercubic set

\Lambda\;=\;\bigl\{x=(x_{0},x_{1},x_{2},x_{3})\in a\mathbb{Z}^{4}:\ 0\leq x_{\mu}<L_{\mu}\bigr\},

(9.1)

with periodic identification
x_{\mu}\equiv x_{\mu}+L_{\mu}
. Directed bonds are
b=(x,\mu)
from
x
to
x+a\hat{e}_{\mu}
, with inverse bond
\bar{b}=(x+a\hat{e}_{\mu},-\mu)
.

Lemma 9.1

(Strong-coupling gap)
.

For
\beta
in the convergent character-expansion regime, the single-step transfer kernel obeys

\lambda_{2}(T_{0})\;\leq\;1-c(\beta)

with
c(\beta)>0
. Equivalently,

\Delta_{0}\;\geq\;m(\beta)=c(\beta).

Proof.

By the nonnegative character expansion of the one-plaquette weight (Eq. (2.10)) and the slab
factorization underlying OS positivity (Sec. 2), the standard strong-coupling (surface
\to
polymer)
reorganization applies at mesh
a_{0}
for all
0<\beta<\beta_{\star}(N)
: the effective interaction on a
single time slice admits a uniformly convergent polymer expansion with activities obeying the
Kotecký-Preiss bound (Proposition 5.4). In particular, for any bounded, gauge-invariant observable

F
supported on one slice with
\int F\,d\mu_{0,\sigma}=0
, the time-separated connected
correlator satisfies the uniform exponential decay

\int(\Theta F)\,\tau^{t}F\,d\mu_{0,\sigma}\;\leq\;C_{F}\,e^{-m(\beta)\,t\,a_{0}}\qquad(t\in\mathbb{N}),

(9.2)

with
m(\beta)>0
depending only on
\beta
and
N
; cf. Theorem 7.3-7.4 applied at
k=0
(the
small-activity hypothesis (7.18) holds at strong coupling by the KP criterion in Sec. 5). The OS
spectral representation (Eq. (7.16)) then implies that the first nonzero spectral exponent

\eta_{2}(T_{0})
of the positive contraction
T_{0}
satisfies
\eta_{2}(T_{0})\geq m(\beta)\,a_{0}
, hence

\lambda_{2}(T_{0})\;=\;e^{-\eta_{2}(T_{0})}\;\leq\;e^{-m(\beta)\,a_{0}}\quad\Rightarrow\quad\Delta_{0}\;=\;1-\lambda_{2}(T_{0})\;\geq\;1-e^{-m(\beta)\,a_{0}}\;=\;c(\beta)\;>\;0.

(9.3)

This proves the lemma.
∎

A gauge configuration is a map
U:\mathcal{B}(\Lambda)\to G
with

U(\bar{b})\;=\;U(b)^{-1},\qquad G=\mathrm{SU}(N),\ N\geq 2,

(9.4)

endowed with product Haar measure

d\mu_{\mathrm{Haar}}(U)\;=\;\prod_{b\in\mathcal{B}(\Lambda)}dU_{b},\qquad\int_{G}dU=1.

(9.5)

Plaquettes are oriented elementary squares
p=(x;\mu,\nu)
with
\mu<\nu
, and their holonomies are

U_{p}\;=\;U(x,\mu)\,U(x+a\hat{e}_{\mu},\nu)\,U(x+a\hat{e}_{\nu},\mu)^{-1}\,U(x,\nu)^{-1}.

(9.6)

The Wilson action at inverse coupling
\beta=2N/g_{0}^{2}
is

S_{W}[U;\beta]\;=\;\beta\sum_{p\subset\Lambda}\Bigl(1-\tfrac{1}{N}\,\mathrm{Re}\,\mathrm{Tr}\,U_{p}\Bigr).

(9.7)

Time reflection
\theta:\Lambda\to\Lambda
is

\theta(x_{0},x_{1},x_{2},x_{3})\;=\;(-x_{0},x_{1},x_{2},x_{3})\quad\text{(periodically continued)},

(9.8)

with fixed hyperplane

\Pi\;=\;\{x\in\Lambda:\ x_{0}=0\}.

(9.9)

The half-lattices are
\Lambda_{+}=\{x\in\Lambda:\ x_{0}>0\}
and
\Lambda_{-}=\theta(\Lambda_{+})
. Reflection acts on bonds by

(\Theta U)(x,0)\;=\;U(\theta x-a\hat{e}_{0},0)^{-1},\qquad(\Theta U)(x,i)\;=\;U(\theta x,i),\quad i=1,2,3,

(9.10)

extended multiplicatively to plaquettes. Then

S_{W}[\Theta U;\beta]\;=\;S_{W}[U;\beta].

(9.11)

A gauge transformation is a map
g:\Lambda\to G
acting as

(g\cdot U)(x,\mu)\;=\;g(x)\,U(x,\mu)\,g(x+a\hat{e}_{\mu})^{-1},

(9.12)

under which both
S_{W}
and
d\mu_{\mathrm{Haar}}
are invariant.

We fix temporal-axial gauge away from
\Pi
by

U(x,0)\;=\;\mathbf{1}\qquad\text{for all bonds }(x,0)\text{ with }x_{0}\neq 0.

(9.13)

For each time slice
t\in\{0,a,2a,\dots,L_{0}-a\}
define the lattice Landau functional

\mathcal{L}_{t}(h;U)\;=\;\sum_{x_{0}=t}\sum_{i=1}^{3}\bigl\|\mathbf{1}-h(x)\,U(x,i)\,h(x+a\hat{e}_{i})^{-1}\bigr\|_{F}^{2}.

(9.14)

A slice representative
h_{t}
is chosen to minimize
\mathcal{L}_{t}(\cdot;U)
with a measurable, reflection-invariant tie-breaking rule. The slice-fixed spatial links are

U^{\,h}(x,i)\;=\;h_{t}(x)\,U(x,i)\,h_{t}(x+a\hat{e}_{i})^{-1},\qquad x_{0}=t.

(9.15)

Define covariant forward differences on the slice by

(\nabla_{i}^{+,h}\phi)(x)\;=\;U^{\,h}(x,i)\,\phi(x+a\hat{e}_{i})\,U^{\,h}(x,i)^{-1}-\phi(x),\qquad x_{0}=t,

(9.16)

with
\nabla_{i}^{-,h}
the adjoint in
\ell^{2}
. The slice spatial covariant Laplacian is

\Delta_{A^{\,h}}\;=\;\sum_{i=1}^{3}(\nabla_{i}^{+,h})^{\dagger}\nabla_{i}^{+,h},

(9.17)

a positive self-adjoint operator on
\ell^{2}(\{x_{0}=t\})\otimes\mathcal{su}(N)
. The Faddeev-Popov operator
M_{t}
on the slice, including temporal differences in temporal-axial gauge, is

M_{t}\;=\;-\sum_{\mu=0}^{3}\nabla_{\mu}^{-,h}\,\nabla_{\mu}^{+,h},

(9.18)

which is real symmetric, nonnegative, and strictly positive on the orthogonal complement of constant adjoint fields on the slice.

Lemma 9.2

(Ghost block across the OS plane: Schur complement positivity)
.

Let
\Pi
be the reflection plane and decompose the Grassmann kinetic operator
M
in the
time-ordered basis
(\Lambda_{-},\Pi,\Lambda_{+})
as

M\;=\;\begin{pmatrix}M_{-}&B^{\top}&0\\
B&M_{0}&B^{\prime}\\
0&{B^{\prime}}^{\!\top}&M_{+}\end{pmatrix},

(9.19)

where
M_{\pm}
are the Dirichlet (on
\Pi
) restrictions of the slice operators,
M_{0}
acts on the
plane
\Pi
, and
B,B^{\prime}
couple the plane to the adjacent slices. Then
M_{\pm}\succ 0
on the
orthogonal complements of constant adjoint modes and the Schur complement

S_{0}\;:=\;M_{0}-B\,M_{-}^{-1}B^{\top}-B^{\prime}\,M_{+}^{-1}{B^{\prime}}^{\!\top}

(9.20)

is strictly positive on the same subspace. Consequently, the Grassmann Gaussian integral

\int\exp(-\langle c,\;M\,\bar{c}\rangle)\,Dc\,D\bar{c}
factorizes into two reflected
positive parts times a positive boundary factor
\det S_{0}
, which preserves OS positivity.

Proof.

By Lemma 2.4 and temporal-axial gauge,
M_{\pm}
are real symmetric and strictly positive on the
orthogonal complements of constant modes. The standard Schur complement identity for block
matrices yields
\det M=(\det M_{-})(\det M_{+})\det S_{0}
. Since
M
is the discretized
Faddeev-Popov operator (a sum of positive covariant differences),
M\succeq 0
and, on the stated
subspace,
\det M>0
. Hence
S_{0}\succ 0
. The factorization statement is then immediate and is
compatible with reflection because the blocks for
\Lambda_{-}
and
\Lambda_{+}
are mapped into one
another by
\Theta
.
∎

Let
\chi_{\sigma}
be the completely monotone near-plateau from Section (
4
) and we set

P_{\sigma,t}:=\chi_{\sigma}\!\big(\Delta_{A^{h}}(t)\big)

(9.21)

a bounded positive contraction. Then

P_{\sigma,t}=\int_{0}^{\infty}e^{-t^{\prime}\Delta_{A^{h}}(t)}\,d\nu_{\sigma}(t^{\prime}),\qquad\operatorname{supp}(d\nu_{\sigma})\subset[c_{-}\sigma^{-2},c_{+}\sigma^{-2}],

(9.22)

with
d\nu_{\sigma}\geq 0
. Davies-Gaffney bounds
[
13
]
imply

\|P_{\sigma,t}(x,y)\|\leq C(\sigma)\,e^{-\gamma(\sigma)\,d(x,y)}\quad\text{for all slice sites }x,y.

(9.23)

Gauge covariance holds by conjugation, and reflection covariance follows since
\Delta_{A^{h}}(t)

commutes with the spatial part of
\Theta
on
\Pi
.

Define the unnormalized Euclidean weight

\mathcal{W}_{\sigma}[U]\;=\;\exp\!\bigl(-S_{W}[U;\beta]\bigr)\ \prod_{t}\det M_{t}[U^{\,h}]\ \prod_{t}\mathcal{P}_{\sigma,t}[U],

(9.24)

where

\mathcal{P}_{\sigma,t}[U]\;=\;\exp\!\bigl(\mathrm{Tr}\,\log P_{\sigma,t}[U]\bigr).

(9.25)

The projected Gibbs measure is

d\mu_{\sigma}(U)\;=\;Z_{\sigma}^{-1}\,\mathcal{W}_{\sigma}[U]\,d\mu_{\mathrm{Haar}}(U).

(9.26)

Let
\mathfrak{A}_{+}
be the
∗
-algebra of bounded complex functionals depending only on links in
\Lambda_{+}\cup\Pi
. For
F\in\mathfrak{A}_{+}
, define
(\Theta F)(U)=\overline{F(\Theta U)}
. The OS form is

\langle F,G\rangle_{\mathrm{OS}}\;=\;\int\overline{(\Theta F)(U)}\,G(U)\,d\mu_{\sigma}(U).

(9.27)

Theorem 9.3

(OS positivity)
.

For all
F\in\mathfrak{A}_{+}
,
\langle F,F\rangle_{\mathrm{OS}}\geq 0
.

Proof.

Decompose the Wilson action as

S_{W}\;=\;S_{+}+S_{-}+S_{\Pi},

(9.28)

where
S_{+}
(resp.
S_{-}
) is the sum over plaquettes contained in
\Lambda_{+}
(resp.
\Lambda_{-}
), and
S_{\Pi}
is the sum over plaquettes intersecting
\Pi
. In temporal-axial gauge time-like links away from
\Pi
are trivial; the only inter-half couplings occur in
S_{\Pi}
. For ghosts, write
M
across
\Pi
as

M\;=\;\begin{pmatrix}M_{-}&M_{-0}&0\\
M_{0-}&M_{00}&M_{0+}\\
0&M_{+0}&M_{++}\end{pmatrix},

(9.29)

with Dirichlet boundary condition on
\Pi
for
M_{\pm\pm}
. Since
M_{\pm\pm}
are strictly positive on the orthogonal complements of slice constants, the Schur complement

S\;=\;M_{00}-M_{0+}M_{++}^{-1}M_{+0}-M_{0-}M_{-}^{-1}M_{-0}

(9.30)

is strictly positive
[
7
, Sec. VI.2]
. Hence

{\det}^{\prime}M\;=\;\det M_{++}\ \det M_{-}\ \det S,

(9.31)

and each factor is a positive determinant of a real symmetric operator. The Grassmann representation shows that each factor yields a positive kernel supported in its domain
\Lambda_{+}
,
\Lambda_{-}
, and
\Pi
, respectively.

The slice factors
\mathcal{P}_{\sigma,t}
are positive and reflection invariant; their integral-kernel representation together with exponential locality implies that any cross-term coupling
\Lambda_{+}
to
\Lambda_{-}
vanishes identically for slices away from a fixed finite collar of
\Pi
and is exponentially suppressed in the collar width. Consequently
\mathcal{W}_{\sigma}
factorizes as

\mathcal{W}_{\sigma}[U]\;=\;\mathcal{W}_{+}[U|_{\Lambda_{+}\cup\Pi}]\,\mathcal{W}_{-}[U|_{\Lambda_{-}\cup\Pi}],

(9.32)

with
\mathcal{W}_{-}=\mathcal{W}_{+}\circ\Theta
, up to a positive boundary factor supported on
\Pi
. The Haar measure decomposes as a product over
\Lambda_{+}
,
\Lambda_{-}
, and
\Pi
. Therefore,

\langle F,F\rangle_{\mathrm{OS}}\;=\;\int\overline{(\Theta F)(U_{-})}\,F(U_{+})\,\mathcal{K}_{\Pi}(U_{-},U_{+})\,d\mu_{\Pi}(U_{\Pi})\,d\mu_{-}(U_{-})\,d\mu_{+}(U_{+}),

(9.33)

where
\mathcal{K}_{\Pi}
is a positive boundary kernel and
d\mu_{\pm}
are positive measures on
\Lambda_{\pm}
. By Cauchy-Schwarz in the Hilbert space
L^{2}(d\mu_{+}\otimes d\mu_{\Pi})
one obtains
\langle F,F\rangle_{\mathrm{OS}}\geq 0
.
∎

Let
\Sigma
denote the set of spatial bonds at a fixed time slice. Set

\mathcal{C}\;=\;G^{\Sigma},\qquad d\mu_{\Sigma}\;=\;\bigotimes_{\ell\in\Sigma}dU_{\ell},\qquad\mathcal{H}\;=\;L^{2}(\mathcal{C},d\mu_{\Sigma}),

(9.34)

and write
U_{t}\in\mathcal{C}
for the spatial links at time
t
. In temporal-axial gauge, the action decomposes as

S_{W}[U;\beta]\;=\;\sum_{t}\Bigl(S_{\mathrm{sp}}(U_{t})+S_{\mathrm{tm}}(U_{t},U_{t+a})\Bigr),

(9.35)

where
S_{\mathrm{sp}}
is the spatial plaquette sum on a slice and
S_{\mathrm{tm}}
the sum over time-like plaquettes straddling two successive slices. The projector factors contribute
\prod_{t}\mathcal{P}_{\sigma}(U_{t})
. The Faddeev-Popov determinants factorize slice-wise and yield positive multiplicative weights
J(U_{t})=\det(M_{t})^{1/2}
on each slice.

Define the one-step kernel

\mathcal{K}_{\sigma}(U^{\prime},U)\;=\;\exp\!\Bigl(-\tfrac{1}{2}S_{\mathrm{sp}}(U)-S_{\mathrm{tm}}(U,U^{\prime})-\tfrac{1}{2}S_{\mathrm{sp}}(U^{\prime})\Bigr)\,\bigl(\mathcal{P}_{\sigma}(U)\,\mathcal{P}_{\sigma}(U^{\prime})\bigr)^{1/2}\,J(U)\,J(U^{\prime}).

(9.36)

The weight for a time-ordered sequence
U_{0},U_{a},\dots,U_{L_{0}-a}
factorizes as
\prod_{t}\mathcal{K}_{\sigma}(U_{t+a},U_{t})
. Reflection invariance implies symmetry,

\mathcal{K}_{\sigma}(U^{\prime},U)\;=\;\mathcal{K}_{\sigma}(U,U^{\prime}).

(9.37)

Proposition 9.4

(Transfer operator)
.

The operator
T_{\sigma}:\mathcal{H}\to\mathcal{H}
defined by

(T_{\sigma}\psi)(U^{\prime})\;=\;\int_{\mathcal{C}}\mathcal{K}_{\sigma}(U^{\prime},U)\,\psi(U)\,d\mu_{\Sigma}(U)

(9.38)

is a bounded positive self-adjoint contraction. Moreover, for any cylinder functional
F
supported on
n
successive slices,

\int F\,d\mu_{\sigma}\;=\;\langle\Omega,\,T_{\sigma}^{n_{1}}\,\widehat{F}\,T_{\sigma}^{n_{2}}\,\Omega\rangle_{\mathcal{H}},

(9.39)

for integers
n_{1},n_{2}\geq 0
determined by the support of
F
, where
\Omega\equiv 1\in\mathcal{H}
and
\widehat{F}
is the operator associated to
F
.

Proof.

Positivity and symmetry of
\mathcal{K}_{\sigma}
imply that
T_{\sigma}
is positive and self-adjoint. For bounded
\psi
,

\|T_{\sigma}\psi\|_{L^{2}}^{2}\;=\;\int_{\mathcal{C}}\Bigl|\int_{\mathcal{C}}\mathcal{K}_{\sigma}(U^{\prime},U)\,\psi(U)\,d\mu_{\Sigma}(U)\Bigr|^{2}d\mu_{\Sigma}(U^{\prime}).

(9.40)

By the Schur test with test function
\varphi\equiv 1
,

\|T_{\sigma}\|\;\leq\;\sup_{U^{\prime}}\int\mathcal{K}_{\sigma}(U^{\prime},U)\,d\mu_{\Sigma}(U)\;=\;\int e^{-\tfrac{1}{2}S_{\mathrm{sp}}(U^{\prime})}\,\bigl(\mathcal{P}_{\sigma}(U^{\prime})\,J(U^{\prime})\bigr)^{1/2}\,\Xi\,d\mu_{\Sigma}(U^{\prime}),

(9.41)

where
\Xi=\sup_{U^{\prime}}\int e^{-S_{\mathrm{tm}}(U,U^{\prime})-\tfrac{1}{2}S_{\mathrm{sp}}(U)}\,(\mathcal{P}_{\sigma}(U)\,J(U))^{1/2}d\mu_{\Sigma}(U)
. Since all exponents are nonnegative and
\mathcal{P}_{\sigma}\leq 1
,
\Xi\leq 1
, hence
\|T_{\sigma}\|\leq 1
. The factorization of the path weight as a product of one-step kernels implies the correlation representation by standard iterated integration; density of simple tensors in
L^{2}
and boundedness of
T_{\sigma}
extend the identity to all cylinder
F
.
∎

The projected Hamiltonian is

H_{\sigma}\;=\;-a^{-1}\,\log T_{\sigma},

(9.42)

a positive self-adjoint operator with spectral support in
[0,\infty)
. For any local gauge-invariant
F
supported on two slices separated by
n
steps,

\langle\Omega,\,\widehat{F}^{\dagger}\,T_{\sigma}^{\,n}\,\widehat{F}\,\Omega\rangle\;=\;\int_{[0,\infty)}e^{-anE}\,d\mu_{F}(E),

(9.43)

where
d\mu_{F}
is a positive measure supported in
[E_{1},\infty)
,
E_{1}
being the bottom of the nonzero spectrum of
H_{\sigma}
.

For
\beta>0
sufficiently small,

\exp\!\Bigl(\beta\,\tfrac{1}{N}\mathrm{Re}\,\mathrm{Tr}\,U_{p}\Bigr)\;=\;\sum_{R\ \mathrm{irrep}}\alpha_{R}(\beta)\,\chi_{R}(U_{p}),\qquad\alpha_{R}(\beta)\,=\,O(\beta^{\,|R|})\ \ (\beta\downarrow 0),

(9.44)

where
|R|
is the number of boxes of the Young diagram of
R
. Link integration using character orthogonality reorganizes partition function and gauge-invariant correlators into sums over connected tiled surfaces
\Sigma
on the dual lattice with weights obeying

|w(\Sigma)|\;\leq\;\Bigl(\tfrac{C_{N}\,\beta}{N}\Bigr)^{|\Sigma|},

(9.45)

for a constant
C_{N}\geq 1
depending only on
N
. Grouping connected surfaces into polymers
\gamma
defines activities
\zeta(\gamma)
with

|\zeta(\gamma)|\;\leq\;A(\beta)^{\,|\gamma|},\qquad A(\beta)\xrightarrow[\beta\downarrow 0]{}0.

(9.46)

The Kotecký-Preiss criterion
[
19
,
25
]
is satisfied for small
\beta
, yielding absolute convergence of the Mayer series for
\log Z
and of all truncated gauge-invariant correlations. Thus for any local gauge-invariant observable
O(x)
there exist
C_{O}<\infty
and
m(\beta)>0
such that

\bigl|\langle O(x)\,O(y)\rangle_{c}\bigr|\;\leq\;C_{O}\,e^{-m(\beta)\,d(x,y)}.

(9.47)

In particular, restricting to time-separated slices and using the spectral representation in Proposition
9.4
gives

\langle\Omega,\,\widehat{O}^{\dagger}\,T_{\sigma}^{\,n}\,\widehat{O}\,\Omega\rangle\;\leq\;C_{O}\,e^{-m(\beta)\,an},

(9.48)

hence

E_{1}(a,\beta)\;\geq\;m(\beta),

(9.49)

uniformly in the spatial volume
[
7
, Ch. III]
.

Fix an integer blocking factor
b\geq 2
, set
a_{k}=b^{k}a
, and let
\Lambda_{k}
be the lattice with temporal spacing
a_{k}
and the same spatial spacings. Write
\mathcal{C}_{k}=G^{\Sigma_{k}}
,
d\mu_{\Sigma_{k}}=\bigotimes_{\ell\in\Sigma_{k}}dU_{\ell}
, and
\mathcal{H}_{k}=L^{2}(\mathcal{C}_{k},d\mu_{\Sigma_{k}})
. The slice-wise horizon projector at scale
k
is

P_{\sigma,k}\;=\;\chi_{\sigma}\!\bigl({\Delta_{A^{\,h}}^{(k)}}\bigr)

(9.50)

with exponential locality constants depending only on
\sigma
. Define a block map
\mathcal{B}_{k}:G^{\mathcal{B}(\Lambda_{k})}\to G^{\mathcal{B}(\Lambda_{k+1})}
by averaging over a reflection-equivariant family
\mathcal{P}(\bar{b})
of fine paths within the union of the two coarse blocks adjacent to
\bar{b}
, followed by nearest-neighbor projection:

\mathcal{B}_{k}(U)_{\bar{b}}\;=\;\mathrm{Proj}_{G}\!\Bigl(\frac{1}{|\mathcal{P}(\bar{b})|}\sum_{\gamma\in\mathcal{P}(\bar{b})}\ \prod_{\ell\in\gamma}U_{\ell}\Bigr).

(9.51)

The coarse projected measure
\mu^{(k+1)}
is defined by pushforward with a positive insertion on internal time boundaries of blocks:

\int_{\mathcal{C}_{k+1}}F(\bar{U})\,d\mu^{(k+1)}(\bar{U})\;=\;\frac{1}{Z_{k}}\int F\!\bigl(\mathcal{B}_{k}(U)\bigr)\,\Bigl(\prod_{\text{internal time boundaries}}\mathcal{P}_{\sigma,k}(U)\Bigr)\,d\mu^{(k)}(U).

(9.52)

Here
\mathcal{P}_{\sigma,k}
is built from
P_{\sigma,k}
and is supported in a fixed temporal collar inside each block.

Theorem 9.5

(OS positivity under blocking)
.

If
\mu^{(k)}
is OS-positive, then
\mu^{(k+1)}
is OS-positive.

Proof.

Let
F
depend on links in
\Lambda_{k+1,+}\cup\Pi
. Then

\langle F,F\rangle_{\mathrm{OS},k+1}\;=\;\frac{1}{Z_{k}}\int\overline{(\Theta F)\!\circ\!\mathcal{B}_{k}(U)}\,\bigl(F\!\circ\!\mathcal{B}_{k}(U)\bigr)\,\Bigl(\prod\mathcal{P}_{\sigma,k}(U)\Bigr)\,d\mu^{(k)}(U).

(9.53)

The composition
F\circ\mathcal{B}_{k}
lies in the positive half-algebra at scale
k
by reflection equivariance and finite range of
\mathcal{B}_{k}
. The insertion
\prod\mathcal{P}_{\sigma,k}
is a positive reflection-invariant functional supported on a finite collar. OS positivity of
\mu^{(k)}
implies the integral is nonnegative.
∎

Each
\mu^{(k)}
admits a positive self-adjoint transfer matrix
T_{\sigma,k}
on
\mathcal{H}_{k}
with
\|T_{\sigma,k}\|\leq 1
.
Let
\Omega_{k}\equiv 1\in\mathcal{H}_{k}
and
H_{\sigma,k}=-a_{k}^{-1}\log T_{\sigma,k}
.

Definition 9.6

(
{\sigma}
modified transfer operator)
.

Let
M_{\sigma}
denote the positive multiplication operator on the one slice
L^{2}
space given by the scalar
p_{\sigma}[U^{h}|_{t}]
from Sec.(
7
).
We define

T_{\sigma,k}\;:=\;M_{\sigma}^{1/2}\,T_{k}\,M_{\sigma}^{1/2},\qquad\Omega_{\sigma,k}\;:=\;\Omega_{k}.

(9.54)

By construction
T_{\sigma,k}
is a positive self adjoint contraction and
(T_{\sigma,k},\Omega_{\sigma,k})
is a vacuum pair; moreover
M_{\sigma}
commutes with OS reflection and gauge transformations on each slice.

Denote by
E_{1,k}
the bottom of the nonzero spectrum of
H_{\sigma,k}
and by
\lambda_{2,k}
the second eigenvalue of
T_{\sigma,k}
, so that

\Delta_{k}:=1-\lambda_{2,k},\qquad E_{1,k}:=-a_{k}^{-1}\log\lambda_{2,k}=-a_{k}^{-1}\log(1-\Delta_{k})

(9.55)

Define
V_{k}:\mathcal{H}_{k+1}\to\mathcal{H}_{k}
by pullback along
\mathcal{B}_{k}
,

(V_{k}\psi)(U)\;=\;\psi\!\bigl(\mathcal{B}_{k}(U)\bigr).

(9.56)

This map is bounded and reflection equivariant.

Lemma 9.7

(Operator order interlacing)
.

There exists a positive operator
E_{k}
on
\mathcal{H}_{k+1}
with
\|E_{k}\|\leq\varepsilon_{k}
such that

T_{\sigma,k+1}\ \preccurlyeq\ V_{k}^{\,*}\,T_{\sigma,k}\,V_{k}\;+\;E_{k},

(9.57)

where
A\preccurlyeq B
means
\langle\psi,A\psi\rangle\leq\langle\psi,B\psi\rangle
for all
\psi
.

Proof.

For
\psi\in\mathcal{H}_{k+1}
,

\langle\psi,T_{\sigma,k+1}\psi\rangle\;=\;\iint\overline{\psi(\bar{U}^{\prime})}\,K_{\sigma,k+1}(\bar{U}^{\prime},\bar{U})\,\psi(\bar{U})\,d\mu_{\Sigma_{k+1}}(\bar{U}^{\prime})\,d\mu_{\Sigma_{k+1}}(\bar{U}),

(9.58)

with
K_{\sigma,k+1}
the coarse one-step kernel. By definition of
\mu^{(k+1)}
,
K_{\sigma,k+1}
is obtained from
\mu^{(k)}
by integrating over fine variables constrained by
\bar{U}^{\prime}=\mathcal{B}_{k}(U^{\prime})
,
\bar{U}=\mathcal{B}_{k}(U)
, with the internal collar insertion. By Cauchy-Schwarz in
L^{2}(d\mu^{(k)})
and positivity of the insertion, one bounds

\langle\psi,T_{\sigma,k+1}\psi\rangle\;\leq\;\langle V_{k}\psi,T_{\sigma,k}V_{k}\psi\rangle\;+\;\langle\psi,E_{k}\psi\rangle,

(9.59)

where
E_{k}
collects cross-collar correlations. The exponential locality of
P_{\sigma,k}
implies that if the collar has fixed temporal width
w
(in units of
a_{k}
) independent of
k
, then

\|E_{k}\|\;\leq\;C\,e^{-c\,w},

(9.60)

with constants independent of
k
. Taking
w=w(k)
increasing, e.g.
w(k)=\lfloor c\,b^{\,k}\rfloor
(or
w(k)\asymp k
), gives

\|E_{k}\|\leq Ce^{-\gamma w(k)}
with
\sum_{k}\|E_{k}\|<\infty
; define
\varepsilon_{k}:=\|E_{k}\|
.

∎

Proposition 9.8

(Quantitative interlacing error)
.

Let
w\in\mathbb{N}
be the collar half-width used in the definition of
\Xi_{k,w}
.
There exist constants
c_{1},c_{2},\gamma>0
(independent of
k
) such that the error term in

(9.52)
satisfies

\|E_{k}\|\;\leq\;\varepsilon_{k}\;\leq\;c_{1}\,e^{-\gamma w}\;+\;c_{2}\,e^{-m_{\ast}a_{k}},

(9.61)

where
m_{\ast}>0
is the uniform clustering rate propagated at scale
k
(see Theorem (
7.4
) and
a_{k}=b^{k}a
. In particular, choosing

w_{k}=\left\lceil\frac{2}{\gamma}\,\log(k+2)\right\rceil\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad\sum_{k\geq 0}\varepsilon_{k}<\infty.

(9.62)

Proof.

Let
S=S_{-}\cup S_{0}\cup S_{+}
be the decomposition of the slab into left, collar, and right regions.
By Lemma (
8.4
), for any gauge-invariant local
functional
F
supported in
S_{-}\cup S_{+}
one has

\Big|\langle F\rangle_{k}-\langle F_{-}\rangle_{k}\,\langle F_{+}\rangle_{k}\Big|\;\leq\;C\,e^{-m^{*}\operatorname{dist}(S_{-},S_{+})},

(9.63)

where
m^{*}>0
is a uniform clustering rate at scale
k
, and the constant
C
depends only on
the block parameters and the Lipschitz seminorms of the local factors; see Theorem (
7.4
) for the
persistence of exponential clustering under the RG step. By construction of the single-RG-step
transfer operator ((
8.36
) implies an operator-norm bound

\big\|W_{k}^{\ast}T_{k+1}W_{k}\;-\;T_{k}\big\|\;\leq\;\varepsilon_{k},

(9.64)

with
\varepsilon_{k}\lesssim e^{-m^{*}b}
, where
b
is the blocking factor and
W_{k}
is the
gauge-invariant conditional expectation implementing the coarse-graining (see Eq.(
8.26
)).
Since
W_{k}\Omega_{k}=\Omega_{k+1}
and
W_{k}^{\ast}\Omega_{k+1}=\Omega_{k}
by normalization,
the pairings
(T_{k},\Omega_{k})
and
(T_{k+1},\Omega_{k+1})
are compatible in the sense of
Appendix (
14
) (Theorem B and Lemma C), hence

\lambda_{2}(T_{k+1})\;\leq\;\lambda_{2}(T_{k})\;+\;\varepsilon_{k},\qquad\Delta_{k+1}\;=\;1-\lambda_{2}(T_{k+1})\;\geq\;\Delta_{k}\;-\;\varepsilon_{k},

(9.65)

where
\lambda_{2}(\cdot)
is the vacuum-orthogonal contraction norm and

\Delta_{k}:=1-\lambda_{2}(T_{k})
(see Eqs.(
8.33
) & (
8.34
)). Iterating
(
9.65
) over scales and summing the geometric tail

\sum_{j\geq k}\varepsilon_{j}\lesssim e^{-m^{*}bk}
proves the claimed transport of the gap from
the strong-coupling regime to the scaling window.
∎

Theorem 9.9

(Step-scaling of gaps)
.

With
\varepsilon_{k}
as in Lemma
9.7
,

\Delta_{k+1}\;\geq\;\Delta_{k}\;-\;\varepsilon_{k}\qquad\text{for all }k\in\mathbb{N}.

(9.66)

In particular,

\liminf_{k\to\infty}\Delta_{k}\;\geq\;\Delta_{0}-\sum_{j\geq 0}\varepsilon_{j}\;>\;0.

(9.67)

Proof.

Let
\lambda_{2,k}
be the second eigenvalue of
T_{\sigma,k}
. For
\psi\perp\Omega_{k+1}
with
\|\psi\|=1
, Lemma
9.7
gives

\langle\psi,T_{\sigma,k+1}\psi\rangle\;\leq\;\langle V_{k}\psi,T_{\sigma,k}V_{k}\psi\rangle\;+\;\varepsilon_{k}.

(9.68)

Set
\phi=V_{k}\psi/\|V_{k}\psi\|
if
V_{k}\psi\neq 0
; otherwise choose any
\phi\perp\Omega_{k}
. Then

\langle\psi,T_{\sigma,k+1}\psi\rangle\;\leq\;\|V_{k}\psi\|^{2}\,\langle\phi,T_{\sigma,k}\phi\rangle\;+\;\varepsilon_{k}\;\leq\;\lambda_{2,k}\;+\;\varepsilon_{k}.

(9.69)

Taking the supremum over unit
\psi\perp\Omega_{k+1}
yields

\lambda_{2,k+1}\;\leq\;\lambda_{2,k}\;+\;\varepsilon_{k}.

(9.70)

Since
\Delta_{k}=-a_{k}^{-1}\log\lambda_{2,k}
and
-\log(\lambda+\varepsilon)\geq-\log\lambda-\varepsilon/(1-\lambda)
on
(0,1]
, absorbing
a_{k}^{-1}
into
\varepsilon_{k}
gives
\Delta_{k+1}\geq\Delta_{k}-\varepsilon_{k}
. Summability implies the liminf bound.
∎

Combining Theorem
9.9
with
\Delta_{0}\geq m(\beta)>0
yields a uniform positive lower bound on
\Delta_{k}
for all
k
.

Let
\xi_{*}=m_{*}^{-1}
denote any positive lower bound for the clustering length uniformly propagated by the reflection-positive renormalization group. The scaling window consists of those scales
k
satisfying

\sigma\ \ll\ a_{k}\ \ll\ \xi_{*},

(9.71)

that is,

\frac{\sigma}{a_{k}}\ \xrightarrow[k\ \text{in window}]{}\ 0,\qquad\frac{a_{k}}{\xi_{*}}\ \xrightarrow[k\ \text{in window}]{}\ 0.

(9.72)

The lower condition ensures that the localization length of
P_{\sigma,k}
is much smaller than the lattice spacing and does not affect the ultraviolet discretization; the upper condition ensures that many transfer steps fit within
\xi_{*}
, allowing controlled continuum interpolation in Euclidean time through
T_{\sigma,k}
. Since
a_{k}=b_{k}a
while
\xi^{\ast}
and
\sigma
are scale-independent,
the window
\sigma\ll a_{k}\ll\xi^{\ast}
is nonempty provided
a\ll\xi^{\ast}
initially.
On such a window, the hypotheses of OS reconstruction hold with a uniform mass threshold,
yielding Schwinger functions and, along a subsequence, a Wightman theory with nonzero gap
[
2
,
7
]
.

Appendix 10
BRST compatibility and parameter dependence

In this section a complete, self-contained account is given of the graded field algebra and its BRST differential on the hypercubic lattice, of the compatibility of the horizon-projector insertion and of the renormalization step with BRST cohomology, and of the step-by-step derivation of reflection positivity and of the transfer time-slicing formalism. We then establish differentiability and stability of all constructions with respect to the infrared cutoff scale
\sigma>0
entering the horizon projector and with respect to the blocking parameter
b\in\{2,3,\dots\}
. OS positivity is asserted and used only for the gauge-invariant, ghost-free sector. Ghost fields enter as auxiliaries for BRST and gauge-fixing; they are not included among OS-tested observables. All positivity statements in this paper concern the
s
-cohomology classes of gauge-invariant observables.

Throughout, the gauge group is
G=\mathrm{SU}(N)
with
N\geq 2
. The lattice spacing is
a>0
. The periodic hypercubic lattice is
\Lambda\subset a\mathbb{Z}^{4}
with Euclidean time direction
\mu=0
. Reflection of sites is the involution

\theta:(x_{0},\mathbf{x})\longmapsto(-x_{0},\mathbf{x}),

(10.1)

and the reflection plane is
\Pi=\{x_{0}=0\}
. The set of bonds is
\mathscr{B}=\{(x,\mu):x\in\Lambda,\ \mu=0,1,2,3\}
, with link variables
U_{(x,\mu)}\in G
and the orientation convention

U_{(x+\hat{\mu},-\mu)}=U_{(x,\mu)}^{-1}.

(10.2)

Plaquettes are elementary oriented squares
p\subset\Lambda
with plaquette variable
U_{p}
given by the ordered product of links around
p
. The Wilson action at inverse bare coupling
\beta=2N/g_{0}^{2}
is

S_{W}[U;\beta]=\beta\sum_{p\subset\Lambda}\Big(1-\frac{1}{N}\Re\mathrm{Tr}\,U_{p}\Big).

(10.3)

Temporal-axial gauge is imposed away from
\Pi
by setting

U_{0}(x)=\mathbf{1}\qquad\text{for all bonds that do not intersect }\Pi.

(10.4)

Reflection acts antilinearly on functionals
F
by

(\Theta F)[U]=\overline{F[U^{\theta}]},

(10.5)

where
U^{\theta}
is obtained by pulling back links under
\theta
and inverting links whose orientation reverses.

Let
\mathcal{g}=\mathcal{su}(N)
be endowed with the real Hilbert-Schmidt inner product

\langle X,Y\rangle=-\mathrm{Tr}(XY),\qquad X,Y\in\mathcal{g}.

(10.6)

Let
s
denote the lattice BRST differential.
The slice-wise horizon projector
P_{\sigma}
and the renormalization map
V_{k}
act on BRST cohomology in the sense that for any BRST-closed gauge-invariant observable
O
one has

s(O)=0\;\Rightarrow\;s(P_{\sigma}O)=0
and
s(O\circ V_{k})=0
,
while for BRST-exact
O=s\Xi
the insertions remain
s
-exact.
Consequently, expectations of gauge-invariant observables computed with the horizon-projected, blocked measures depend smoothly on
\sigma
and
b
and are BRST-cohomological.
Let
\mathfrak{A}_{\mathrm{link}}
be the unital
*
-algebra generated by matrix-valued coordinate functions on
\prod_{b\in\mathscr{B}}G
and by their right- and left-translation derivations. Introduce Grassmann ghost fields
c,\bar{c}:\Lambda\to\mathcal{g}
and commuting Nakanishi-Lautrup fields
B:\Lambda\to\mathcal{g}
. Let
\mathfrak{A}_{\mathrm{gh}}
be the graded
*
-algebra generated by polynomial cylinder functions of
(c,\bar{c},B)
with the canonical
\mathbb{Z}_{2}
-grading given by ghost number, and with the adjoint given by sitewise
*
on
\mathcal{g}
and conjugation of coefficients. The full graded algebra is the graded tensor product

\mathfrak{A}=\mathfrak{A}_{\mathrm{link}}\widehat{\otimes}\mathfrak{A}_{\mathrm{gh}}.

(10.7)

Definition 10.1

(BRST complex and differential)
.

With
\mathfrak{A}_{\mathrm{link}},\mathfrak{A}_{\mathrm{gh}}
as in Eq.(
10.7
), set

\mathfrak{A}:=\mathfrak{A}_{\mathrm{link}}\widehat{\otimes}\mathfrak{A}_{\mathrm{gh}}
.
Define the BRST differential
s:\mathfrak{A}\to\mathfrak{A}
by its action on generators:

\displaystyle s\,U(x,\mu)

\displaystyle=c(x)\,U(x,\mu)-U(x,\mu)\,c(x+\hat{\mu}),

(10.8)

\displaystyle s\,c(x)

\displaystyle=-\tfrac{1}{2}[c(x),c(x)],

\displaystyle s\,\bar{c}(x)

\displaystyle=i\,b(x),\qquad s\,b(x)=0,

extended by graded Leibniz and by
s(\cdot)^{\ast}=(s\cdot)^{\ast}
.
The (gauge-fixed) lattice action is of the form
S_{\mathrm{gf}}=s\Psi
for a local gauge-fixing
fermion
\Psi
(e.g., lattice Landau gauge), and
s^{2}=0
holds identically.

Proposition 10.2

(BRST compatibility of the horizon insertion)
.

Let
P_{\sigma}(t)=\chi_{\sigma}\!\big({\Delta_{A^{h}}(t)}\big)
be the slice horizon operator
in either regime (A) or (B) above, and let
I_{\sigma}=\prod_{t}p_{\sigma}[U^{h}_{t}]
be the slice-wise
insertion in the Euclidean measure. Then
s\,I_{\sigma}=0
, hence
I_{\sigma}
acts on BRST cohomology
classes and preserves them. Consequently,
T_{\sigma}
commutes with the BRST projector onto
cohomology.

Proof.

The operator
P_{\sigma}(t)
is a gauge-invariant, reflection-covariant functional of the Landau
representative
A^{h}(t)
; hence it is invariant under infinitesimal gauge transformations and

s
-exact variations. The scalar choices
p_{\sigma}=\operatorname{Tr}P_{\sigma}
or

p_{\sigma}=\exp(-\langle\varphi,(I-P_{\sigma})\varphi\rangle)
are thus
s
-invariant. In Secs.(
7
-
9
) we adopt the concrete choice
p_{\sigma}=\mathrm{Tr}\,P_{\sigma}
fixed there.
Since
s
is
a graded derivation,
s\,I_{\sigma}=\sum_{t}(s\,p_{\sigma}[U^{h}_{t}])\prod_{t^{\prime}\neq t}p_{\sigma}[U^{h}_{t^{\prime}}]=0
.
∎

Lemma 10.3

(Nilpotency)
.

The map
s
is a degree-
+1
graded derivation on
\mathfrak{A}
and satisfies

s^{2}=0.

(10.9)

Proof.

The graded Leibniz rule is built into the definition. It suffices to check
s^{2}
on generators. Using (
10.8
),

\displaystyle s^{2}U_{(x,\mu)}

\displaystyle=i\,s(c(x))\,U_{(x,\mu)}-i\,c(x)\,s(U_{(x,\mu)})-i\,s(U_{(x,\mu)})\,c(x+\hat{\mu})+i\,U_{(x,\mu)}\,s(c(x+\hat{\mu}))

(10.10)

\displaystyle=-\tfrac{i}{2}[c(x),c(x)]U_{(x,\mu)}-i\,c(x)\,(i\,c(x)\,U_{(x,\mu)}-i\,U_{(x,\mu)}\,c(x+\hat{\mu}))

\displaystyle-i\,(i\,c(x)\,U_{(x,\mu)}-i\,U_{(x,\mu)}\,c(x+\hat{\mu}))\,c(x+\hat{\mu})+\tfrac{i}{2}U_{(x,\mu)}[c(x+\hat{\mu}),c(x+\hat{\mu})],

and cancellations follow from the Jacobi identity in
\mathfrak{g}
together with the antisymmetry of the Grassmann variables, hence
s^{2}U_{(x,\mu)}=0
. Moreover,

s^{2}c(x)=-\tfrac{1}{2}s[c(x),c(x)]=-\tfrac{1}{2}\big([sc(x),c(x)]-[c(x),sc(x)]\big)=0,

(10.11)

and
s^{2}\bar{c}(x)=s\mathcal{B}(x)=0
,
s^{2}\mathcal{B}(x)=0
by (
10.8
). Extending by the graded Leibniz rule yields
s^{2}=0
on
\mathfrak{A}
.
∎

Let
\mathcal{F}
denote the lattice Landau gauge condition and
\Psi[\bar{c},U]=\sum_{x}\langle\bar{c}(x),\mathcal{F}[U](x)\rangle
the gauge-fixing fermion. Formally
S_{\mathrm{gf}}+S_{\mathrm{FP}}=s\Psi
, but we will not rely on this identity; instead, we use
s
only as a differential on
\mathfrak{A}
to control cohomology of observables. The BRST cohomology at ghost number zero is

\mathcal{H}^{0}_{\mathrm{BRST}}:=\frac{\ker\big(s:\mathfrak{A}^{0}\to\mathfrak{A}^{1}\big)}{\mathrm{im}\big(s:\mathfrak{A}^{-1}\to\mathfrak{A}^{0}\big)}.

(10.12)

The algebra
\mathfrak{A}_{\mathrm{phys}}
of strictly gauge-invariant, even-Grassmann, local functionals injects canonically into
\mathcal{H}^{0}_{\mathrm{BRST}}
.

On each Euclidean time slice
t\in a\mathbb{Z}
, consider the lattice Landau functional

\mathcal{L}_{t}(g;U):=\sum_{\mathbf{x},\,i=1}^{3}\mathrm{Re}\,\mathrm{Tr}\Big(\mathbf{1}-g(t,\mathbf{x})\,U_{(t,\mathbf{x};i)}\,g(t,\mathbf{x}+\hat{\imath})^{-1}\Big).

(10.13)

For every
U
and
t
, let
h_{t}[U]
be a measurable, reflection-covariant choice of a global minimizer. Define the slice-wise representative
A^{h}[U]
from the gauge-transformed links
U^{\,h_{t}[U]}
. The fundamental modular region
\mathcal{M}
is the set of links whose representative is an absolute minimum of
\mathcal{L}_{t}
; for
\mathrm{SU}(N)
,
\mathcal{M}
contains exactly one representative of almost every gauge orbit up to the global center
[
12
]
.

Let
\Delta_{A^{h}[U]}=\sum_{i=1}^{3}(D^{h}_{i})^{\dagger}D^{h}_{i}
be the covariant spatial Laplacian on each slice. Fix a Gevrey cutoff
\chi\in C^{\infty}([0,\infty))
with

\chi(\lambda)=1\ \text{for }\lambda\in[0,1],\qquad\chi(\lambda)=0\ \text{for }\lambda\geq 2,

(10.14)

and subfactorial derivative bounds. For
\sigma>0
set
\chi_{\sigma}(\lambda)=\chi(\lambda/\sigma)
and define the horizon projector

P_{\sigma}(U):=\chi_{\sigma}\big({\Delta_{A^{h}[U]}}\big).

(10.15)

Then
P_{\sigma}(U)
is a positive contraction with heat-kernel representation

P_{\sigma}(U)=\int_{0}^{\infty}e^{-t\,\Delta_{A^{h}[U]}}\,d\nu_{\sigma}(t),

(10.16)

where
d\nu_{\sigma}
is a finite positive Borel measure supported in
[c_{1}\sigma^{-2},c_{2}\sigma^{-2}]
for some
0<c_{1}<c_{2}<\infty
. Its integral kernel is exponentially localized with constants uniform in the spatial volume
[
13
,
15
]
.

Lemma 10.4

(BRST invariance of the slice representative)
.

For almost every
U
with respect to Haar measure, the map
U\mapsto A^{h}[U]
depends only on the gauge orbit of
U
. Consequently, for every
F\in\mathfrak{A}
that is a functional of
A^{h}
and its covariant derivatives,

sF=0.

(10.17)

Proof.

If
U^{g}
lies on the orbit of
U
, then
\mathcal{L}_{t}(g^{\prime};U^{g})=\mathcal{L}_{t}(gg^{\prime}g^{-1};U)
. The set of absolute minima is thus carried into itself by
g
on the left and
g^{-1}
on the right; the reflection- and gauge-covariant tie-breaking rule yields
h_{t}[U^{g}]=g\,h_{t}[U]
. Therefore
U^{\,h_{t}[U^{g}]}=U^{\,h_{t}[U]}
and
A^{h}[U^{g}]=A^{h}[U]
. The BRST variation is an infinitesimal gauge transformation, hence
sA^{h}=0
almost everywhere. The claim follows by the chain rule.
∎

Proposition 10.5

(BRST-closedness of the horizon projector)
.

For every
\sigma>0
and every cylinder functional
F\in\mathfrak{A}
,

s\,\mathrm{Tr}\,P_{\sigma}(U)=0,\qquad s\,\langle X,P_{\sigma}(U)X\rangle=0

(10.18)

for all
X\in\ell^{2}(\Lambda_{t})\otimes\mathcal{g}
. Equivalently,

s\,P_{\sigma}(U)=0.

(10.19)

Proof.

By Lemma
10.4
,
\Delta_{A^{h}[U]}
is BRST-invariant. Functional calculus preserves invariance; thus for any bounded Borel
f
,
s\,f(\Delta_{A^{h}[U]})=0
. Taking
f(\lambda)=\chi_{\sigma}({\lambda})
yields
sP_{\sigma}=0
. The statements for quadratic forms and traces follow by linearity.
∎

Let
\mathcal{B}_{b}
be the coarse-graining map from fine links to coarse links of spacing
ba
, defined by the nearest-neighbor Frobenius projection of the arithmetic mean of ordered path products along a reflection-symmetric family of paths inside adjacent blocks. Gauge equivariance implies

s\,(F\circ\mathcal{B}_{b})=(sF)\circ\mathcal{B}_{b}

(10.20)

for all cylinder functionals
F
.

Proposition 10.6

(Chain-map property of the RG step)
.

Let
\mu_{\sigma}
be the OS-positive gauge-field measure with slice-wise insertion of
P_{\sigma}(U)
, and let
\Theta_{\sigma}(U)
be the product over internal time boundaries of blocks of the positive slice operators derived from
P_{\sigma}(U)
. Define

(\mathcal{R}_{b,\sigma}F)(U):=\mathbb{E}_{\mu_{\sigma}}\!\big[F\big(\mathcal{B}_{b}(U)\big)\,\Theta_{\sigma}(U)\big].

(10.21)

Then for all
F\in\mathfrak{A}
,

s\big(\mathcal{R}_{b,\sigma}F\big)=\mathcal{R}_{b,\sigma}\big(sF\big).

(10.22)

Consequently,
\mathcal{R}_{b,\sigma}
descends to a well-defined map on
\mathcal{H}^{0}_{\mathrm{BRST}}
.

Proof.

Gauge equivariance of
\mathcal{B}_{b}
gives
s(F\circ\mathcal{B}_{b})=(sF)\circ\mathcal{B}_{b}
. By Proposition
10.5
,
\Theta_{\sigma}
is BRST-closed. The Wilson-Haar measure is gauge invariant; expectation commutes with
s
. Therefore

s(\mathcal{R}_{b,\sigma}F)=\mathbb{E}_{\mu_{\sigma}}\!\big[(sF)\circ\mathcal{B}_{b}\,\Theta_{\sigma}\big]=\mathcal{R}_{b,\sigma}(sF).

(10.23)

If
F=sG
, then
\mathcal{R}_{b,\sigma}F=s(\mathcal{R}_{b,\sigma}G)
, hence
\mathcal{R}_{b,\sigma}
induces a map on cohomology.
∎

Define the even-Grassmann subspace
\mathcal{F}_{+}
of cylinder functionals supported in
\Lambda_{+}\cup\Pi
. The Osterwalder-Schrader sesquilinear form is

\langle F,G\rangle_{\mathrm{OS},\sigma}:=\int\overline{(\Theta F)[U]}\,G[U]\;d\mu_{\sigma}(U),

(10.24)

with

d\mu_{\sigma}(U)=Z^{-1}\exp(-S_{W}[U])\prod_{t\in a\mathbb{Z}}\mathcal{K}_{\sigma,t}(U)\;d\mu_{\mathrm{Haar}}(U),

(10.25)

where each
\mathcal{K}_{\sigma,t}(U)
is a positive slice factor built from
P_{\sigma}(U)
at time
t
.

Lemma 10.7

(Factorization in temporal-axial gauge)
.

In temporal-axial gauge away from
\Pi
, the Wilson weight and the factors
\mathcal{K}_{\sigma,t}
factorize as a product of three terms supported in
\Lambda_{+}
,
\Pi
, and
\Lambda_{-}
, respectively, with no direct coupling between
\Lambda_{+}
and
\Lambda_{-}
. Moreover, the cross terms of the kernels of
\mathcal{K}_{\sigma,t}
between
\Lambda_{+}
and
\Lambda_{-}
vanish in operator norm in the thermodynamic limit.

Proof.

Time-like plaquettes that do not intersect
\Pi
are trivial in temporal-axial gauge, and the action splits into contributions from
\Lambda_{+}
,
\Lambda_{-}
, and a boundary slab supported on
\Pi
. The factor
\mathcal{K}_{\sigma,t}
depends only on links at time
t
through
P_{\sigma}(U)
, whose kernel is exponentially localized on the slice. If
t>0
the support of
\mathcal{K}_{\sigma,t}
lies in
\Lambda_{+}\cup\Pi
; if
t<0
it lies in
\Lambda_{-}\cup\Pi
. Exponential decay of the kernel of
P_{\sigma}(U)
implies that cross terms between
\Lambda_{+}
and
\Lambda_{-}
vanish in operator norm as the time extent grows, by Schur estimates
[
13
,
15
]
.
∎

Theorem 10.8

(Reflection positivity)
.

For every
\sigma>0
, the form (
10.24
) is positive semidefinite on
\mathcal{F}_{+}
.

Proof.

Let
F=\sum_{j}\alpha_{j}F_{j}
with
F_{j}\in\mathcal{F}_{+}
supported in disjoint finite regions of
\Lambda_{+}\cup\Pi
. By Lemma
10.7
, the measure factorizes as

d\mu_{\sigma}(U)=d\mu_{+,\sigma}(U_{+})\,\mathcal{B}_{\sigma}(U_{|\Pi})\,d\mu_{-,\sigma}(U_{-}),

(10.26)

with
d\mu_{\pm,\sigma}
positive measures supported in
\Lambda_{\pm}\cup\Pi
and
\mathcal{B}_{\sigma}
a positive boundary kernel on
\Pi
. Then

\langle F,F\rangle_{\mathrm{OS},\sigma}=\int\overline{\Big(\sum_{j}\alpha_{j}(\Theta F_{j})[U_{-}]\Big)}\,\Big(\sum_{k}\alpha_{k}F_{k}[U_{+}]\Big)\,\mathcal{B}_{\sigma}(U_{|\Pi})\;d\mu_{+,\sigma}\,d\mu_{-,\sigma},

(10.27)

which is the squared
L^{2}(\mathcal{H}_{\Pi},\mathcal{B}_{\sigma})
-norm of
\sum_{k}\alpha_{k}F_{k}[U_{+}]
, hence nonnegative
[
1
,
2
,
10
]
.
∎

Define the null space

\mathcal{N}_{\sigma}=\{F\in\mathcal{F}_{+}:\langle F,F\rangle_{\mathrm{OS},\sigma}=0\},

(10.28)

and
\mathcal{D}_{\sigma}=\mathcal{F}_{+}/\mathcal{N}_{\sigma}
. The completion of
\mathcal{D}_{\sigma}
is the physical Hilbert space
\mathcal{H}_{\sigma}
. Time translation by one lattice step in the positive direction acts on functionals by

(\tau F)[U]=F[\tau^{-1}U],\qquad(\tau^{-1}U)_{(x,\mu)}=U_{(x-a\hat{0},\mu)}.

(10.29)

The transfer operator
T_{\sigma}:\mathcal{H}_{\sigma}\to\mathcal{H}_{\sigma}
is defined on representatives by

\langle[F],T_{\sigma}[G]\rangle_{\mathrm{OS},\sigma}:=\langle\tau F,G\rangle_{\mathrm{OS},\sigma}.

(10.30)

Theorem 10.9

(Transfer operator)
.

For every
\sigma>0
,
T_{\sigma}
is a well-defined bounded self-adjoint positive operator on
\mathcal{H}_{\sigma}
with
\|T_{\sigma}\|\leq 1
, and

T_{\sigma}=P_{\sigma}^{1/2}\,T\,P_{\sigma}^{1/2},

(10.31)

where
T
is the unprojected transfer operator acting on
L^{2}(\text{links at fixed time};\,\text{Haar})
.
By definition (
10.31
), the compression map
P_{\sigma}^{1/2}:\mathcal{H}\!\to\!\mathcal{H}_{\sigma}
intertwines
T
with
T_{\sigma}
,

P_{\sigma}^{1/2}\,T\;=\;T_{\sigma}\,P_{\sigma}^{1/2},

(10.32)

equivalently, the following square commutes:
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{H}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{H}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{H}_{\sigma}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{H}_{\sigma}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces T}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces P_{\sigma}^{1/2}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces P_{\sigma}^{1/2}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces T_{\sigma}}

Proof.

Reflection positivity and translation invariance yield
\langle\tau F,\tau F\rangle_{\mathrm{OS},\sigma}\leq\langle F,F\rangle_{\mathrm{OS},\sigma}
, so
T_{\sigma}
is a contraction. Symmetry follows from invariance under reflection and time reversal; positivity from
\langle[F],T_{\sigma}[F]\rangle_{\mathrm{OS},\sigma}\geq 0
. The compression formula arises by explicit factorization of the weight across two consecutive time slices: the slice-wise factor
P_{\sigma}
multiplies boundary data by
P_{\sigma}^{1/2}
, whence
T_{\sigma}=P_{\sigma}^{1/2}TP_{\sigma}^{1/2}

[
10
, Ch. 3]
.
∎

Proposition 10.10

(BRST compatibility of the transfer operator)
.

For every
F\in\mathfrak{A}_{\mathrm{phys}}
and every
n\in\mathbb{N}
,

\pi_{\sigma}\big(\tau^{n}F\big)=T_{\sigma}^{n}\,\pi_{\sigma}(F),\qquad\pi_{\sigma}(sF)=0,

(10.33)

and the diagram

\begin{array}[]{ccc}\mathfrak{A}_{\mathrm{phys}}&\xrightarrow{\ \ \tau\ \ }&\mathfrak{A}_{\mathrm{phys}}\\
\pi_{\sigma}\downarrow&&\downarrow\pi_{\sigma}\\
\mathcal{H}_{\sigma}&\xrightarrow{\ \ T_{\sigma}\ \ }&\mathcal{H}_{\sigma}\end{array}

(10.34)

commutes. In particular,
T_{\sigma}
acts on BRST cohomology classes and preserves them.

Proof.

The first identity is the definition of
T_{\sigma}
. The second follows from
sF=0
for
F\in\mathfrak{A}_{\mathrm{phys}}
. Commutativity is immediate.
∎

The Hamiltonian is defined by spectral calculus as

H_{\sigma}=-a^{-1}\log T_{\sigma},

(10.35)

a positive self-adjoint operator on
\mathcal{H}_{\sigma}
.

Set
f_{\sigma}(\lambda)=\chi_{\sigma}(\lambda)=\chi(\lambda/\sigma)
. For
r\in\mathbb{N}
, the chain rule gives

\partial_{\sigma}^{r}f_{\sigma}(\lambda)=\sum_{m=1}^{r}\sigma^{-r}\,p_{r,m}\!\Big(\tfrac{\lambda}{\sigma}\Big)\,\chi^{(m)}\!\Big(\tfrac{\lambda}{\sigma}\Big),

(10.36)

for explicit polynomials
p_{r,m}
. Use the Helffer-Sjöstrand representation
[
15
,
27
]
for
f_{\sigma}({\Delta})
to justify differentiation under the integral sign.

Lemma 10.11

(Operator-norm differentiability of
P_{\sigma}
)
.

For every
r\in\mathbb{N}
there exists
C_{r}<\infty
such that for all
\sigma>0
and all gauge fields
U
,

\big\|\partial_{\sigma}^{r}P_{\sigma}(U)\big\|_{\ell^{2}\to\ell^{2}}\leq C_{r}\,\sigma^{-r}.

(10.37)

Moreover, the integral kernels of
\partial_{\sigma}^{r}P_{\sigma}(U)
enjoy exponential off-diagonal decay with constants uniform in the spatial volume and polynomially controlled in
\sigma^{-1}
.

Proof.

Write

P_{\sigma}(U)=\frac{1}{\pi}\int_{\mathbb{C}}\bar{\partial}\widetilde{f}_{\sigma}(z)\,({\Delta_{A^{h}[U]}}-z)^{-1}\,d^{2}z,

(10.38)

with
\widetilde{f}_{\sigma}
an almost-analytic extension of
f_{\sigma}
obeying

|\bar{\partial}\widetilde{f}_{\sigma}(z)|\leq C_{k}\,\sigma^{-k-1}(1+|\mathrm{Re}\,z|)^{-k}\,|\mathrm{Im}\,z|^{k}

(10.39)

for all
k
. Differentiation under the integral sign is justified by dominated convergence using
\|({\Delta}-z)^{-1}\|\leq|\mathrm{Im}\,z|^{-1}
. Each
\sigma
-derivative produces a factor
\sigma^{-1}
and derivatives of
\chi
evaluated at
\lambda/\sigma
; boundedness of all derivatives of
\chi
on a compact set yields
\|\partial_{\sigma}^{r}P_{\sigma}(U)\|\leq C_{r}\sigma^{-r}
. Exponential kernel decay follows from Combes-Thomas resolvent bounds for finite-range positive operators together with the almost-analytic bounds
[
14
,
15
]
.
∎

Corollary 10.12

(Differentiability of
T_{\sigma}
and
H_{\sigma}
)
.

Let
T(a)
be the one-step transfer operator on the slice Hilbert space and

T_{\sigma}(a)=P_{\sigma}^{1/2}\,T(a)\,P_{\sigma}^{1/2}
. Then for each
r\in\mathbb{N}
,

\partial_{\sigma}^{r}T_{\sigma}(a)
exists in operator norm and

\|\partial_{\sigma}^{r}T_{\sigma}(a)\|\;\leq\;C^{\prime}_{r}\,\sigma^{-r}\,\|T(a)\|,

(10.40)

with constants
C^{\prime}_{r}<\infty
depending only on
(C_{r},\|P_{\sigma}\|)
from Lemma 10.9.
Moreover, on the spectral subspace where
T_{\sigma}(a)
has spectrum in
(0,1]
bounded away from

0
, the Hamiltonian
H_{\sigma}(a)=-a^{-1}\log T_{\sigma}(a)
is
C^{\infty}
in
\sigma
and

\|\partial_{\sigma}^{r}H_{\sigma}(a)\|\;\leq\;a^{-1}\,C^{\prime\prime}_{r}\,\sigma^{-r},

(10.41)

with
C^{\prime\prime}_{r}
depending on the distance of
\mathrm{spec}(T_{\sigma}(a))
to
0
.

Proof.

Differentiate
T_{\sigma}(a)=P_{\sigma}^{1/2}T(a)P_{\sigma}^{1/2}
using the product rule and Lemma 10.9,
plus the holomorphic functional calculus for
X\mapsto X^{1/2}
on positive operators.
For
H_{\sigma}(a)
use the holomorphic functional calculus for
\log
on sectors bounded away
from
0
and the chain rule.
∎

Let
\langle\cdot\rangle_{\sigma}
denote expectation with respect to
d\mu_{\sigma}
. For a local bounded observable
F
supported on finitely many time slices,

\langle F\rangle_{\sigma}=\int F(U)\,\prod_{t=-T}^{T}\mathcal{K}_{\sigma,t}(U)\,d\mu(U),

(10.42)

where
d\mu
is the
\sigma
-independent Wilson-Haar measure.

Proposition 10.13

(Smoothness of expectations and of
T_{\sigma}
)
.

If
F
is a local, gauge-invariant cylinder functional supported on
t\in[-T,T]
, then
\sigma\mapsto\langle F\rangle_{\sigma}
is
C^{\infty}
on
(0,\infty)
. Moreover, for
|\sigma-\sigma^{\prime}|
sufficiently small,

\|T_{\sigma}-T_{\sigma^{\prime}}\|_{\mathcal{H}_{\sigma}\to\mathcal{H}_{\sigma^{\prime}}}\;\leq\;C\,|\sigma-\sigma^{\prime}|.

(10.43)

In particular,
\sigma\mapsto T_{\sigma}
is strongly and hence norm-continuous on compact
\sigma
-intervals disjoint from
\{0\}
.

Proof.

Differentiating under the integral is justified by dominated convergence using Lemma
10.11
and exponential locality of
\mathcal{K}_{\sigma,t}
. For the transfer operator, Theorem
10.9
gives

T_{\sigma}=P_{\sigma}^{1/2}TP_{\sigma}^{1/2}.

(10.44)

The functional calculus representation of the square root implies

\|P_{\sigma}^{1/2}-P_{\sigma^{\prime}}^{1/2}\|\leq C\|P_{\sigma}-P_{\sigma^{\prime}}\|\leq C^{\prime}|\sigma-\sigma^{\prime}|,

(10.45)

hence

\|T_{\sigma}-T_{\sigma^{\prime}}\|\leq\|P_{\sigma}^{1/2}-P_{\sigma^{\prime}}^{1/2}\|\,\|T\|\,\|P_{\sigma}^{1/2}\|+\|P_{\sigma^{\prime}}^{1/2}\|\,\|T\|\,\|P_{\sigma}^{1/2}-P_{\sigma^{\prime}}^{1/2}\|\leq C|\sigma-\sigma^{\prime}|.

(10.46)

Continuity on
\mathcal{H}_{\sigma}
follows by density of cylinder vectors.
∎

Consequently, the Hamiltonians
H_{\sigma}=-a^{-1}\log T_{\sigma}
form a norm-resolvent continuous family on any compact
\sigma
-interval disjoint from
\{0\}
, and eigenvalues vary continuously with
\sigma

[
27
]
.
The blocking factor
b\in\{2,3,\dots\}
enters through
\mathcal{B}_{b}
and through the placement of horizon insertions on internal time boundaries of blocks.

Proposition 10.14

(Stability under changes of
b
)
.

Fix
\sigma>0
. For any two blocking factors
b,b^{\prime}\geq 2
and any local observable
F
supported on finitely many coarse time slices,

\big\|\mathcal{R}_{b,\sigma}F-\mathcal{R}_{b^{\prime},\sigma}F\big\|\;\leq\;C(F)\,\mathbf{1}_{\{b\neq b^{\prime}\}},

(10.47)

with
C(F)
depending on
F
and
\sigma
but not on the volume. Moreover, both
\mathcal{R}_{b,\sigma}
and
\mathcal{R}_{b^{\prime},\sigma}
commute with
s
and preserve reflection positivity.

Proof.

The maps
\mathcal{B}_{b}
and
\mathcal{B}_{b^{\prime}}
differ only through the choice of path families inside adjacent blocks. For local
F
, the difference
F\circ\mathcal{B}_{b}-F\circ\mathcal{B}_{b^{\prime}}
is supported in a finite neighborhood of the support of
F
enlarged by at most one block diameter, and its pointwise size is bounded by a constant depending on first derivatives of
F
because the Frobenius projection is
1
-Lipschitz. The horizon insertions on internal time boundaries differ by finitely many slice factors, each varying by at most a constant depending on
\sigma
since
P_{\sigma}
is a bounded positive contraction. Integration against the Wilson-Haar measure yields the stated bound with a constant independent of the volume. BRST commutation is Proposition
10.6
and is independent of
b
. Reflection positivity follows from Theorem
10.8
because factorization across
\Pi
and exponential locality of slice insertions hold for all
b
.
∎

Appendix 11
Relation to constructive RG schemes

This section presents a complete, self-contained derivation of reflection positivity and transfer-time-slicing for lattice Yang-Mills, establishes the stability of these structures under exponentially local horizon insertions, and contrasts the resulting multiscale framework with earlier constructions. Throughout,
G=\mathrm{SU}(N)
with
N\geq 2
is a compact, connected Lie group endowed with normalized Haar measure
dU
. The analysis is uniform in the spatial volume and admits the thermodynamic limit. Standard representation-theoretic facts are used in the form of the Peter-Weyl theorem
[
29
]
.

Fix
a>0
and integers
L,T\in\mathbb{N}
. The periodic Euclidean space-time lattice is

\Lambda\;=\;\big\{x=(x_{0},\mathbf{x})\in a\mathbb{Z}^{4}:-\tfrac{Ta}{2}\leq x_{0}<\tfrac{Ta}{2},\ -\tfrac{La}{2}\leq x_{i}<\tfrac{La}{2},\ i=1,2,3\big\}\big/\!\sim,

(11.1)

where
\sim
identifies opposite faces. The set of directed bonds (links) is

\mathcal{B}\;=\;\{(x,\mu):\,x\in\Lambda,\ \mu\in\{0,1,2,3\}\},

(11.2)

with reversed bond
-(x,\mu)=(x+a\hat{\mu},-\mu)
. A gauge field is a map
U:\mathcal{B}\to G
satisfying
U(-b)=U(b)^{-1}
. For an oriented plaquette
p
with bounding bonds
b_{1},b_{2},b_{3},b_{4}
in cyclic order, the plaquette variable is

U_{p}\;=\;U(b_{1})\,U(b_{2})\,U(b_{3})\,U(b_{4}).

(11.3)

The Wilson action at inverse bare coupling
\beta>0
is

S_{W}[U;\beta]\;=\;\beta\sum_{p\subset\Lambda}\left(1-\frac{1}{N}\,\Re\operatorname{Tr}\,U_{p}\right).

(11.4)

The Euclidean gauge measure is the probability measure

d\mu_{\beta}(U)\;=\;Z_{\beta}^{-1}\,\Big(\prod_{b\in\mathcal{B}}dU(b)\Big)\,\exp\!\big(-S_{W}[U;\beta]\big),

(11.5)

where
Z_{\beta}
normalizes the total mass to one.

Time reflection
r:\Lambda\to\Lambda
is

r(x_{0},\mathbf{x})\;=\;(-x_{0},\mathbf{x}),\qquad\Pi\;=\;\{x\in\Lambda:\ x_{0}=0\},\qquad\Lambda_{\pm}\;=\;\{x\in\Lambda:\ \pm x_{0}>0\}.

(11.6)

The induced action
\theta
on links is defined by

(\theta U)(x,\mu)\;=\;\begin{cases}U\big(r(x),\mu\big),&\mu\in\{1,2,3\},\\
U\big(r(x)-a\hat{0},0\big)^{-1},&\mu=0.\end{cases}

(11.7)

If
F
is a complex functional depending only on
\{U(b):b\subset\Lambda_{+}\}
, its OS-reflected conjugate is

(\Theta F)(U)\;=\;\overline{F(\theta U)}.

(11.8)

The Osterwalder-Schrader semi-inner product on such functionals is

\langle F,G\rangle_{\mathrm{OS}}\;=\;\int\overline{(\Theta F)(U)}\,G(U)\,d\mu_{\beta}(U).

(11.9)

Let
\widehat{G}
be the unitary dual with characters
\chi_{R}
and dimensions
d_{R}
. By the Peter-Weyl theorem
[
29
]
and positivity of the heat kernel on
G

[
4
]
, for every
\beta\geq 0
there are coefficients
c_{R}(\beta)\geq 0
such that, for each plaquette
p
,

\exp\!\Big(\beta\tfrac{1}{N}\Re\operatorname{Tr}U_{p}\Big)\;=\;\sum_{R\in\widehat{G}}c_{R}(\beta)\,\chi_{R}(U_{p}).

(11.10)

Theorem 11.1

(OS positivity for the Wilson measure)
.

For every
\beta\geq 0
and every functional
F
supported in
\Lambda_{+}
, one has

\langle F,F\rangle_{\mathrm{OS}}\;\geq\;0.

(11.11)

Proof.

Decompose the plaquettes into those contained in
\Lambda_{+}
, in
\Lambda_{-}
, and those crossing
\Pi
. Write

S_{W}\;=\;S_{+}+S_{-}+S_{0},

(11.12)

with the obvious meaning. Then

\langle F,F\rangle_{\mathrm{OS}}\;=\;Z_{\beta}^{-1}\int\overline{F(\theta U)}\,F(U)\,e^{-S_{+}[U]-S_{-}[U]}\,e^{-S_{0}[U]}\,\prod_{b\in\mathcal{B}}dU(b).

(11.13)

The factor
e^{-S_{+}[U]-S_{-}[U]}
depends separately on links in
\Lambda_{+}
and
\Lambda_{-}
; the coupling across
\Pi
is encoded in
e^{-S_{0}[U]}
. For a crossing plaquette
p
with
U_{p}=U(b_{1})U(b_{2})U(b_{3})U(b_{4})
, where
b_{1},b_{2}
lie in
\Lambda_{+}
and
b_{3},b_{4}
lie in
\Lambda_{-}
, the expansion (
11.10
) gives

e^{-\beta(1-\tfrac{1}{N}\Re\operatorname{Tr}U_{p})}\;=\;e^{-\beta}\sum_{R}c_{R}(\beta)\,\operatorname{Tr}\!\Big(D_{R}\big(U(b_{1})U(b_{2})\big)\,D_{R}\big(U(b_{4})^{-1}U(b_{3})^{-1}\big)\Big),

(11.14)

with
D_{R}
a unitary representative. Setting
X_{+}=D_{R}(U(b_{1})U(b_{2}))
and
X_{-}=D_{R}(U(b_{4})^{-1}U(b_{3})^{-1})
, one has

\operatorname{Tr}(X_{+}X_{-})\;=\;\sum_{i,j}(X_{+})_{ij}\,(X_{-})_{ji},

(11.15)

and
\theta
maps
X_{+}
to
X_{-}^{\dagger}
. Thus each crossing plaquette contributes a positive rank-one kernel on a boundary Hilbert space
\mathcal{K}
attached to
\Pi
. Taking the product over all crossing plaquettes,
e^{-S_{0}[U]}
is a positive combination of rank-one kernels. Inserting this representation into (
11.13
) and integrating first over
\Lambda_{-}
yields a norm square in
\mathcal{K}
of an
\Lambda_{+}
-measurable vector weighted by
e^{-S_{+}[U]}
. The nonnegativity (
11.11
) follows.
∎

Let

\mathcal{C}\;=\;G^{E_{s}},\qquad E_{s}\;=\;\{(x,i)\in\mathcal{B}:\ x_{0}=0,\ i=1,2,3\},

(11.16)

be the configuration space of spatial links at time
0
, with product Haar measure

d\mu_{\mathrm{Haar}}\;=\;\prod_{(x,i)\in E_{s}}dU(x,i).

(11.17)

Set
\mathcal{H}=L^{2}(\mathcal{C},d\mu_{\mathrm{Haar}})
. Denote by
\mathcal{S}
the slab
\{x\in\Lambda:0\leq x_{0}<a\}
and by
\partial\mathcal{S}
its spatial boundary at times
0
and
a
. For
U_{0},U_{a}\in\mathcal{C}
, define the one-step kernel

\mathcal{K}_{\beta}(U_{a},U_{0})\;=\;\int\exp\!\Big(-\sum_{p\subset\mathcal{S}}\beta\big(1-\tfrac{1}{N}\Re\operatorname{Tr}U_{p}\big)\Big)\,\prod_{b\subset\mathcal{S}\setminus\partial\mathcal{S}}dU(b),

(11.18)

where the integral is over links strictly inside
\mathcal{S}
, with boundary values pinned to
U_{0}
and
U_{a}
. The transfer matrix is the integral operator

(T_{\beta}\psi)(U_{a})\;=\;\int_{\mathcal{C}}\mathcal{K}_{\beta}(U_{a},U_{0})\,\psi(U_{0})\,d\mu_{\mathrm{Haar}}(U_{0}).

(11.19)

Theorem 11.2

(Transfer-matrix positivity and self-adjointness)
.

For every
\beta\geq 0
, the operator
T_{\beta}
is a positive, self-adjoint contraction on
\mathcal{H}
.

Proof.

Self-adjointness follows because reversing the slab in time exchanges the boundary configurations and leaves the integrand invariant; hence

\mathcal{K}_{\beta}(U_{a},U_{0})\;=\;\overline{\mathcal{K}_{\beta}(U_{0},U_{a})}.

(11.20)

To prove positivity, split
\mathcal{S}
into two half-slabs of thickness
a/2
separated by a mid-slice at time
a/2
. Let
\widetilde{\mathcal{C}}=G^{\widetilde{E}_{s}}
be the configuration space of spatial links on the mid-slice. Define
H_{\beta}:L^{2}(\mathcal{C})\to L^{2}(\widetilde{\mathcal{C}})
by

(H_{\beta}\psi)(U_{a/2})\;=\;\int\exp\!\Big(-\sum_{p\subset[0,a/2]}\beta\big(1-\tfrac{1}{N}\Re\operatorname{Tr}U_{p}\big)\Big)\,\psi(U_{0})\,\prod_{b\subset[0,a/2]\setminus\partial}dU(b)\,d\mu_{\mathrm{Haar}}(U_{0}).

(11.21)

Define
H_{\beta}^{\ast}
analogously on the upper half-slab. Concatenation of the two half-slabs yields

\mathcal{K}_{\beta}(U_{a},U_{0})\;=\;\int_{\widetilde{\mathcal{C}}}\overline{(H_{\beta}\mathbf{1}_{U_{0}})(U_{a/2})}\,(H_{\beta}\mathbf{1}_{U_{a}})(U_{a/2})\,d\mu_{\mathrm{Haar}}(U_{a/2}),

(11.22)

whence
\mathcal{K}_{\beta}=H_{\beta}^{\ast}H_{\beta}
as kernels. Therefore

\langle\psi,T_{\beta}\psi\rangle_{\mathcal{H}}\;=\;\int_{\widetilde{\mathcal{C}}}\big\|H_{\beta}\psi\big\|_{L^{2}(\mathcal{C})}^{2}\,d\mu_{\mathrm{Haar}}(U_{a/2})\;\geq\;0.

(11.23)

Finally,
\|T_{\beta}\|\leq 1
follows from reflection positivity
[
1
,
2
,
5
]
; equivalently, by gauge and translation invariance the integral of
\mathcal{K}_{\beta}(U_{a},U_{0})
over
U_{a}
is constant in
U_{0}
, and a normalization of
d\mu_{\mathrm{Haar}}
gives
\|T_{\beta}\|\leq 1
.
∎

By spectral calculus,

H_{\beta}\;=\;-\,a^{-1}\,\log T_{\beta}

(11.24)

is a nonnegative self-adjoint operator on
\mathcal{H}
with spectrum contained in
[0,\infty)
; it generates Euclidean time translations in the OS reconstruction
[
2
,
7
]
.

Let
\mathscr{H}_{t}
be the real Hilbert space of site-adjoint fields on time slice
t
with inner product induced by lattice counting measure and the Killing form. Let
\Delta_{A^{h}(t)}
be the gauge-covariant Laplacian on
\mathscr{H}_{t}
, constructed from the reflection-covariant, slice-wise Landau minimizer
A^{h}
as in Section 2. Fix
\sigma>0
and a Gevrey cutoff
\chi_{\sigma}:[0,\infty)\to[0,1]
with
\chi_{\sigma}(\lambda)=1
for
\lambda\leq\sigma
,
\chi_{\sigma}(\lambda)=0
for
\lambda\geq 2\sigma
, and subfactorial derivative bounds. Define the slice-wise horizon operator

P_{\sigma}(t)\;=\;\chi_{\sigma}\!\big({\Delta_{A^{h}(t)}}\big),

(11.25)

which is a positive contraction on
\mathscr{H}_{t}
. By the Helffer-Sjöstrand functional calculus
[
13
]
and Combes-Thomas resolvent bounds
[
14
]
, there exist constants
C(\sigma),\gamma(\sigma)>0
such that the integral kernel satisfies

\|P_{\sigma}(t;x,y)\|\;\leq\;C(\sigma)\,e^{-\gamma(\sigma)\,d(x,y)}.

(11.26)

uniformly in the volume and in the background
A^{h}
selected on the slice.
In particular, all slice insertions built from
P_{\sigma}
are exponentially local and reflection invariant.

Positivity representation:
We distinguish two cases;

(A) Completely monotone cutoff (heat-kernel regime).

If
\chi_{\sigma}
is completely monotone on
[0,\infty)
with
\chi_{\sigma}(0)=1
and

\chi_{\sigma}(\lambda)\leq C_{0}e^{-c_{0}\lambda/\sigma^{2}}
, then by Bernstein’s theorem there
exists a
finite positive
Borel measure
\nu_{\sigma}
on
(0,\infty)
such that

P_{\sigma}(t)=\int_{0}^{\infty}e^{-s\,\Delta_{A^{h}}(t)}\,d\nu_{\sigma}(s),

(11.27)

in the strong operator sense. This representation is used in the OS-positivity arguments
because it exhibits
P_{\sigma}(t)
as a positive mixture of heat kernels, compatible with
reflection covariance and exponential locality.

(B) Gevrey cutoff with compact spectral support (Helffer-Sjöstrand regime).

If
\chi_{\sigma}
is Gevrey with compact support (hence
not
completely monotone),
we do
not
assert a heat-kernel representation. Exponential locality of

P_{\sigma}(t)=\chi_{\sigma}\!\big({\Delta_{A^{h}}(t)}\big)
nevertheless follows from the
Helffer-Sjöstrand almost-analytic functional calculus combined with Combes-Thomas
resolvent bounds for finite-range positive operators. In this case, all OS-positivity and
transfer-operator constructions proceed by inserting the
positive slice functional

p_{\sigma}[U^{h}_{t}]\;:=\;\mathrm{Tr}\,P_{\sigma}(t)\quad\text{or}\quad p_{\sigma}[U^{h}_{t}]\;:=\;\exp\!\big(-\langle\varphi_{t},(I-P_{\sigma}(t))\varphi_{t}\rangle\big),

(11.28)

with a fixed reflection-invariant test field
\varphi_{t}
, so that the Euclidean weight is
multiplied by a slice-local, nonnegative, reflection-covariant factor. This preserves OS
positivity and maintains exponential locality.
Let
\mathcal{I}_{\sigma}[U]
denote the slice-wise insertion obtained by multiplying, over all times
t
, the Gaussian weight implementing
P_{\sigma}(t)
on
\mathscr{H}_{t}
; concretely, in BRST gauge-fixed form this is a product of exponentials of quadratic forms in the slice-adjoint fields, each equal to a positive functional of
U
due to (
11.27
).

Proposition 11.3

(OS positivity with slice-wise horizon insertions)
.

The measure

d\mu_{\beta,\sigma}(U)\;=\;Z_{\beta,\sigma}^{-1}\,\mathcal{I}_{\sigma}[U]\,\exp\!\big(-S_{W}[U;\beta]\big)\,\prod_{b\in\mathcal{B}}dU(b)

(11.29)

is OS-reflection positive: for every
F
supported in
\Lambda_{+}
,

\int\overline{(\Theta F)(U)}\,F(U)\,d\mu_{\beta,\sigma}(U)\;\geq\;0.

(11.30)

Proof.

The proof of Theorem
11.1
reduces (
11.13
) to a positive combination of rank-one kernels supported on
\Pi
. It suffices to check that
\mathcal{I}_{\sigma}
preserves the rank-one positivity across
\Pi
. By (
11.27
), each slice factor
P_{\sigma}(t)
is a positive mixture of heat semigroups
e^{-s\Delta_{A^{h}(t)}}
. The operator
\Delta_{A^{h}(t)}
decomposes into the direct sum of its restrictions to
\Lambda_{\pm}\cap\{x_{0}=t\}
and a nearest-neighbor boundary coupling on
\Pi\cap\{x_{0}=t\}
. For each
s>0
, the semigroup
e^{-s\Delta_{A^{h}(t)}}
is positivity preserving and admits an integral kernel factorization across
\Pi
with respect to a positive boundary measure, by Gaussian integration on graphs. Integrating in
s
against
\nu_{\sigma}
and multiplying over
t
preserves positivity. Exponential locality (
11.26
) ensures that any residual off-diagonal contributions across
\Pi
are summable and can be absorbed into the positive boundary measure without changing sign, uniformly in the volume. Inserting this factorization into (
11.13
) with
S_{W}
replaced by
S_{W}-\log\mathcal{I}_{\sigma}
yields (
11.30
).
∎

The transfer kernel
K_{\beta,\sigma}
is defined by inserting
\mathcal{I}_{\sigma}
into (
11.18
). The half-slab factorization used in (
11.22
) continues to hold with
P_{\sigma}
inserted on the mid-slice, implying

K_{\beta,\sigma}\;=\;H_{\beta,\sigma}^{\ast}\,H_{\beta,\sigma}

(11.31)

for a suitable
H_{\beta,\sigma}
, whence the associated transfer matrix
T_{\beta,\sigma}
is a positive, self-adjoint contraction on
\mathcal{H}
and

H_{\beta,\sigma}\;=\;-\,a^{-1}\,\log T_{\beta,\sigma}

(11.32)

is nonnegative self-adjoint.

The multiscale framework developed here preserves transfer-matrix positivity and self-adjointness at every scale by design. The two structural mechanisms are, first, the reflection-covariant selection of a gauge-invariant transverse representative at each time slice, which ensures that the covariant Laplacian and its functional calculus commute with time reflection, and second, the use of an exponentially local, slice-wise horizon operator
P_{\sigma}
admitting the positive heat-kernel representation (
11.27
). As a consequence, the OS positivity embodied in Theorem
11.1
and Theorem
11.2
is stable under all insertions and coarse-grainings employed in the renormalization group.

In the classical transfer-matrix construction for Wilson lattice gauge theory
[
5
]
, positivity and self-adjointness of
T_{\beta}
are established directly from the slab integral without infrared projectors. While sufficient for a single scale, that approach does not provide a mechanism to maintain uniform locality across scales. In the renormalization group programs of Osterwalder-Seiler
[
4
]
and Balaban
[
20
]
, small- and large-field cluster bounds are obtained by axial gauges, large-field regulators, and Gaussian multiscale decompositions. Those works do not propagate an explicit transfer-matrix positivity through the flow, and they do not invoke a slice-wise positive heat-kernel calculus such as (
11.27
). By contrast, the present scheme builds the finite-range decomposition from the background-covariant Laplacian of the reflection-covariant representative and anchors locality constants to the completely monotone representation (
11.27
). This yields range and norm bounds that are uniform in the number of renormalization steps and that align reflection positivity with multiscale locality. It is precisely this alignment that underpins the spectral step-scaling inequalities proved later, a feature that, to our knowledge, is absent from earlier multiscale constructions for non-Abelian lattice gauge theories.

Bridge to Paper III

We collect here, without further proof, the precise outputs established in this paper that will be used in the continuum construction of Paper III.

Proposition 11.4

(Outputs for the continuum OS/Wightman construction in Paper III)
.

Fix a blocking factor
b\geq 2
and consider a finite coarsening trajectory
a_{k+1}=b\,a_{k}
starting from a fine mesh
a_{0}>0
. Then:

(i)

(
Uniform ultraviolet stability
) The polymer activity satisfies the Kotecký-Preiss smallness criterion at every scale with constants independent of the spatial volume and of the number of coarsening steps; in particular there are
C<\infty
, such that

\|\Phi_{k+1}\|_{a}\;\leq\;C\,\|\Phi_{k}\|_{a}^{2}+C,\,\delta_{k},\qquad\sum_{k}\delta_{k}<\infty,

(11.33)

and the effective action remains local with finite range uniformly in
k
.
(See Theorem 6.7 and Lemmas 6.4-6.6.)

(ii)

(Persistence of exponential clustering)

For every gauge-invariant, even-parity observable with finite support,
the connected correlators exhibit exponential decay with a
scale-independent

rate
m_{*}>0
in the spatial directions and a positive lower bound
m_{t}>0
in the
Euclidean time direction as realized by the transfer matrix.

See Theorems 7.3-7.4 and Proposition 7.5.

(iii)

(
Step-to-step spectral comparison
) Writing
\Delta_{k}:=1-\lambda_{2}(T_{k})
and
E_{1,k}=-a_{k}^{-1}\log\lambda_{2}(T_{k})
, the transfer matrices satisfy the ordered comparison

T_{k+1}\;\preccurlyeq\;V_{k}^{*}\,T_{k}\,V_{k}\;+\;\varepsilon_{k}\,\mathbf{1}\quad\text{with}\quad\varepsilon_{k}\downarrow 0\ \text{summable},

(11.34)

which implies the interlacing inequality

\lambda_{2}(T_{k+1})\;\leq\;\lambda_{2}(T_{k})+\varepsilon_{k},\qquad\text{hence}\qquad\Delta_{k+1}\;\geq\;\Delta_{k}-\varepsilon_{k}.

(11.35)

Consequently any stabilized positive
\liminf_{k}\Delta_{k}
along a finite coarsening path persists under continuum interpolation at fine meshes and yields a strictly positive lower bound for the continuum mass parameter employed in Paper III.

All statements above hold with constants independent of the spatial volume; OS positivity and gauge invariance are preserved at each step by the slice-local, positive inserts and the nearest-
SU(N)
block projection.

The renormalization step here
coarsens
the lattice (
a_{k+1}=b\,a_{k}
), and we use it solely to
propagate a strictly positive spectral gap and scale-uniform locality/clustering parameters across
scales. The actual
continuum limit
in Paper III is taken along
refining
meshes

a\downarrow 0
. The point of Proposition
11.4
is that the uniform outputs-(i) KP
smallness and locality, (ii) a scale-independent clustering rate
m_{*}>0
, and (iii) the interlacing
inequality with
\sum_{k}\varepsilon_{k}<\infty
-ensure that the OS semigroups at fine meshes inherit a
strictly positive mass parameter from any stabilized positive
\liminf_{k}\Delta_{k}
. This is the only
input Paper III needs for the OS
\to
Wightman reconstruction with a nonzero mass threshold.
The continuum limit
a\downarrow 0
itself, together with the construction of Schwinger functions satisfying the OS axioms
[
1
,
2
]
and the Wightman reconstruction with a strictly positive spectral gap, is carried out in Paper III. No continuum claim is asserted in the present paper beyond the quantitative, scale-uniform outputs summarized in Proposition
11.4
.

Appendix 12
Conclusion

In the present work we have sought to bring order into a difficult matter: the construction of a nonperturbative theory of Yang-Mills fields that remains faithful to both the principles of gauge invariance and the demands of positivity. We have shown that it is possible to design a renormalization procedure on the lattice which, step by step, respects reflection positivity and gauge symmetry without compromise. The essential device is simple in spirit: on each time-slice we choose a definite transverse representative, and with the help of a smooth horizon projector we temper the long-range fluctuations. Out of these ingredients we build a block transformation, and from it arises a finite-range decomposition whose locality does not deteriorate as the scale changes.

From this foundation follow three consequences of decisive importance. First, the polymer expansion remains controlled no matter how many times the renormalization step is applied. Second, the fall-off of correlations-the very expression of a mass gap-persists with a rate that is independent of scale. Third, by comparing the transfer operators from one scale to the next, we find that the spectral gap cannot vanish along the flow; it retains a strictly positive lower bound. None of this requires perturbation theory: only the elementary facts of positivity, locality, and covariance are employed.

The meaning of these results is twofold. Conceptually, the scheme reconciles the Euclidean positivity structure with nonperturbative gauge fixing, something that has long resisted precise formulation. Quantitatively, the control of finite-range interactions allows us to carry information from the strong-coupling domain into the scaling window without loss. In this way the bridge from Euclidean clustering to Hamiltonian gaps is kept intact. Thus the theory is placed within reach of a continuum construction in which a strictly positive spectral threshold is preserved.

With the uniform inputs obtained here, one can proceed to the continuum limit, constructing Schwinger functions that satisfy the Osterwalder-Schrader axioms and performing the Wightman reconstruction. At the same time, a sharpening of the constants-concerning the radius of convergence, the decay rates, and the error bounds-would illuminate questions of universality and extend the scaling window. Taken together, these advances outline a concrete road that leads toward the long-sought resolution of the Yang-Mills mass gap problem. Although the present work is entirely lattice-constructive and does not invoke gauge/gravity duality,
it is useful to note a common heuristic parallel: in AdS/CFT-motivated discussions, a confinement
scale or mass gap on the gauge-theory side is often associated with a finite correlation length, while
finite-temperature phases are modeled by AdS black holes; geodesic/thermal probes in such
backgrounds are frequently used as diagnostics of correlation-length scales.
The analysis is entirely non-holographic. Occasional references to the AdS
Einstein-Power-Yang-Mills black-hole literature serves only as contextual motivation,

[
30
]
.

Data Availability

No datasets were generated or analyzed during the current study. All results are derived from mathematical derivations and rigorous analytical arguments, which are fully contained within the manuscript. Therefore, no data are associated with this research work.

Conflict of Interest

The authors declare that there are no conflicts of interest regarding the publication of this paper.

Appendix 13
Technical tools for the polymer expansion

Throughout this appendix we work on a fixed space-time lattice
\Lambda\subset a\mathbb{Z}^{4}
with periodic boundary conditions, where
a>0
is the lattice spacing. Sites are denoted
x=(x_{0},x_{1},x_{2},x_{3})\in\Lambda
. The graph metric is the
\ell^{1}
distance

d(x,y)=\sum_{\mu=0}^{3}|x_{\mu}-y_{\mu}|\qquad(x,y\in\Lambda).

(13.1)

For a nonempty finite set
X\subset\Lambda
its diameter is

\operatorname{diam}(X)=\max\{\,d(x,y):x,y\in X\,\}.

(13.2)

Blocks are closed
\ell^{\infty}
-cubes of side
b\in\mathbb{N}
(in lattice units); a block decomposition is a partition of
\Lambda
into such cubes. When thermodynamic limits are discussed, they are taken along a van Hove sequence; all constants are uniform in the volume.

Let
E(\Lambda)
denote the set of oriented nearest-neighbor bonds of
\Lambda
. The configuration space of link variables is

\mathcal{U}=\prod_{\ell\in E(\Lambda)}\mathrm{SU}(N),

(13.3)

endowed with the product Haar probability measure. The Euclidean Gibbs measure
\mu
is a Borel probability on
\mathcal{U}
with density proportional to the Wilson Boltzmann factor, possibly multiplied by gauge-fixing determinants and reflection-compatible insertions. Reflection is the involution
\theta(x_{0},\mathbf{x})=(-x_{0},\mathbf{x})
. Writing
\Theta
for the pullback by
\theta
and
\mathfrak{A}_{+}
for the
\sigma
-algebra generated by cylinder functions supported in
\Lambda_{+}=\{x\in\Lambda:x_{0}>0\}
, we assume
Osterwalder-Schrader (OS) reflection positivity
: for all complex
F
measurable with respect to
\mathfrak{A}_{+}
,

\int_{\mathcal{U}}\overline{F\circ\Theta}\,F\,d\mu\;\geq\;0.

(13.4)

Unless otherwise indicated,
L^{p}
-norms
\|\,\cdot\,\|_{p}
and inner products
\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle
are taken with respect to
\mu
. The Frobenius norm on matrices is
\|A\|_{F}=(\operatorname{Tr}\,A^{\dagger}A)^{1/2}
. For kernels
K:\Lambda\times\Lambda\to\mathbb{C}^{m\times m}
we write
\|K\|_{\ell^{1}\to\ell^{1}}
for the operator norm on
\ell^{1}(\Lambda;\mathbb{C}^{m})
and
\|K\|_{\infty}=\sup_{x,y}\|K(x,y)\|_{F}
. Symbols
c,C,c_{*},C_{*}
denote finite positive constants which may change from line to line, with dependencies indicated when relevant.

13.1
Kotecký-Preiss criterion in the diameter norm

A polymer is a finite, connected subset
X\subset\Lambda
, where connectedness is for the nearest-neighbor graph. Two polymers
X,Y
are
incompatible
, written
X\nsim Y
, if
X\cap Y\neq\varnothing
; otherwise they are compatible. The family of all polymers is
\mathcal{P}
. A polymer activity is a complex function
z:\mathcal{P}\to\mathbb{C}
. The hard-core polymer gas partition function is

\Xi(z)=\sum_{\Gamma}\;\prod_{X\in\Gamma}z(X),

(13.5)

where the sum is over all finite compatible families
\Gamma\subset\mathcal{P}
. The connected (Ursell) coefficients
\phi^{T}(X_{1},\dots,X_{n})
are defined so that

\log\Xi(z)=\sum_{n\geq 1}\frac{1}{n!}\sum_{(X_{1},\dots,X_{n})\in\mathcal{P}^{n}}\phi^{T}(X_{1},\dots,X_{n})\prod_{i=1}^{n}z(X_{i}),

(13.6)

and admit the representation

\phi^{T}(X_{1},\dots,X_{n})=\sum_{G\in\mathcal{C}_{n}}\;\prod_{\{i,j\}\in E(G)}f(X_{i},X_{j}),\qquad f(X,Y)=-\mathbf{1}_{\{X\nsim Y\}},

(13.7)

where
\mathcal{C}_{n}
is the set of connected simple graphs on
\{1,\dots,n\}
and
E(G)
denotes the edge set of
G
.

For
a>0
the diameter norm of
z
is

\|z\|_{a}=\sup_{x\in\Lambda}\;\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}X\in\mathcal{P}\\
x\in X\end{subarray}}|z(X)|\,e^{a\,\operatorname{diam}(X)}.

(13.8)

The Kotecký-Preiss admissibility condition in the diameter gauge asserts the existence of
a>0
such that

\sup_{X\in\mathcal{P}}\;\sum_{Y\nsim X}\,|z(Y)|\,e^{a\,\operatorname{diam}(Y)}\,e^{a\,d(X,Y)}\;\leq\;a\,\operatorname{diam}(X),

(13.9)

where

d(X,Y)=\min\{\,d(x,y):x\in X,\,y\in Y\,\}.

(13.10)

In dimension four, (
13.9
) follows from
\|z\|_{a}\leq\eta
with
\eta>0
small enough, since the number of polymers
Y
intersecting the
d
-neighborhood of
X
of radius
r
grows at most exponentially in
r
. All geometric constants entering the counting of polymers in the four-dimensional lattice are uniform in the
volume and the block scale, so the admissible
(a,\eta)
in the KP condition may be chosen independently of the
RG step
k
used in Section 6.

Theorem A.1 (Kotecký-Preiss in the diameter norm).

\displaystyle\text{Assume \eqref{p2:eq:KP}. Then the series \eqref{p2:eq:logXi} converges absolutely. Moreover, for each }x\in\Lambda\text{ one has}

(13.11)

\displaystyle\sum_{n\geq 1}\frac{1}{n!}\!\!\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}(X_{1},\dots,X_{n})\in\mathcal{P}^{n}\\
x\in X_{1}\cup\cdots\cup X_{n}\end{subarray}}\!\!|\phi^{T}(X_{1},\dots,X_{n})|\prod_{i=1}^{n}|z(X_{i})|\;\leq\;a,

\displaystyle\text{and for every polymer }X,\ \ \ u(X):=\sum_{n\geq 1}\frac{1}{(n-1)!}\!\sum_{X_{2},\dots,X_{n}\in\mathcal{P}}\!\phi^{T}(X,X_{2},\dots,X_{n})\prod_{i=2}^{n}z(X_{i})

\displaystyle\text{satisfies }\ |u(X)|\leq|z(X)|\,e^{a\,\operatorname{diam}(X)}.

Proof.

Using (
13.7
), the Penrose tree-graph bound yields

|\phi^{T}(X_{1},\dots,X_{n})|\ \leq\ \sum_{T\in\mathcal{T}_{n}}\ \prod_{\{i,j\}\in E(T)}\mathbf{1}_{\{X_{i}\nsim X_{j}\}},

(13.12)

where
\mathcal{T}_{n}
is the set of spanning trees on
\{1,\dots,n\}
. Fix a root, say
1
, in
T
. For each edge
\{i,j\}
with parent
p(i)
toward the root, bound
\mathbf{1}_{\{X_{i}\nsim X_{p(i)}\}}\leq e^{-a\,d(X_{i},X_{p(i)})}
and multiply and divide by
e^{a\,\operatorname{diam}(X_{i})}
. Iterating from the leaves to the root and applying (
13.9
) at each step gives

\sum_{X_{2},\dots,X_{n}}\ \prod_{\{i,p(i)\}\in E(T)}\mathbf{1}_{\{X_{i}\nsim X_{p(i)}\}}\ \prod_{i=2}^{n}|z(X_{i})|\ \leq\ e^{a\,\operatorname{diam}(X_{1})}\ \prod_{i=2}^{n}a\,\operatorname{diam}(X_{p(i)}).

(13.13)

Summing over
T\in\mathcal{T}_{n}
and using
|\mathcal{T}_{n}|=n^{\,n-2}
together with the factor
1/n!
in (
13.6
) yields absolute convergence and the first bound. The estimate for
u(X)
follows by fixing
X_{1}=X
and repeating the argument.
\square

The criterion is stable under replacement of
\operatorname{diam}(X)
by a gauge equivalent weight, e.g.
a_{1}|X|+a_{2}\operatorname{diam}(X)
, and under coarse-graining, since the exponential factor absorbs finite combinatorial growth.

13.2
A tree-graph inequality

Let
n\geq 2
and let
\{a_{ij}\}_{1\leq i<j\leq n}
be nonnegative symmetric coefficients. For a graph
G
on
\{1,\dots,n\}
define the weight

w(G)=\prod_{\{i,j\}\in E(G)}a_{ij}.

(13.14)

Set
\sigma_{i}=\sum_{j\neq i}a_{ij}
. Denote by
\mathcal{C}_{n}
the set of connected simple graphs and by
\mathcal{T}_{n}
the set of trees on
\{1,\dots,n\}
.
